## DEF-529: Phase 96 dialogs paint elevation-2, not the documented elevation-3 ladder step (--shadow-dialog orphaned)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-189, Phase 96-F diff-pass TFL-648)
- Phase: 96 (app-wide modern visual design refresh)
- Files: `src/renderer/styles.css` (`.modal-dialog` `:5728`, `.sheet` `:8616`), `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` (sections 10/12), `test/unit/renderer/designSystem.test.ts` (elevation mapping), `e2e/phase96_design_system.spec.cjs` (dialog guard)
- Expected: per Phase 96 Ruling 5 and the doc, dialog/sheet = `--elevation-3` (`--shadow-dialog`); the dialog root's computed `box-shadow` equals `var(--elevation-3)`.
- Actual: the dialog root (`.sheet`/`.modal-dialog`, e.g. `[data-prefs-dialog]` shell `sheet sheet-prefs`) computes `var(--elevation-2)` in all three themes; both surfaces consume `--shadow-popover`. After Phase 96, `--shadow-dialog` (level 3) has one consumer, `.reading-view` (`styles.css:18239`).
- Repro: launch -> open a document -> `[data-open-preferences]` -> measure the dialog root computed `box-shadow` (adversary probe `test-fixtures/phase96-adversary/probe_state_and_dialog.cjs`) -> equals elevation-2, not elevation-3.
- Escape class: wrong-oracle - `designSystem.test.ts` asserts the token mapping `--shadow-dialog === var(--elevation-3)` but never a dialog consumer; the shipped e2e dialog guard logs the shadow but does not assert it.
- CTO triage (2026-10-04): ACCEPTED, LOW, assigned frontend-dev (TFL-649). Fix: `.modal-dialog` and `.sheet` consume `--shadow-dialog` (matching the documented ladder); add a dialog-shadow assertion to the shipped e2e. Blocks Phase 96 phase close.
- qa (TFL-650, 2026-10-04): CLOSED. `.modal-dialog` (`styles.css:5728`) and `.sheet` (`:8616`) now declare `box-shadow: var(--shadow-dialog)`, and the frosted override (`:12464-12472`) layers `var(--shadow-dialog)` over the glass insets; `--shadow-dialog: var(--elevation-3)` in all three theme blocks (`:534`, `:710`, `:952`). `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase96_design_system.spec.cjs` -> 6 passed / 0 failed. The dialog root's outer drop-shadow equals computed `var(--elevation-3)` in every theme: light `rgba(15,23,42,0.14) 0px 4px 16px 0px, rgba(15,23,42,0.18) 0px 12px 40px 0px`; dark `rgba(0,0,0,0.55) 0px 4px 16px 0px, rgba(0,0,0,0.6) 0px 12px 40px 0px`; frosted the same outer pair plus its two documented inset glass edges. No other surface's shadow changed by the fix (only `.modal-dialog`/`.sheet` moved from `--shadow-popover` to `--shadow-dialog`).

## DEF-530: The design doc's unqualified 3:1 graphic floor contradicts its own decorative empty-state mark tint (--fg-faint at 2.16-2.91:1)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-190, Phase 96-F diff-pass TFL-648)
- Phase: 96 (app-wide modern visual design refresh)
- Files: `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` (sections 11 and 12), `src/renderer/styles.css` (`.empty-state-mark` `:3402`)
- Expected: the doc states an unqualified "icons/graphics clear >= 3:1 in light, dark AND frosted".
- Actual: section 11 mandates the hero-mark tint `--fg-faint`; it measures 2.16-2.56:1 on the light surfaces and 2.75-2.91:1 on the dark surfaces (frosted clears). The mark is decorative and `aria-hidden` (`EmptyState.tsx:35`), which WCAG 1.4.11 exempts (it applies only to graphics required to understand content).
- CTO triage (2026-10-04): ACCEPTED, LOW, doc-only, assigned frontend-dev (TFL-649). Fix: amend `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` section 12 to state the decorative `aria-hidden` empty-state mark is exempt from the 3:1 graphic floor; keep the tasteful tint. Blocks Phase 96 phase close.
- qa (TFL-650, 2026-10-04): CLOSED. `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` section 12 (Contrast contract, `:215-228`) now states the one documented exemption is the decorative `aria-hidden` empty-state hero mark (`.empty-state-mark`, tinted `--fg-faint`), exempt from the 3:1 graphic floor per WCAG 1.4.11. The `.empty-state-mark` CSS is unchanged (`styles.css:3402` still `color: var(--fg-faint)`; the DEF-528 hero-size override at `:16886` is a size rule, not a tint change). `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase96_design_system.spec.cjs` -> 6 passed / 0 failed.

## DEF-528: Phase 96 empty-state hero marks render at 17-18px on the command palette and ContextPanel, not the 32px `--tf-icon-size-hero`

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa (TFL-644, Phase 96-E phase validation, TFL-510)
- Phase: 96 (app-wide modern visual design refresh)
- Files: `src/renderer/styles.css` (the surface svg-size group at `:16859-16874`, `.context-panel svg` `:16863`, `.command-palette svg` `:16866`), `src/renderer/components/EmptyState.tsx`
- Expected: the designed empty-state hero mark renders at `--tf-icon-size-hero` (32px) on every applied surface (Phase 96 Ruling 6; `icons/Icon.tsx` `size="hero"` = 32).
- Actual: on the command-palette no-results (`.command-palette-empty`) and the ContextPanel edit-content (`.context-panel-empty`) empty states the mark renders at 17-18px in all three themes. The Phase-94 surface group `.context-panel svg, .command-palette svg { width/height: var(--tf-icon-size) }` (`styles.css:16859-16874`) beats the `Icon size="hero"` attribute, and it also pins `min-width/min-height` at 18px.
- Repro: launch -> open a document -> Ctrl+K, type a non-matching query (palette empty), or enter the EDIT stage (context-panel edit-content empty); measure `.empty-state-mark svg` -> 17-18px. Phase 96-E e2e captured it in `screenshots/phase96/command-palette-empty-*.png` and `context-panel-edit-content-*.png`.
- Escape class: wrong-oracle - `designSystem.test.ts` pins token presence, not the surface-scoped rendered SVG size, so it did not catch this; the Phase 96-E e2e is the only oracle that did.
- Attribution: Phase 96-D (`EmptyState` implementation) interacting with the Phase-94 surface svg-size rule.
- CTO triage (2026-10-04): ACCEPTED, MEDIUM, assigned frontend-dev (TFL-645). Blocks Phase 96 phase-close (success criterion 5). Fix: a higher-specificity `.empty-state .empty-state-mark svg` rule consuming `--tf-icon-size-hero` (all four of width/height/min-width/min-height), plus a source-contract guard, plus an explicit documented carve-out for the two unreachable empty states (zero-page rail, no-document Inspector).
- frontend-dev (TFL-645): FIX-READY. Added `.empty-state .empty-state-mark svg { width/height/min-width/min-height: var(--tf-icon-size-hero) }` at `styles.css:16876-16887` + a `designSystem.test.ts` guard + the DESIGN-SYSTEM.md 15.4 carve-out. First verification (TFL-646) found the selector was DEAD: `EmptyState.tsx:35` renders `<Icon className="empty-state-mark" />` and `Icon.tsx` returns lucide's `<svg className="empty-state-mark">` directly, so `.empty-state-mark` IS the svg and the descendant `svg` selector matched nothing; the 18px surface rule still won (e2e 3 passed / 3 failed; measured 18px all themes).
- frontend-dev (TFL-647 rework): FIX-READY. Selector corrected to `.empty-state .empty-state-mark` (`styles.css:16886`, specificity 0,2,0), all four dimensions on `var(--tf-icon-size-hero)`; the guard now renders `EmptyState` and asserts the selector MATCHES the mark and does NOT match the dead `.empty-state-mark svg`, so the phantom-selector failure cannot recur.
- qa (TFL-646, 2026-10-04): CLOSED. Re-verification after the TFL-647 rework on a freshly rebuilt renderer. `test:unit -- designSystem emptyState commandBar phase36CommandPalette phase36ContextPanel` -> 9 files / 149 tests passed; `test:e2e -- e2e/phase96_design_system.spec.cjs` -> 6 passed / 0 failed (was 3/3); `verify` -> `conventions: clean (343 file(s))`, 0 type errors. Measured hero mark: command-palette no-results and ContextPanel edit-content = 32 / 32 / 32 px (light/dark/frosted); recent-empty and samples-empty unchanged at 32px. Blast radius `phase94_noAdHocIcons phase43IconUniqueness def339_iconFloor designTokensContract phase40SemanticPalette phase38LegibilityContrast` -> 6 files / 130 tests passed. No floor/contrast regression.

## DEF-527: The Bates update dialog defaults the page scope to All pages, so editing a partial run silently re-stamps every page

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-188, Phase 90 diff-pass TFL-632)
- Phase: 90 (TFL-630 replacement driver)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Apply a Bates run covering only pages 1-2 of a 5-page document.
2. Open the unified REVIEW list, select that Bates row, press its edit control (`[data-review-element-edit]`) to open `BatesDialog` in update mode.
3. Change X/Y or padding and click `[data-bates-apply]` ("Update numbering") without touching the page-scope control.

Expected: the update keeps the run on its OWN pages (1-2). The same phase's watermark update does exactly that - `WatermarkDialog` seeds `rangeAll=false`, `rangeFrom=pages[0]`, `rangeTo=pages[pages.length-1]` from `WatermarkInfo.pages` (`src/renderer/components/WatermarkDialog.tsx:242-254`).

Actual: the dialog emits `settings.pages = [1,2,3,4,5]`. The update-mode re-seed block sets `setRangeAll(true)` unconditionally (`src/renderer/components/BatesDialog.tsx:233`), and `batesPagesForScope(true, ...)` returns every page (`BatesDialog.tsx:150-152`). `onBatesConfirm` forwards that payload to `engine.updateBates` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:6444-6451`), which removes every stream of the run then re-bakes the handed `settings.pages` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4794-4798`). A two-page run therefore becomes document-wide. Recoverable with one undo, and the "All pages" radio is visible, but the default is wrong and inconsistent with the sibling watermark edit.

Evidence: ADV-188 (`ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md`); probe log `[p90adv|SCOPE] run pages=[1,2] emitted pages=[1,2,3,4,5] editId=bates-1`; `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialogScopeAdversary.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` -> 1 passed / 1 passed exit 0. Engine fidelity of `updateBates` to the handed `pages` proven by `test/unit/main/phase90BatesAdversary.test.ts` E7. The shipped `test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx:249-276` covers update mode but never asserts `settings.pages`.

Fix owner: frontend-dev. Direction (CTO-ruled): in `BatesDialog`'s update-mode branch, when `editTarget.pages.length > 0` seed `rangeAll=false`, `rangeFrom=editTarget.pages[0]`, `rangeTo=editTarget.pages[editTarget.pages.length-1]` exactly as `WatermarkDialog.tsx:242-254` does; keep `rangeAll=true` on the apply path and for an empty `pages`. Add the missing page-scope assertion to `test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx`.

History:
- adversary (TFL-632): filed ADV-188.
- CTO triage (2026-10-03): ACCEPTED -> DEF-527 (MEDIUM); assigned frontend-dev as TFL-633. Blocks Phase 90 phase-close (no close while an OPEN defect remains).
- frontend-dev (TFL-633, 2026-10-03): FIX READY. `BatesDialog.tsx` update-mode re-seed now seeds `rangeAll=false`, `rangeFrom=editTarget.pages[0]`, `rangeTo=editTarget.pages[last]` when `editTarget.pages.length > 0`; empty `pages` and the apply path fall back to `rangeAll=true` + `clampedPage`, mirroring `WatermarkDialog.tsx:242-254`. `phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx:271-277` now asserts `settings.pages === [1,2]` for the partial run. Evidence: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` -> 11 passed / 11; scope probe -> 1 passed with log now `emitted pages=[1,2]` (not edited); `npm.cmd run verify` conventions clean (342 files), tsc exit 0. Non-contiguous after-reorder run seeds first..last as the watermark does (noted, out of scope). doc-maintenance: no changes required.
- CTO (2026-10-03): DEF-527 -> FIX-READY; phase-close QA (TFL-634) to confirm and CLOSE.
- qa (TFL-634, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. Source `BatesDialog.tsx:224-232` seeds `rangeAll=false`, `rangeFrom=runPages[0]`, `rangeTo=runPages[last]` when `editTarget.pages.length > 0`, else `rangeAll=true`; apply path (`:242`) keeps `rangeAll=true`. `phase90BatesDialog.test.tsx:274-275` asserts `settings.pages` equals the partial run and not `[1,2,3,4,5]`. Named green runs: unit 11 files / 120 tests; `phase90BatesDialogScopeAdversary` probe log now `emitted pages=[1,2]` (was `[1,2,3,4,5]`); e2e `phase90_bates_inspector` 7 passed. `npm.cmd run verify` conventions clean (342 files), tsc exit 0.

## DEF-525: Two stacked DialogShell surfaces both dismiss on one Escape (no top-most guard)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-186, Phase 92 gate diff-pass TFL-513-G)
- Phase: 92 (DialogShell ownership of Esc)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open the About sheet, then trigger the Update prompt without closing About (the Command Palette `about` entry, then an `update:statusChanged {kind:"available"}`); both are open (`[data-dialog-shell]` count = 2).
2. Press Escape once.

Expected: the top surface owns Esc - one Escape dismisses only the Update prompt, leaving About open.

Actual: one Escape dismisses BOTH (`{about:false, update:false, shells:0}`). Cause: `DialogShell.tsx:146-156` adds an independent `window` keydown listener per open shell; `preventDefault()` does not stop the other listeners, so every open shell's `onClose` fires on the same keydown. Pre-Phase-92 this pair only both-closed when focus sat inside the update backdrop (UpdatePromptDialog's Esc was scoped to its backdrop's React `onKeyDown` = HEAD `UpdatePromptDialog.tsx:566-568`); post-adoption it closes both unconditionally.

Evidence: ADV-186 (`ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md`); probe `test-fixtures/phase92-adversary/probe_stacking.cjs` / `.log`.

Fix (proposed): add a top-most guard in `DialogShell` - a module-level stack of open shell ids; only the last-opened (topmost) open shell handles Esc (and releases its entry on close). Keep `onClose`-omitted must-answer behaviour. Add a unit case stacking two shells and asserting one Esc closes only the top.

History:
- adversary (TFL-513-G): filed ADV-186.
- CTO triage (2026-10-03): ACCEPTED -> DEF-525 (MEDIUM); frontend-dev to add the top-most Esc guard.
- frontend-dev (TFL-623): fix delivered - `DialogShell.tsx` gains a module-level `openShellStack` + per-instance `shellToken`; the Esc effect pushes on open / removes on cleanup and only the stack tail handles Esc; must-answer/backdrop/focus/drag untouched. New stacked-Esc unit case in `dialogShell.test.tsx` (A then B: one Esc fires only B; unmount B then Esc fires A). Evidence: `dialogShell dialogShellClass ocrDialog bugB8_closeTabSavePrompt bugDEF128_closePromptSaveAs bugDEF117_hooksAboveEarlyReturn phase52Dialogs` -> 7 files / 106 tests pass; `verify` clean, tsc exit 0. Left uncommitted.
- CTO (2026-10-03): DEF-525 -> FIX-READY; phase-close QA (TFL-624) to confirm and CLOSE.
- qa (this issue, TFL-624): CLOSED. `DialogShell.tsx:115-169` holds the module-level `openShellStack` + per-instance `shellToken`; only the stack tail handles Esc; the stacked-Esc case (dialogShell.test.tsx:594-624: mount A then B, one Esc fires only B, unmount B then Esc fires A) passes, and the shell's must-answer/backdrop/focus/drag cases in the same file all pass. Commands: unit set (12 files / 212 tests) pass; `npm run test:e2e -- phase92_dialog_shell` 74/74; `npm run verify` conventions clean + tsc exit 0.

## DEF-524: EncryptDialog's header close X is no longer disabled while an encryption is busy

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: frontend-dev (TFL-610, Phase 92 chunk E1) - flagged as an assumption against a wrong CTO DO-NOT; CTO-triaged to a defect
- Phase: 92 (DialogShell adoption)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open `EncryptDialog`, enter a password and click Encrypt so the dialog is busy.
2. Click the header close X.

Expected: the close X is `disabled` while busy (pre-adoption behavior: the header close button carried `disabled={busy}`), so the user cannot dismiss the dialog mid-encrypt.

Actual: after the E1 adoption the shell renders the close X enabled while busy; only the backdrop is blocked (`blockBackdropClose={busy}`). The user can unmount the dialog mid-operation and lose the encrypt result/feedback.

Attribution: the E1 brief's DO-NOT said "Do not add `closeDisabled` - no E1 dialog disabled its header close X", which was wrong for EncryptDialog (its shipped header close did carry `disabled={busy}`, verified at the pre-adoption file). The dev followed the brief, so this is a CTO brief error that produced a real regression against Phase 92 Ruling 7 ("adopters must not remove an existing disabled reason") and Ruling 8 ("every dialog keeps its ... disabled logic").

Evidence:
- Pre-adoption `EncryptDialog.tsx` header close carried `disabled={busy}` (the first `disabled={busy}` after the `<h2>`/`aria-labelledby`, before the body controls).
- Post-adoption `EncryptDialog.tsx` passes `blockBackdropClose={busy}` but not `closeDisabled`; frontend-dev's TFL-610 report records the assumption.

Fix: add `closeDisabled={busy}` to `EncryptDialog`'s `DialogShell`. No other E1 dialog disabled its close X (AuditSpace/FillFromCsv/FormDataIo/InsertPages/Bates/BlankPages/SignatureManager), so no other change.

History:
- frontend-dev (TFL-610): observed and flagged as an assumption against the brief's DO-NOT.
- CTO triage (2026-10-03): ACCEPTED -> DEF-524 (MEDIUM); frontend-dev to add `closeDisabled={busy}`.
- frontend-dev (TFL-614): fix delivered - one prop `closeDisabled={busy}` added to `EncryptDialog`'s `DialogShell` (after `blockBackdropClose={busy}`); nothing else changed. Evidence: `phase52Dialogs phase94_noAdHocIcons dialogShell dialogShellClass` -> 4 files / 39 tests pass; `verify` clean (341 files), tsc exit 0. Left uncommitted.
- CTO (2026-10-03): DEF-524 -> FIX-READY; E1 focused-verification QA dispatched (TFL-615) to confirm and CLOSE.
- qa (TFL-615, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. Source confirms `EncryptDialog.tsx:119` passes `closeDisabled={busy}` alongside `blockBackdropClose={busy}`; `DialogShell.tsx:222` renders the header close X `disabled={closeDisabled}` and the shipped dual size classes are retained (`size="tool"` -> `modal-dialog-tool` + `className="encrypt-dialog modal-dialog-wide"`). Encrypt's action hooks/labels/disabled logic preserved (`data-encrypt-confirm`). Retest command `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run phase52Dialogs phase94_noAdHocIcons dialogShell dialogShellClass` -> 4 files / 39 tests passed; blockBackdropClose/closeDisabled shell coverage in `dialogShell.test.tsx:336-377`.

## DEF-521: DialogShell focuses a disabled default action, leaving no control focused on open

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: qa (TFL-590, Phase 92 chunk D2b focused verification) as an observation; CTO-triaged to a defect
- Phase: 92 (the shell's once-per-open focus contract)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open `CreateFromImagesDialog` (Welcome -> Create from images; root hook `data-create-from-images-dialog`).

Expected: a control is focused on open (a visible focus state). Pre-adoption the dialog focused the first interactive control (`dialogRef.current?.querySelector("button, input, [tabindex]")?.focus()`, now deleted), i.e. the header close X.

Actual: `DialogShell`'s once-per-open focus effect (`src/renderer/components/DialogShell.tsx:125-131`) always calls `defaultActionRef.current?.focus()`; `CreateFromImagesDialog`'s default action ("Create PDF") is `disabled={!valid}` and disabled until an image is picked, so `.focus()` is a no-op on a disabled button and `document.activeElement` stays on `<body>` - no visible focus on open. The effect deps are `[open]`, so it never re-focuses once the image list makes the action enabled.

Attribution: shell-level, not specific to CreateFromImagesDialog. Any adopted dialog whose marked default action is disabled at open loses initial focus the same way (e.g. `ValidateDocumentDialog` Run when `runDisabled`). Affects Phase 92 success criterion 5 (preserved keyboard navigation and focus order).

Evidence:
- qa TFL-590 verdict: "initial focus now targets the default action ('Create PDF'), which is disabled until an image is added, so on open no control is focused".
- `DialogShell.tsx:125-131` (focus effect), `:209` (`ref={isDefault ? defaultActionRef : undefined}`); `CreateFromImagesDialog.tsx` action `disabled: !valid`.

Fix (proposed): in the shell's once-per-open focus effect, when the default action is disabled, fall back to the first enabled control in the dialog (`button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`), so open always lands a visible focus. Keep focusing the default action when it is enabled.

History:
- qa (TFL-590): observed; classified LOW, non-blocking.
- CTO triage (2026-10-03): ACCEPTED -> DEF-521; frontend-dev to add the shell focus fallback plus a unit test in `dialogShell.test.tsx`.
- frontend-dev (TFL-591): fix delivered. `DialogShell.tsx` gains `dialogRef` on the `TfDialog` root and the once-per-open focus effect falls back to the first enabled control when the marked default is disabled; new case `focuses the first enabled control when the default action is disabled` in `dialogShell.test.tsx:261-280`, existing enabled-default case unchanged. Evidence: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run dialogShell dialogShellClass createFromImagesDialog createFromImagesResponsive validateDocumentDialog phase52Dialogs bugDEF117_hooksAboveEarlyReturn` -> 6 files / 91 tests pass; `verify` clean (341 files), tsc exit 0. No doc drift (Ruling 7 / phase-92 criterion 5 already require it). Left uncommitted.
- CTO (2026-10-03): DEF-521 -> FIX-READY; qa retest dispatched (TFL-596) to independently verify and CLOSE.
- qa (TFL-596, 2026-10-03): retest PASS, CLOSED. First pass was red only on a stale `bugB13_focusedOnceDialogs` source-scan left by the fix (the DEF-519 class, not a product regression), so the close was delegated to [TFL-597] (frontend-dev, test-only regex realignment); after it landed both required commands are green. Command 1 `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run dialogShell dialogShellClass createFromImagesDialog createFromImagesResponsive validateDocumentDialog phase52Dialogs bugDEF117_hooksAboveEarlyReturn` -> 6 files / 91 tests passed. Command 2 `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run bugB13_focusedOnceDialogs def197_canonicalLayerWired bugB12_mergeAfterPageAndModalBlock bugB18_insertReplaceModalBlock phase45DialogSquare` -> 5 files / 53 tests passed. Items 1-4 all PASS: fix confined to `DialogShell.tsx` + one `dialogShell.test.tsx` case; enabled-default path unchanged; new fallback case asserts the header close X is focused when the default is disabled; `createFromImagesDialog.test.tsx` primary stays disabled until an image is added. Evidence: `tfl596_evidence.log` / `tfl596_retest.log` artifacts.

## DEF-520: The destructive "Delete pages" confirm button lost its Trash2 glyph after the DialogShell adoption

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-184, Phase 94E diff-pass)

## DEF-515: A read-only Bates/watermark list scan mutates the serialized document bytes

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa (TFL-521)
- Phase: 90 (TFL-509 chunk A, contract + engine ops)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build a 3-page 612x792 Helvetica fixture (one drawn `PAGE-N` per page); load it into `EngineService` as `doc-1`.
2. Capture `engine.getDocumentBytes('doc-1')` -> hash A.
3. Call `engine.getBates('doc-1')` (a read-only list op; returns `[]` on this fresh doc).
4. Capture `engine.getDocumentBytes('doc-1')` -> hash B, and `engine.isModified('doc-1')`, then `engine.undo('doc-1')`.
5. Repeat step 3-4 for `engine.getWatermarks('doc-1')` on a fresh load, and for `getBates` after one `addBates`.

Expected: A read-only list op must not alter the saved byte image; hash B === hash A, `modified` stays false and no undo entry is created (Phase 90 chunk A QA item 6; the developer explicitly flagged that scans normalize page entries).

Actual: hash B !== hash A on the first scan of every page (both `getBates` and the pre-existing `getWatermarks`); `modified` stays false and no undo entry is pushed. The mutation is idempotent: a second scan leaves the bytes at hash B. Root cause: `_forEachBatesMarker` (`engine.ts:4653`) and `_scanWatermarkMarkers` (`engine.ts:4859`) call `page.node.normalizedEntries().Contents`, which lazily rewrites a page whose `/Contents` is a single stream into a `/Contents` array; `serializeDoc`'s `copyPages` then emits the array form, so an otherwise-unmodified document serializes differently after merely being listed. No page content is lost; the byte stream, and therefore any later save, silently churns.

Evidence:
- Probe `test/unit/main/phase90BatesOpsQa.test.ts` (qa-owned), command `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/phase90BatesOpsQa.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 3 failed | 4 passed (7)`.
- getBates on a fresh doc: before `3a7e54e7673ec7f1e01bb77874b77c7916f7e89dfbf698bd8c74f5881ad63449` -> after `4ec7c5378bf0027c2a7c0b688729368f65b2fead4d280f3862e37e9a229c0161`; after2 `4ec7c5378bf0027c2a7c0b688729368f65b2fead4d280f3862e37e9a229c0161`; `modified=false`, `undoOk=false`.
- getWatermarks on a fresh doc: before `3a7e54e7...` -> after `4ec7c537...`; `modified=false`, `undoOk=false`.
- getBates after one `addBates` ([1,2], x30/y40): before `10a9fabd59aa2098533171659982e711726be004519f8cdf583835229f91adcd` -> after `bf460adad4e43e60e0f002022df61ec993fe5843e68e46406806ca7d8bfdcda7`.

History:
- qa (TFL-521): opened - independent probe for the TFL-512 chunk A verification; byte-image purity rule violated by the first marker scan, `modified`/undo rules hold. Follow-up fix routing is the CTO's.
- CTO (TFL-511, 2026-10-04): routed as TFL-526 to backend-dev (Phase 90 fix).
- backend-dev (TFL-526, 2026-10-03): FIX-READY, reason recorded verbatim: "`_forEachBatesMarker` (engine.ts:4656) and `_scanWatermarkMarkers` (engine.ts:4864) now read `page.node.Contents()` (a pure lookup) instead of `page.node.normalizedEntries().Contents`, which called `normalize()` and rewrote `/Contents` into an array plus the autoNormalizeCTM q/Q wrapper. Apply paths (engine.ts:4727, :4920, :4948) left unchanged; no `modified`/undo/save side effect added." Companion test-baseline correction disclosed: `test/unit/main/watermark.test.ts` "deleteWatermark removes the stream and the Contents array is back to pre-apply size" now establishes its normalized baseline with a warm-up add+delete round trip (its setup had depended on DEF-515); `preLen` and every assertion unchanged; qa's probe `phase90BatesOpsQa.test.ts` not edited. Dev evidence: `npm run verify` conventions clean (340 files), tsc exit 0; `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/phase90BatesOpsQa.test.ts` -> Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 7 passed (7) (was 3 failed | 4 passed); 6-file regression suite 87 passed.
- CTO (TFL-511, 2026-10-04): FIX-READY recorded with the developer's reason above. Not CLOSED - qa alone sets CLOSED; independent retest dispatched as [TFL-594](/TFL/issues/TFL-594) (FIX-READY defect retest).
- qa (TFL-594, 2026-10-03): CLOSED - independent retest. `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/phase90BatesOpsQa.test.ts` -> Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 7 passed (7) (was 3 failed | 4 passed); all three read-op purity cases green with hash pairs identical (getBates fresh: before=after=after2=`57a6abe...89bb9c`, `modified=false`, `undoOk=false`; getWatermarks fresh: before=after=`57a6abe...89bb9c`; getBates-after-add: before=after=`c036b67...ffd6f9`; getWatermarks-after-add: before=after=`323f38b...3ac6d`). Blast radius `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/watermark.test.ts` -> Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 37 passed (37); `git diff` of that file shows only the disclosed warm-up add+delete baseline swap, `preLen` and every assertion (`preLen+1`, `preLen`, `preLen`) unchanged - no relaxation. `npm run verify` -> `conventions: clean (341 source file(s) scanned)`, tsc exit 0 (341 not 340: the qa probe and other untracked Phase 90/94 files are now counted; no convention violation). On-disk anchors confirmed: read paths `engine.ts:4656` / `:4864` use `page.node.Contents()`; apply paths `engine.ts:4727` / `:4920` / `:4948` still use `normalizedEntries().Contents`. qa probe not edited; no `src/` edits.

## DEF-505: In-session `exportText` omits a Phase-10 `editTextRun` committed after a replace

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-173)
- Phase: 86 (FEA-038 search and replace)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build the 1-page Helvetica fixture (page 1 `SECRET` y700, `SIBLING` y600) and load it.
2. `engine.replaceText('d', { occurrences: [SECRET_OCC], replacement:'PUBLIC' })`.
3. `engine.editTextRun('d', { page:1, rect: runRect(600), newText:'EDITED' })` (the SIBLING line); note `ok:true`.
4. Read `engine.exportText('d')` in-session.
5. `engine.save('d')`, load into a second engine and read `exportText` again; then replace `PUBLIC` -> `FINAL` and read `exportText` once more.

Expected: in-session `exportText` reflects every committed edit in the session, matching the save+reopen text.

Actual: after step 4 the page text is `SIBLINGPUBLIC` — the just-committed `EDITED` is missing. After save+reopen (step 5) it is `SIBLINGPUBLICEDITED`, so the edit IS persisted. `getDocumentBytes` (probe A13) contains the `EDITED` operator and the later `PUBLIC` -> `FINAL` replace works, so the live document holds the edit; only `exportText`'s direct `doc.pdfDoc.save({ useObjectStreams:false })` (`engine.ts:2290`) fails to surface it after a replace installed its own single-entry `/Contents` array. A user who replaces text, edits text, then exports text gets stale/missing content with no warning.

Evidence: probe A9 FAIL at line 261 (`expected 'SIBLINGPUBLIC' to contain 'EDITED'`); observations `[A9] after edit= "SIBLINGPUBLIC"`, `[A9] after save+reopen= "SIBLINGPUBLICEDITED"`, `[A9] again= {"replaced":1,"skipped":[]}`, `[A9] after again= "SIBLINGFINAL"`. Log `test-fixtures/TFL-450-p86-adv-probe.log`.

History:
- qa: opened (reproduced from ADV-173, TFL-449)
- CTO (TFL-425): FIX-READY - backend-dev TFL-451: pdf-lib's `PDFFlateStream` cached encoded bytes on the first `getContents()` and `PDFContentStream.push` never invalidated it; added `refreshPageContentStream` / `refreshDocumentContentStreams` (re-encode from live operators) after the replace anchors and after `editTextRun` draws, and before `exportText`'s raw save. In-session `exportText` now contains the post-replace edit. Awaiting qa retest.
- qa (TFL-452): CLOSED - probe A9 passes: in-session `[A9] after edit= "SIBLINGPUBLICEDITED"` matches the save+reopen extraction `[A9] after save+reopen= "SIBLINGPUBLICEDITED"`, and the later PUBLIC -> FINAL replace still applies. Probe suite 17 passed / 1 failed (A1 by design); phase unit 25/25 (2 files); blast-radius 274/274 (26 files); e2e 7/7; `npm run verify` exit 0.

- Found by: adversary (ADV-174)
- Phase: 86 (FEA-038 search and replace)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build the 1-page Helvetica fixture with a drawable `SECRET` run; load it.
2. `engine.replaceText('d', { occurrences: [SECRET_OCC], replacement: 'A\u4e2dB' })` — an ASCII char, a CJK char the StandardFont cannot encode, then an ASCII char.
3. Read `engine.exportText('d')` and the result report.

Expected: the op is fail-loud. `_replaceTextImpl` already refuses when a non-empty replacement has NO drawable characters (`engine.ts:2824-2829`); a mixed replacement must likewise be reported (refused, or skip/warn naming the dropped characters) so the user knows the drawn text is not what they typed.

Actual: `replaced: 1`, `skipped: []`, page text `SIBLINGAB` — the CJK character was silently dropped by `sanitizeForStandardFont` and the op reported unqualified success with no warning. The renderer's report line reads "1 replaced, 0 skipped" while the replacement text is silently altered. Violates Phase 86 success criterion 3 (fail-loud, never silently dropped); the CTO raised the suggested MEDIUM to HIGH on that basis.

Evidence: probe A11 FAIL at line 290 (`expected 'SIBLINGAB' to contain '\u4e2d'`); `[A11] result= {"replaced":1,"skipped":[]} text= "SIBLINGAB"`. Log `test-fixtures/TFL-450-p86-adv-probe.log`.

History:
- qa: opened (reproduced from ADV-174, TFL-449)
- CTO (TFL-425): FIX-READY - backend-dev TFL-451: chose the refuse-loudly path; `_replaceTextImpl` now compares `sanitizeForStandardFont(replacement)` with the original and returns `engine-error` naming the undrawable characters before any mutation (new `undrawableStandardFontChars` helper). Test: `A中B` is refused, the page text is unchanged. Awaiting qa retest (the adversary probe A11 asserts the CJK char is DRAWN, which contradicts this accepted outcome - qa must correct that assertion to refusal/unchanged).
- qa (TFL-452): CLOSED - corrected ONLY the probe A11 oracle assertion to the accepted refuse-loudly behaviour (it now expects `ok:false` / typed `engine-error` and an unchanged page). Probe A11 passes: `[A11] result= {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"engine-error","message":"replaceText: the replacement contains characters the StandardFont cannot draw: \"中\""}} text= "SECRETSIBLING"` - refused loudly, no mutation. Probe suite 17 passed / 1 failed (A1 by design); phase unit 25/25 (2 files); blast-radius 274/274 (26 files); e2e 7/7; `npm run verify` exit 0.

## DEF-507: A term split across more than one show run is found by Find but always skipped by Replace

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-175)
- Phase: 86 (FEA-038 search and replace)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Run pure `planReplace` probe B1: content `BT /F1 12 Tf 10 20 Td [(HEL) -20 (LO)] TJ ET` with a rect covering the whole array and `find:'HELLO'` — a visual word split into two show strings of one `TJ` (common kerning/word-splitting).
2. Run probe B2: content `BT /F1 12 Tf 10 20 Td (HEL) Tj /F2 12 Tf (LO) Tj ET` with `find:'HELLO'` — a word split by a `Tf` font switch.

Expected: a term the Find bar reports as an occurrence can be replaced (the renderer's `hitToOccurrence`, `DocumentView.tsx:243-285`, builds a rect for a multi-item hit and hands it to the engine; success criterion 1 promises "replace all occurrences across the document").

Actual: both cases are always returned in `skipped`, removing nothing: `reason: "the covered glyphs span more than one text run"`. `resolveOccurrence` (`src/shared/searchReplace.ts:524-527`) rejects any occurrence whose covered glyphs do not all live in exactly ONE show run, so Replace-all can never change such a term although Find lists it. The shipped "replaces inside a TJ array" unit test only covers a match fully contained in ONE array element, so the intended TJ-array coverage is not actually exercised.

Evidence: probe B1 FAIL at line 369 and B2 FAIL at line 376 (`expected 1 to be +0`); `[B1]`/`[B2] removed= 0 skipped= [{"page":1,"rect":{"x":8,"y":15,"width":40,"height":18},"find":"HELLO","reason":"the covered glyphs span more than one text run"}]`. Log `test-fixtures/TFL-450-p86-adv-probe.log`.

History:
- qa: opened (reproduced from ADV-175, TFL-449)
- CTO (TFL-425): FIX-READY - backend-dev TFL-451: `resolveOccurrence` now groups the covered glyphs by run in reading order, skips runs contributing no covered glyph, requires each run's covered indices to be contiguous, concatenates them to match `find`, and emits ONE anchor at the FIRST covered glyph using the first covered run's font; the single-run veto is removed. Probes B1/B2 now pass. Awaiting qa retest.
- qa (TFL-452): CLOSED - probes B1/B2 pass: `[B1] removed= 5 skipped= []` (TJ-split) and `[B2] removed= 5 skipped= []` (Tf switch), one anchor at the first covered glyph, no skip. Probe suite 17 passed / 1 failed (A1 by design); phase unit 25/25 (2 files); blast-radius 274/274 (26 files); e2e 7/7; `npm run verify` exit 0.

## DEF-496: carryOutlines copies /Prev (and any other ref-valued key) as a raw source-document ref

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-166, Phase 85 diff-pass)
- Phase: 85 (editable outline tree; /Outlines carry path)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build a 2-page PDF with outline siblings BM1, BM2 where BM2 carries the standard `/Prev BM1ref` (`test-fixtures/adv-p85/adv-166-outline-prev.pdf`); load and call `engine.getDocumentBytes` (the serialize path save uses), reload and resolve output BM2's /Prev.
2. Repeat with a node carrying a custom `/SE <source StructElem ref>` (`adv-166-outline-se.pdf`).

Expected: the output /Prev is either absent or points at the sibling node in the OUTPUT document; /SE points at a copied structure element or is dropped - never at a raw source object number.

Actual: output BM2 `/Prev` serializes as `7 0 R`, which in the output resolves to the BM2 node itself (self-referential /Prev); `/SE` `6 0 R` resolves to the outline item node. Root cause: `copyOutlineNode` (`src/main/services/page-organize.ts:136-159`) only special-cases `/Parent /First /Next /Last /Dest /A`; any other `PDFRef` falls through to `clonePrimitive` (`page-organize.ts:317-345`), which returns the SOURCE `PDFRef` verbatim (line 324).

Evidence: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-166; probe case4/7a and case7a.

Impact: MEDIUM - corrupts the outline /Prev structure on every save of any real bookmarked PDF (every sibling after the first carries /Prev); /SE corruption is a tagged-PDF accessibility concern. Owner: backend-dev.

History:
- CTO (TFL-383, 2026-10-03): ADV-166 accepted; filed; assigned to backend-dev as TFL-421.
- qa (TFL-422, 2026-10-02): CLOSED - fix confirmed. Probe suite 16 passed / 0 failed (baseline 11/5); previously failing cases case4/7a (`case4-7a-nodes`) and case7a (`case7a`) now pass: BM2 `/Prev` resolves to the output BM1 node, and the custom `/SE` source ref no longer aliases an output object. Rebuild exit 0; e2e 4/0; unit 57 passed; verify exit 0. Code: `page-organize.ts:118-159` (`copyOutlineNode`) no longer clones arbitrary refs verbatim; `/Prev` is rewired by `copyOutlineChain` (`page-organize.ts:177-235`).

## DEF-497: an inline-dict sibling chain loses every sibling after the first

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-167, Phase 85 diff-pass)
- Phase: 85 (editable outline tree; /Outlines carry path)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build a PDF whose outline root /First points at an INLINE (direct) dict `InlineA`, chained `/Next` to a second inline dict `InlineB` (`test-fixtures/adv-p85/adv-167-outline-inline.pdf`).
2. Load, `getDocumentBytes`, reload and read the outline titles.

Actual: `case4-7b-titles ["InlineA"]` - `InlineB` is dropped. Evidence: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-167; probe case4/7b.

Impact: LOW - exotic input (the PDF spec expects outline items as indirect objects), but silent data loss when it occurs. Owner: backend-dev.

History:
- CTO (TFL-383, 2026-10-03): ADV-167 accepted; filed; assigned to backend-dev as TFL-421.
- qa (TFL-422, 2026-10-02): CLOSED - fix confirmed. Probe suite 16 passed / 0 failed (baseline 11/5); previously failing case4/7b now passes: `case4-7b-titles ["InlineA","InlineB"]` (both inline siblings survive). Rebuild exit 0; e2e 4/0; unit 57 passed; verify exit 0. Code: `copyOutlineChain` (`page-organize.ts:177-235`) cycle guard now keys on object identity for inline dicts instead of the literal `'inline'` tag.

## DEF-498: an indirect /Dest (and indirect GoTo /D) is silently dropped on save

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-168, Phase 85 diff-pass)
- Phase: 85 (editable outline tree; /Outlines carry path)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build a PDF with one node whose `/Dest` is an indirect reference to the dest array, and a second node whose `/A` is an indirect GoTo whose `/D` is an indirect reference to the dest array (both legal).

Rebuild exit 0; e2e 4/0; unit 57 passed; verify exit 0. Code: `remapDest` (`page-organize.ts:261-345`) now resolves a `PDFRef` to its array instead of returning null.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Rebuild (`npm.cmd run build`) then open a 3-page PDF carrying 3 top-level bookmarks targeting visible pages 1, 2 and 2 (built in-spec with `@cantoo/pdf-lib`, mirroring `e2e/phase59_outline_flush.spec.cjs`).
2. Expand the Outline section; edit it through the panel so the accepted tree is `Bookmark 1 -> 1`, `Added -> 3` with child `Bookmark 3 -> 2` (add/rename/retarget/indent/delete).
3. Save-As to a temp `.pdf`, then reopen that file in the app (the app is the compliant reader).

Expected (Phase 85 criterion 3): the re-read `/Outlines` matches the edited shape and the app shows the page badges `1 / 3 / 2`, and navigation to an edited bookmark jumps to its page. Criterion 2 also requires navigation after editing to keep working.

Actual: titles and nesting survive, but every row's `[data-outline-page]` shows `–` (no target) and `resolveOutlinePage` returns null, so navigation reports "Bookmark has no page target". The SAVED file's `/Dest` is malformed: a raw pdf-lib dump of `p85-saved.pdf` shows each node's `/Dest` is `size 2` `[PDFRef, PDFName]` (i.e. `[pageRef /XYZ]`). `writeOutline` (`src/main/services/page-organize.ts:495-499`) writes `[pageRef /XYZ null null null]`, but the serialize-path `remapDest` (`src/main/services/page-organize.ts:244-273`) rebuilds the destination array and copies only `PDFName`/`PDFNumber`/`PDFString` elements, silently dropping the three `PDFNull` coordinates. pdf.js rejects the resulting XYZ destination without coordinates, so the target is lost. The same happens after an in-session undo: one `setOutline` edit + Ctrl+Z re-reads the refreshed engine bytes and every row's page badge is `–`.

Evidence:
- Raw `/Dest` dump: `[{"title":"Bookmark 1","dest":{"size":2,"els":["PDFRef","PDFName"]}}, ...]` (coordinates gone).
- `[p85|reload-rows] [{"path":"0","title":"Bookmark 1","page":"–",...},{"path":"1","title":"Added","page":"–",...},{"path":"1/0","title":"Bookmark 3","page":"–",...}]`.
- `[p85|rows-after-undo] [{"path":"0","title":"Bookmark 1","page":"–",...},...]`.
- Screenshot `screenshots/phase85_saved_reload.png`: the reloaded outline shows `Bookmark 1  –`, `Added  –`, `Bookmark 3  –`.
- Failing e2e assertions verbatim: `DEF-493: the reloaded outline must keep its page targets (1,3,2)` Expected `["1","3","2"]`, Received `["–","–","–"]`; and `DEF-493: the post-undo reseed must keep the outline page targets (1,2,2)` Expected `["1","2","2"]`, Received `["–","–","–"]`.

Impact: HIGH - bookmark page targets are silently lost for the app's own reader and any compliant reader after save/reload or undo, breaking Phase 85 criteria 3 and 2-after-reload. The lenient unit oracle (`test/unit/main/phase85Outline.test.ts` `readOutlineTree`) resolves `dest[0]` regardless of XYZ arity, which is why the unit tests pass. Fix owner: backend-dev (`remapDest` must preserve the full destination array including `PDFNull`, or `writeOutline`'s XYZ form must survive the serialize remap without losing its fit arguments).

History:
- qa (TFL-414, 2026-10-03): filed from the Phase 85 phase validation (FAIL); the two DEF-493 e2e assertions failed.
- CTO (TFL-383, 2026-10-03): accepted; assigned to backend-dev as TFL-415 (FIX-READY). qa re-validation is TFL-417 (with TFL-416).
- qa (TFL-417, 2026-10-03): RE-VALIDATION FAIL - still OPEN. Rebuilt (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0, dist includes TFL-415) and re-ran `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase85_outline_edit.spec.cjs` (2 passed / 2 failed). Failing assertions verbatim: `DEF-493: the reloaded outline must keep its page targets (1,3,2)` Expected `["1","3","2"]`, Received `["–","–","–"]`; and `DEF-493: the post-undo reseed must keep the outline page targets (1,2,2)` Expected `["1","2","2"]`, Received `["–","–","–"]`. TFL-415 preserved the `PDFNull` XYZ coordinates so the saved `/Dest` is now a 5-element array, but it is still malformed: the saved object stream literally contains `/Dest [ 4 0 R /#2FXYZ null null null ]`. `remapDest` (`src/main/services/page-organize.ts:259`) calls `PDFName.of(el.asString())`, but `@cantoo/pdf-lib` `PDFName.asString()` returns the name WITH its leading slash (`"/XYZ"`), so `PDFName.of("/XYZ")` yields the name `"//XYZ"` (serialized `/#2FXYZ`). pdf.js `isValidExplicitDest` rejects the fit keyword (`"/XYZ"` != `XYZ`) and drops the destination, so reload and undo rows show `–`. The in-spec persistence oracle (`readOutlineTree`) passed only because it checks `Dest[0]` (the page ref), never `Dest[1]`; the "strict" unit oracle (`test/unit/main/phase85Outline.test.ts:372-409`) also omits a `Dest[1] === /XYZ` assertion. Fix: in `remapDest` reuse the `PDFName` (`out.push(el)`) or strip the leading slash before `PDFName.of`. Screenshot `screenshots/phase85_saved_reload.png`: `Bookmark 1 –`, `Added –`, `Bookmark 3 –`.
- qa (TFL-417 re-run, 2026-10-03): CLOSED - Phase 85 re-validation PASS after TFL-419. Rebuilt (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0, dist includes TFL-415 + TFL-419) and re-ran `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase85_outline_edit.spec.cjs`: 4 passed / 0 failed (P85-CORE, P85-FAIL-LOUD, P85-DEF492-EMPTY, P85-BLAST-UNDO). `src/main/services/page-organize.ts` now reuses the immutable `PDFName` at all four sites (lines 259, 268, 321, 333), so `Dest[1]` serializes as the Name `/XYZ`. The prior failing assertions now pass: `DEF-493: the reloaded outline must keep its page targets (1,3,2)` Expected `["1","3","2"]` Received `["1","3","2"]` and `DEF-493: the post-undo reseed must keep the outline page targets (1,2,2)` Expected `["1","2","2"]` Received `["1","2","2"]`. Evidence lines: `[p85|reload-rows] Bookmark 1 -> 1, Added -> 3, Bookmark 3 -> 2`; `[p85|rows-after-undo] Bookmark 1 -> 1, Bookmark 2 -> 2, Bookmark 3 -> 2`; `[p85|persisted-tree] 1/3/2`. Screenshot `screenshots/phase85_saved_reload.png` hung on the reloaded edited tree showing badges 1 / 3 / 2.

## DEF-492: A document with no existing outline cannot be given its first bookmark - the Outline section is hidden whenever `readOutline` returns null, so `[data-outline-add]` is unreachable

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: CTO code review (Phase 85, before qa)
- Phase: 85 (editable outline tree; FEA-035)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open any PDF whose catalog has no `/Outlines` (e.g. `assets/samples/report.pdf`), or a merged/reorganized document that lost its bookmarks (the FEA-035 motivating case).
2. Expand the left Pages rail and look for the Outline section and its `[data-outline-add]` verb.

Expected (Phase 85 contract): the outline panel is available for an outline-less document and `[data-outline-add]` creates the first entry - `docs/phase-specs/phase-85.md` Feature C and the CONTROL-INDEX both state "add a sibling entry to the selected row, or a first entry when the outline is empty", and `src/renderer/App.tsx:2046-2049` states "An outline-less document seeds an empty (non-null) model so the panel can add a first entry."

Actual: the section never renders. `readOutline` returns `null` when `getOutline()` yields no items (`src/renderer/pdf/pdfjs.ts:191-195`); App stores that as `open.session.outline` and forwards it (`src/renderer/App.tsx:10489`); and `ContextPanel` gates the whole Outline section on `outline !== null` (`src/renderer/components/ContextPanel.tsx:408`). Because the section is skipped, `OutlinePanel` (and its editable `data-outline-toolbar` / `[data-outline-add]`) never mounts, even though `effectiveOutlineEditor` is non-null (entries = [], `App.tsx:10454-10462`).

Evidence: `src/renderer/components/ContextPanel.tsx:408,429`; `src/renderer/pdf/pdfjs.ts:191-195`; `src/renderer/App.tsx:10454-10462,10489`.

Impact: HIGH - the primary FEA-035 use case (add bookmarks to a document or merged result that has none) is impossible from the UI. The panel's model-level empty-add works in isolation (`test/unit/renderer/phase85OutlineEditor.test.tsx`), which is why the unit tests did not catch the unmounting gate. Fix owner: frontend-dev.

History:
- CTO (TFL-383, 2026-10-03): filed from code review before qa; assigned to frontend-dev.
- qa (TFL-414, 2026-10-03): PARTIALLY VERIFIED - the gate fixed. ## DEF-491: Redaction over-removes a glyph when a mark touches the axis-aligned bounding box of a ROTATED glyph but not the glyph itself

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-164, Phase 84 diff-pass)
- Phase: 84 (True redaction)
- Escape: over-approximation (AABB) accepted by the specified test matrix, which had no rotated-glyph case

Steps to reproduce (pure module, deterministic):
1. Content stream: `q 0.7071067811865476 0.7071067811865476 -0.7071067811865476 0.7071067811865476 200 200 cm BT /F1 10 Tf 1 0 0 1 0 0 Tm (A) Tj ET Q`.
2. Call `removeRedactedGlyphs(content, [{ rect: { x: 194.0, y: 207.0, width: 0.5, height: 2.0 } }], fixedAdvance500)`.
3. The mark rect lies entirely OUTSIDE the glyph's true 45-degree quad, but touches the AABB.

Expected: 0 glyphs removed (content unchanged), because the mark visually covers no part of the glyph.

Actual: 1 glyph removed (output `... Tm [-500] TJ ...`). `glyphBox` (`src/shared/redaction.ts:602-631`) transforms the four glyph-cell corners and returns their axis-aligned bounding box; the hit test at `:672-673` uses `rectsIntersect` (`:492-499`) against that AABB. For a rotation that is not a multiple of 90 degrees the AABB is strictly larger than the true rotated quad, so a mark can remove an unmarked neighbouring character. Confidentiality-safe (over-removal, never under-removal), reachable for content-stream-rotated text (watermarks, vertical table headers/labels, imported rotated-text PDFs) - the app's Rotate verb sets page `/Rotate` (`engine.ts:2121`), which does not rotate content-stream text.

Screenshot: none (pure-geometry repro; `e2e/phase84_redaction_adversary.spec.cjs` test `ADV84-A`, probe `A2c-over-removal`).

History:
- CTO (TFL-382, 2026-10-02): ACCEPTED from ADV-164 (LOW). Owner backend-dev (`src/shared/redaction.ts`): replace the AABB hit test with a true rect-vs-quad intersection (keep the rotated cell corners instead of reducing to min/max) and add the deterministic 45-degree case to `test/unit/main/redaction.test.ts`. Dispatched as TFL-409. qa FIX-READY retest follows.
- backend-dev (TFL-409, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY. `glyphBox` -> `glyphQuad` now returns the four page-space corners (`src/shared/redaction.ts:639`); new pure `rectIntersectsQuad` (`:495`) does a separating-axis test on the rect axes + the quad edge normals; the `planString` hit test uses it (`:697-698`); the now-unused `rectsIntersect` removed. Unrotated glyphs reduce to the same strict overlap as before. `test/unit/main/redaction.test.ts` +2 cases (rotated 45-degree glyph: AABB-only touch keeps the glyph with byte-identical content; a centroid mark removes it). Evidence: `npm run test:unit -- test/unit/main/redaction.test.ts` -> 10 passed (10); `npm run typecheck` -> exit 0; attachment 0ef11bf8-f0b1-415a-ba63-881221b89e28. qa retest pending.
- qa (TFL-410, 2026-10-02): CLOSED. Independent retest spec `test/unit/main/def491_retest.test.ts` (new, 3 cases) re-encodes the ADV-164 repro from scratch: NEGATIVE mark `{x:194.0,y:207.0,w:0.5,h:2.0}` on the 45-degree glyph's AABB -> `removedGlyphs === 0` and content byte-identical; POSITIVE centroid mark `{x:199.65,y:203.89,w:0.5,h:0.5}` -> `removedGlyphs === 1`; REGRESSION unrotated fully-covered glyph -> exactly 1. Evidence: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/def491_retest.test.ts` -> 3 passed (3); blast radius `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/redaction.test.ts test/unit/main/redactionEngine.test.ts` -> 16 passed (16) = 10 + 6; `npm.cmd run verify` -> conventions clean (327 files), typecheck exit 0. No source or existing spec touched; work uncommitted for git-agent.

## DEF-490: Redact overlay has no CSS, so `.redact-layer` is position:static — a real page drag creates no marks and the control bar overlaps the action dock

- Status: CLOSED

## DEF-488: Installed app silently reports "up-to-date" and shows no OTA notification because an invalid ambient GH token turns the public feed into a swallowed 401

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: operator (board report, 2026-10-02)
- Phase: 82 (OTA updater regression)
- Escape: wrong-oracle

Steps to reproduce:
1. Install/launch a packaged Jovrel build older than the latest published release (installed base here: 1.46.0). Ensure the environment carries an invalid `TFLEX_GH_TOKEN` (User-scope var on the reporting machine).
2. Let the app finish its launch auto-check, then use Help -> "Check for Update..." (or `window.tflex.update.check()`).
3. Read `window.tflex.update.getStatus()`.

Expected: criterion 2/3 - the launch check surfaces an in-app "update available" prompt, and the manual check finds the newer published release and offers download/install/restart; a build already current reports "up to date" with no error.

## DEF-478: Format Painter consumes the captured format when a just-placed box is committed while the painter is armed

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-155)
- Phase: 80 (Format Painter)

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, open `assets/samples/report.pdf` through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`.
2. Arm the Edit text-box verb (`[data-dock-verb="editTextBox"]`), drag+type a committed box `P80F-SRC`, set it to Times/18/bold/#3366cc/charSpacing 2, select it and click `[data-txt-format-painter]` (`aria-pressed="true"`).
3. With the painter armed, drag a NEW box on empty canvas (~55%, 12%) - it is renderer-only. At this point the painter stays armed, the hint is visible, and `tflexDiagnostics().engineState.textBoxes` is unchanged (the DEF-476 guard holds at placement).
4. Type `P2-PLACED` into the new box and blur the panel Text field to commit it; capture the engine model and painter state, then press Ctrl+Z twice.

Expected: per the fix's contract (`DocumentView.tsx:1447-1449`, `resolveFormatPainterApply`) a box the placement verb just created is non-applicable; it must keep showing the hint until the user deliberately selects a committed box as the target. Completing the create gesture (typing + commit) must not silently consume the painter.

Actual: on commit the painter applies the captured format to the just-created box as a SEPARATE engine op and disarms, with no target-selection gesture. `P2-PLACED`'s engine model became exactly the source format (Times/18/bold/#3366cc/charSpacing 2); the painter went `aria-pressed="true"` -> `false`, hint null. Undo archaeology: after the first Ctrl+Z the box still exists with its creation style (Helvetica/12/#000000); a second Ctrl+Z removes it - proving the apply was a distinct op. Root cause: `painterTargetIsTransientBox` reads `selectedTextBox.isNew`, which is cleared when the engine echo lands (`replace-text-boxes`); on that same render the committed box's key (`box:P2-PLACED`) differs from `painterArmedKeyRef` (`box:P80F-SRC`), so `resolveFormatPainterApply` returns `apply`; the transient guard covers only the uncommitted window, not the commit transition.

Screenshots: screenshots/adv-p80fix-p2-transient.png, screenshots/adv-p80fix-p2-committed.png, screenshots/adv-p80fix-place-committed.png

History:
- orchestrator: filed from ADV-155 triage (ACCEPTED)
- orchestrator: FIX-READY from frontend-dev TFL-336. Fix: a `painterCreatedIdsRef` set records the ids of boxes created while the painter is armed; `painterTargetIsTransientBox` now takes an optional `createdWhileArmed` set and returns transient for any such id, so a placed box stays non-applicable through the commit transition; only a different pre-existing committed box applies. The set is cleared on arm/disarm/apply. Unit spec adds the DEF-478 commit-transition case and a "pre-existing committed box still applies" case. Reported: 3 unit files / 57 tests pass, `verify` clean, `build:renderer` exit 0.
- qa TFL-337: retested on the rebuilt fixed build (`npm.cmd run build` exit 0; `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase80_format_painter.spec.cjs`, 7 tests / 7 passed; `npm.cmd run test:unit -- --run test/unit/renderer/phase80_formatPainter.test.tsx test/unit/renderer/phase80_formatPainter_fixes.test.tsx test/unit/renderer/phase21_textPropertiesPanel.test.tsx`, 3 files / 57 tests passed; `npm.cmd run verify` exit 0). DEF-478 regression PASS. Added the DEF-478 e2e regression (`DEF-478 commit transition keeps the painter armed; only a different committed box applies`). With the painter armed on committed `P80F-SRC` (Times/18/bold/#3366cc/charSpacing 2) and the placement verb still armed, dragging a NEW box, typing `P80F-PLACED` and blurring the panel Text field to COMMIT left `[data-txt-format-painter]` `aria-pressed="true"` with `[data-txt-format-painter-hint]` ("Format Painter armed: select a text box or text annotation to apply.") visible; the committed box's engine model stayed its OWN creation style (`Helvetica/12/#000000`, no apply op). Selecting a DIFFERENT pre-existing committed box (`P80F-TGT`, Helvetica/12) then took the full captured format in ONE action and the painter disarmed; `P80F-PLACED` stayed untouched. Evidence: screenshots/def477-armed-hint-after-commit.png, screenshots/def477-applied-different-box.png. Blast-radius neighbours DEF-474/475/476 stayed green in the same run. Status CLOSED.
- CTO (TFL-339, 2026-10-02): renumber ruling - this Phase 80 defect was filed as DEF-477 and collided with the Phase 81 print-preset defect DEF-477 already committed in 16034a2. Renumbered to DEF-478; Phase 81's DEF-477 keeps its number. Traceability references in `DocumentView.tsx` and the two Phase 80 specs are renamed to DEF-478 by frontend-dev TFL-340.

## DEF-476: Format Painter silently loses the picked-up format on an empty-canvas click while the placement verb is armed

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-153)
- Phase: 80 (Format Painter)

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, open `report.pdf` through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`.
2. In Edit mode create a committed text box `P80-A` and set it to Times/18 through the FORMAT TEXT panel.
3. Select `P80-A`, click `[data-txt-format-painter]` (`aria-pressed="true"`).
4. Single-click an empty area of page 1 at ~(85%, 85%) while the Edit text-box placement verb is still armed; poll `window.tflexDiagnostics().engineState.textBoxes` and `aria-pressed` every 40ms for 3s.

Expected: per the diff contract (`DocumentView.tsx:1447-1449`) a non-applicable / no-target selection keeps the painter armed and surfaces `[data-txt-format-painter-hint]`; the captured format is not consumed.

Actual: the painter held `aria-pressed="true"` for ~220ms after the click, then flipped to `false` with no apply, no hint, and no engine text-box change (the box list stayed `["P80-A:Times"]`). The still-armed placement verb creates a transient uncommitted text box that the apply effect treats as a target, applies the captured patch to and disarms; the target-change cleanup then drops the empty box - net, the picked-up format is silently lost.

Screenshot: screenshots/adv-p80-pageclick2.png

History:
- orchestrator: filed from ADV-153 triage (ACCEPTED)
- orchestrator: FIX-READY from frontend-dev TFL-323. Root cause: a placement-verb box (renderer-only, `isNew`) was treated as an apply target. Fix: `targetIsTransient` makes the apply decision return the hint, so the painter stays armed and the format is not consumed.
- qa TFL-326: retested on the fixed build (`npm.cmd run build`; `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase80_format_painter.spec.cjs`, 6 tests / 5 passed). DEF-476 regression FAILED. With the editTextBox placement verb armed (`aria-pressed="true"`) and the painter armed on P80-SRC, a single click inside page 1 at 85%/10% left `[data-txt-format-painter]` `aria-pressed="false"`, `[data-txt-format-painter-hint]` absent, and `engineState.textBoxes` unchanged (no apply); the click spawned a transient uncommitted "Type text..." box and an `Engine error: updateTextBox: text box ... not found` toast. The captured format is still silently consumed (see screenshots/def476-canvas-click.png). Fix incomplete: the unit-level `resolveFormatPainterApply({ targetIsTransient: true })` returns the hint, but the live apply path does not keep the painter armed or surface the hint. Reopened FIX-READY -> OPEN.
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (attempt 2) from frontend-dev TFL-328. Root cause confirmed: `painterTargetIsTransient` read the EditOverlay's post-commit `editTextTarget` report, which lags the authoritative reducer selection by one render, so it was false at the apply tick. Fix: added `TextBoxPlacement.isNew` (set by `placeNewTextBox`, cleared when the engine echo rehydrates the mirror via `replace-text-boxes`), a new pure helper `painterTargetIsTransientBox`, and the live apply pass now derives transience from the same-render authoritative mirror (`selectedTextBox.id === painterTarget.id && selectedTextBox.isNew`) with the overlay report only as a fallback. The unit spec now covers the LIVE derivation with a lagging report. Reported: 3 unit files / 55 tests pass, `verify` clean, `build:renderer` exit 0.
- qa TFL-333: retested on the rebuilt fixed build (`npm.cmd run build` exit 0; `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase80_format_painter.spec.cjs`, 6 tests / 6 passed; `npm.cmd run test:unit -- --run test/unit/renderer/phase80_formatPainter.test.tsx test/unit/renderer/phase80_formatPainter_fixes.test.tsx test/unit/renderer/phase21_textPropertiesPanel.test.tsx`, 3 files / 55 tests passed; `npm.cmd run verify` exit 0). DEF-476 regression PASS. With the editTextBox placement verb armed (`aria-pressed="true"`) and the painter armed on P80-SRC, a single click inside page 1 at 85%/10% left `[data-txt-format-painter]` `aria-pressed="true"`, showed `[data-txt-format-painter-hint]` ("Format Painter armed: select a text box or text annotation to apply."), and left `engineState.textBoxes` unchanged (`["P80-SRC:1:Times","P80-TGT:1:Helvetica"]`; no apply, no `updateTextBox: ... not found` toast). A different committed box (P80-TGT, Helvetica/12) then took the full captured format in one action (font/size/bold/italic/underline/color/align/lineHeight/list/indent/charSpacing/highlight) and the painter disarmed. Evidence: screenshots/def476-canvas-click.png (armed + hint), screenshots/def476-applied-after.png (apply). Status CLOSED. Blast-radius neighbours DEF-474 and DEF-475 stayed green in the same run.

## DEF-474: Cross-page Format Painter silently fails (arm on page 1, target a box on page 2)

- Status: CLOSED

- Found by: adversary (ADV-151)
- Phase: 80 (Format Painter)

Steps to reproduce:

Same-page page1->page1, cross-page page2->page1 and same-page page2->page2 all apply; only page1 source -> page2 target fails, reproduced in two independent runs. History:

- orchestrator: FIX-READY from frontend-dev TFL-323. Root cause: the panel read the authoritative `selectedTextBox` while the painter key came only from the per-page overlay's last `editTextTarget` report, so a stale report kept the key on the source box. Fix: `resolvePainterTarget` returns the engine's selected box when the box tool is active (annotation wins; otherwise the reported target), so a page-2 selection is a new key and applies in one action.

## DEF-471: Save-time form fill report calls every untouched empty multi-widget option group `option-unknown` ("option not found: Off"), so a correctly-filled document shows "93 filled, 12 skipped" with 12 false error lines

Steps to reproduce:

## DEF-456: At the 640px minimum window with 10 tabs the strip overflows by 140px - tail tabs and the "+" control are clipped

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: adversary (ADV-141)
- Phase: 72 (operator item 8 / criterion 7)

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, then `node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs b` - opens 10 bundled documents, resizes the window to 640x800.

Expected (criterion 7): with 10 tabs at the 640px minimum, every colorful tab is the SAME width, NO tab's right edge exceeds the strip's right edge, and `.tab-list` `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` (no horizontal overflow, `overflow-x` hidden).

Actual: `.tab-list` clientWidth 156, scrollWidth 296 (overflow 140px); all 10 tabs clamp to the 24px hard floor; 5 tabs' right edges (rightmost 436) exceed the strip's right edge (330) and the `.tab-new` "+" control's left edge is 442 - all clipped out of the bar and unreachable. Root cause: `planTabOverflow` clamps the computed fit width UP to `HARD_MIN_TAB_WIDTH = 24` (`AppHeader.tsx:138-142`), contradicting its own comment (`AppHeader.tsx:84-87`, "Even this is exceeded if the tabs cannot fit"). The unit oracle encodes the bug (`phase59PaletteAndTabOverflow.test.tsx:311,324,337` assert `>= HARD_MIN_TAB_WIDTH`).

History:
- orchestrator: opened (accepted from ADV-141). Owner frontend-dev (TFL-213). Fix: the plan must always satisfy `count*width + (count-1)*gap <= available` - the width may shrink below the 24px compactness threshold (title elides; close stays last child) and/or the inter-tab gap collapses toward 0 - so the 640px/10-tab state never overflows; repoint the unit assertions to the fit invariant. Goal confirmed achievable, so criterion 7 stands unchanged.
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying frontend-dev, TFL-213 - `planTabOverflow` (`AppHeader.tsx:84-152`) now returns the largest width satisfying `count*width + (count-1)*gap <= available`, applying the compactness floor only while it fits; the colorful `.tab` padding yields to `--tf-tab-width` (`styles.css:2079-2099`) so a >20px tab is renderable; the unit assertions were repointed to the fit invariant (`phase59PaletteAndTabOverflow.test.tsx:302-352,383-401`) and the 640px e2e now opens 10 tabs. Evidence: unit 26 passed; e2e 3 passed; measured 640px/10-tab `scrollWidth=156 == clientWidth=156`, uniform width, every tab and the "+" inside the strip; default 16-tab `scrollWidth=1656 == clientWidth=1656`. qa retests before CLOSED.)
- qa: CLOSED (TFL-214 Phase 72 phase-close). `node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs b` -> at 640x800 with 10 tabs: `.tab-list` clientWidth 156 == scrollWidth 156, horizOverflow 0, clipped 0, uniform width 10 (widthSpread 0), "+" right edge 326 inside the strip right edge 330; default window uniform width 160, overflow 0. `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- ... e2e/phase59_tab_overflow.spec.cjs` passed, including the 640px minimum case.

## DEF-455: The active colorful tab never reaches the strip foot / canvas - it floats 6.5px above the strip bottom in all three themes

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: adversary (ADV-140)
- Phase: 72 (operator item 2 / criterion 2)

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, then `node test-fixtures/adv-p72-probe.cjs a` - two documents open so one colorful tab is active and one inactive.

Expected (criterion 2): the active tab extends DOWN to the strip's bottom edge / canvas top - bottom gap <= 1px, no separator line, its fill continuous with the canvas; only inactive tabs float (>= 2px gaps).

Actual: the active tab measures topGap = bottomGap = 6.5px to `.tab-list` (7.5px to the canvas top) in light, dark and frosted - it is vertically centred like the inactive chips, only 4px taller. Root cause: `align-self: flex-end` (`styles.css:2126`) is declared on the inner `.tab` div, but the flex item of `.tab-list` is the wrapping `<li>` (`AnimatedTab.tsx:157-165`, computed `display: list-item`, `align-self: auto`), so the property is inert.

Screenshot: screenshots/adv-p72-a-zoom-active-light.png.

History:

## DEF-438: Form field controls do not follow page rotation — the FormsOverlay editor layer stays at unrotated coordinates, so controls float off their widgets on a rotated form page

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa (TFL-110 Phase 65 close, phase validation; built tree on master HEAD d1868d4)
- Phase: 65 (rendering fidelity; criterion 4's "on a rotated page" clause)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (`launchApp`) and open `test-fixtures/phase65/form-956-anon.pdf` through the toolbar
   Open button, stubbing `dialog.showOpenDialog`.
2. Scroll to form page 3 and set zoom to 100%.
3. Select the page-3 thumbnail in the rail and click the PAGES Action Dock's `[data-dock-verb="rotate"]`
   verb (one clockwise quarter turn).

Expected (Phase 65 criterion 4): the control's measured box equals the widget `/Rect` mapped through the
page scale at the rotated orientation — the editor layer follows the page.

Actual: the page rotates (engine `rotations[2] === 1`; the page wrapper swaps to 841.9 x 595.3 CSS px and
the canvas paints the now-landscape page), but the `FormsOverlay` editors keep their UNROTATED coordinates.
`form-2-text_p3_2` still measures `[180.5, 71.4, 121.0, 23.3]` (its rotation-0 box) where the rotated
mapping gives `[751.5, 180.5, 19.0, 121.0]` (width should be the widget's height, 19 px). The blue text
editors, checkboxes and radios all float horizontally over the vertically-rotated page and no longer sit on
their printed widget boxes; only the canvas-painted read-only widget rotates with the page. Root cause:
`editorStyle` (`src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx:680-690`) positions by `rect.x * cssScale` /
`rect.y * cssScale` with no rotation input, and `FormsOverlay` receives no `rotation` prop (it is not
threaded from `PageView`, `src/renderer/components/PageView.tsx:969`). `PageView` swaps the wrapper dims for
a quarter turn but the `pdf-page-rot-N` class it sets (`PageView.tsx:898-901`) has no CSS rule anywhere.

Impact: on a rotated form page a user cannot see or hit a field where its widget is drawn; edits land in the
wrong visual place. MEDIUM: materially degrades the supported rotate-a-form-page workflow; no document
corruption/data loss, and the operator's `956.pdf` has zero rotated pages (all `rotations` 0), so the
primary unrotated form workflow is unaffected. Breaks criterion 4's stated rotated-page clause, so the
phase gate cannot close clean under criterion 4 as written.

Evidence: `screenshots/p65-956-rot90.png` (page 3 rotated; printed artwork runs vertically, editors stay
horizontal); automated assertion `e2e/phase65_form_layer.spec.cjs` test `(c2)`. Log tail:
```
[P65-c2] rotations after=[0,0,1,0,0,0]
[P65-c2] wrapper=841.9x595.3 scale=1.0000
[P65-c2] form-2-text_p3_2 measured=[180.5,71.4,121.0,23.3] rot90exp=[751.5,180.5,19.0,121.0]
```
Command: `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase65_form_layer.spec.cjs --reporter=list` -> 6 passed / 1 failed.

Origin: Phase 65 criterion 4 (REQUIREMENTS.md 4120-4121) rotated-page geometry; observed by qa during the
TFL-110 phase-close walk.

## DEF-437: Book View's Close control is hit-test dead — the collapsed Inspector strip overlaps it, so a real click never dismisses Book View

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa (TFL-100 Phase 66 chunk 1 focused verification, working tree f3cd127)
- Phase: 66 (chunk 1; the read-only Book View shell)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (`launchApp`) and open `assets/samples/report.pdf` (or the cbz fixture
   `test-fixtures/phase56/phase56-comic.cbz`) through the toolbar Open button, stubbing
   `dialog.showOpenDialog`.
2. Click the canvas top-left `[aria-label="Book View"]` entry. The read-only Book View opens
   correctly (rail and Inspector collapse, the Action Dock is gone).
3. Click the Book View header's `[aria-label="Close book view"]` (top-right X) with a real click.

Expected: Book View dismisses and the prior rail/Inspector/dock state is restored.

Actual: the click never reaches the Close button. The Inspector stays MOUNTED as a 44px
absolutely-positioned collapsed strip at the right edge (`.inspector`, x=2516..2560 in a 2560px
window, `z-index: 30`, `pointer-events: auto`) and the `.book-view` surface does not reserve the
panel column, so the header's Close control (x=2524..2548) sits underneath it.
`document.elementFromPoint` at the Close centre (2536,64) returns the Inspector collapse toggle's
`<path d="m10 15-3-3 3-3">`, and Playwright's real click times out with
`... from <div class="inspector" ... data-inspector-collapsed="true"> subtree intercepts pointer
events`. A `{ force: true }` click still lands on the overlay and does nothing. This is the
DEF-357 / DEF-377 collision class: a region whose right-edge control does not reserve
`--tf-tools-inset` loses its click to the Inspector's interactive child.

The close handler itself is correct: invoking `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Close book
view"]').click()` fires it, `[data-book-view]` unmounts and the panel state restores
(`before {rail:false, insp:false, dock:1}` -> `during {rail:true, insp:true, dock:0}` ->
`after {rail:false, insp:false, dock:1}`). The defect is the pointer hit test only, but it makes
the only exit control of the shell unusable with the mouse.

Commands + output (verbatim):
- `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase66_bookview.spec.cjs` -> `3 failed`; each failure is
  `TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` on
  `[aria-label="Close book view"]`, with the Inspector subtree intercepting pointer events.
  Entry/open parts pass first: `P66_PANEL {"before":{"rail":"false","inspector":"false"},
  "during":{"rail":"true","inspector":"true"},"dockBefore":1,"dockDuring":0}`.
- `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase56_reading.spec.cjs e2e/def395_retest.spec.cjs` -> the
  re-pointed cbz shell tests fail at the same Close click for the same reason.
- Probe geometry (temporary diagnostic spec, now removed): `bookView={"x":64,"y":44,"width":2496,
  "height":1348}`, `close={"x":2524,"y":52,"width":24,"height":24}`,
  `inspector={"x":2516,"y":44,"width":44,"height":1348}` `zIndex=30` `position=absolute`,
  `hitAtClose={"tag":"path"}`.

Impact: the Book View shell's Close control is not reachable by a real pointer click, so a user
cannot leave Book View. HIGH: a stated Phase 66 criterion ("on Close the prior rail/Inspector/dock
state is restored") cannot be exercised through the UI and the only exit control is dead; no
document corruption.

Evidence: `e2e/p66_bookview_run.log`, `e2e/p66_focused_run.log`,
`screenshots/phase66-pdf-shell.png`. Source anchors:
`src/renderer/components/BookView.tsx:164-172` (the Close button, right-aligned in the header),
`src/renderer/styles.css:18131-18149` (`.book-view` / `.book-view-header` do not reserve
`--tf-tools-inset`, unlike `.canvas-overlay` and `.protection-notice-region`),
`src/renderer/styles.css:7904-7907` (the collapsed Inspector inset token).

History:
- qa: OPEN (TFL-100 Phase 66 chunk 1 focused verification; the entry/read-only-shell parts PASS, the real Close click times out). See the entry above for repro and geometry.
- orchestrator: routed to frontend-dev as TFL-108 -- CSS-only fix so `.book-view` reserves the Inspector column (`margin-right: var(--tf-tools-inset, 0px)`), mirroring `.document-scroller` (styles.css:4417) and `.document-column > .validation-notice` (styles.css:17616-17618), plus a sibling hit-test unit test mirroring `phase53_protectionNoticeInspectorHitTest.test.ts`. qa re-verifies chunk 1 on completion (Focused verification) and sets CLOSED.
- frontend-dev (TFL-108): FIX-READY (uncommitted in working tree). `.book-view` rule (selector `.book-view {`, now styles.css:18339) gained `margin-right: var(--tf-tools-inset, 0px);` (line 18345); no pointer-events/z-index change, header/nav untouched. NEW `test/unit/renderer/phase66_bookViewInspectorHitTest.test.ts` asserts the reservation against a collapsed-Inspector sibling. Verification command: build + `e2e/phase66_bookview.spec.cjs` + unit run + `npm run verify`.
- orchestrator: dispatched qa (FIX-READY defect verification) to re-run the real-Close-click e2e for DEF-437 and set CLOSED or re-OPEN with evidence.
- qa: CLOSED (TFL-114 FIX-READY verification). The `.book-view { margin-right: var(--tf-tools-inset, 0px); }` fix (styles.css:18345) reserves the Inspector column; the real (non-forced) Close click now lands and dismisses Book View for both formats. Commands + counts: (1) `npm.cmd run build` -> exit 0 (typecheck clean; vite 2661 modules; esbuild main/preload done). (2) `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase66_bookview.spec.cjs` -> `3 passed` / 0 failed; decisive assertion (real click on `[aria-label="Close book view"]`, `[data-book-view]` -> 0, `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().length` unchanged) passed for BOTH `assets/samples/report.pdf` and `test-fixtures/phase56/phase56-comic.cbz`; P66_PANEL during `{rail:true,inspector:true,dock:0}`, P66_RESTORE after `{rail:false,inspector:false,dock:1}`. (3) `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase66_bookViewInspectorHitTest.test.ts` -> `5 passed` (1 file). (4) `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase56_reading.spec.cjs e2e/def395_retest.spec.cjs` -> `11 passed` / 1 failed; the sole failure is `e2e/phase56_reading.spec.cjs:526` `[data-conversion-dismiss]` count 0 — the uncommitted Phase 67 `ConversionNotice.tsx` collapse rewrite replaced the dismiss control, an obsolete-oracle drift of the same class as DEF-439, NOT a DEF-437 Close-click failure (the Close-click neighbours test 11 "cbz reader control ...
