## DEF-436: 956.pdf renders every form field twice — pdf.js paints the widget appearance on the canvas under the FormsOverlay editor, and editors are mis-placed/missed

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: operator (TFL-49 "Encrypted form issue", reported 2026-09-30)
- Phase: post-Phase 59 (field-layer rendering; Phase 65 contract)

ESCAPE: scope-excluded — Phase 59 item 4 was scoped to the native FILL mechanism (field `/V`,
regenerated widget appearances, fill report). The rendered field LAYER (one control per widget, no
double-draw, exact on-screen geometry) was outside that item's verification scope, so no Phase 59
probe asserted it. CTO names the missed blast radius: every form-bearing PDF's on-screen field
rendering. Brief standard updated: a form-fill phase must verify BOTH the written value and the
rendered layer.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex at master HEAD (1.45.4) and open
   `C:\Users\tanzi\OneDrive\Desktop\Parent visa\956.pdf` (empty-user-password encrypted AcroForm).
2. Scroll to a form page (pages 3-6) and look at the field boxes; edit a text field, e.g. "Email
   address".

Expected (operator, "cleanly like Adobe"): each field is drawn exactly ONCE, as an interactive
control sitting exactly on its widget box; every fillable field has a control; the page does not show
a second, offset box under it; the result looks like an Adobe-rendered form.

Actual (operator): "The app tries to place fields as layer on the form. It misses several fields in
the process. The overlapping layers can be seen. It looks very unpolished." The page canvas already
paints each widget's own appearance (pdf.js `PDFPageProxy.render` is called with the default
`annotationMode = AnnotationMode.ENABLE` at `src/renderer/components/PageView.tsx:690-693`; the
canvas path draws annotation appearances at rotation 0), and `FormsOverlay`
(`src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx`) paints a second transparent, accent-bordered HTML editor over
the same box. Fields whose editor is transparent/thin-bordered read as "missing"; the field box
painted on the canvas reads as the "overlapping layer".

Read-only facts about the operator's file (verified by CTO, `@cantoo/pdf-lib`, empty password; the
file was NOT modified):
- 6 pages, all 841.89pt tall; `%PDF-1.5`, linearised, `/Encrypt` present, `/AcroForm` present,
  `/XFA` absent. It loads with an empty user password (no password prompt needed).
- 105 AcroForm fields (84 `PDFTextField`, 21 `PDFCheckBox`), 129 widgets total; fields live on pages
  3-6 (34 / 34 / 27 / 10); every field maps to a page and every widget has a non-degenerate `/Rect`
  (zero-rect count 0) through the engine's own `findFieldPage` / `getFieldRect`
  (`src/main/services/forms.ts:336`, `:395`). Multi-widget button groups exist (e.g. `mg.title` 4
  widgets, `mg.reason ex` 6 widgets).
- So the "missed fields" and "overlapping layers" are a RENDERING fault, not an engine enumeration
  fault: the engine reports all 105 fields with valid rects, and the renderer paints a duplicate.

Evidence: `screenshots/p59-956-filled.png` (the operator's file in the app: printed form boxes and
overlay editors both visible; the Inspector reads "Form fields 105"; `mg.*` groups and the "Title:
Mr/Mrs/Miss/Ms/Other" row show doubled boxes). Source anchors:
`src/renderer/components/PageView.tsx:690-693` (render call, no `annotationMode`),
`src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx:48-111` (overlay + zero-rect fallback stack),
`src/renderer/styles.css:6884-6948` (`.forms-layer` / `.form-editor`, transparent fill),
`src/main/services/forms.ts:635-709` (`getFormFields`).

Impact: the flagship form-filling capability looks broken on a real government form — fields appear
twice, some read as missing, and the user perceives the whole feature as unpolished. HIGH: a stated
operator acceptance requirement ("fills completely, no missed fields, clean like Adobe") is not met
on screen; no document corruption.

History:
- CTO: opened (TFL-49). Filed with ESCAPE: scope-excluded and routed to Phase 65
  (REQUIREMENTS.md Phase 65, added 2026-10-01). Owner: renderer (frontend-dev) for the single-layer
  field rendering; engine (backend-dev) only if the characterisation proves geometry/enumeration is
  incomplete. qa to reproduce on the current tree, build an anonymised fixture from the operator's
  file, and confirm closure with before/after screenshots and control-count evidence.
- qa: retested (TFL-89 / Phase 65 chunk 1 FOCUSED VERIFICATION on the built tree). Fixture
  `test-fixtures/phase65/form-956-anon.pdf` (generator `test-fixtures/phase65/make-fixture.cjs`) reproduces the
  operator topology: 6 pages, 105 fields, 129 widgets, per-page widgets 42/42/35/10 on pages 3-6, 84 text +
  21 button fields (six multi-widget groups, incl. `mg.reason ex` 6 widgets and `mg.title` 4). The operator
  file was read only, never modified or committed. Spec: `e2e/phase65_form_layer.spec.cjs`.
  Verdicts:
  - (a) CONTROL COUNT — PASS. dom==engine per page (42/42/35/10); totals engine=129 dom=129 missing=0
    extras=0; `mg.reason ex` renders 6 controls for its 6 widgets.
  - (b) SINGLE LAYER — FAIL (partial). Fillable empty widgets: canvas grey=0/5820 (no widget /AP box under
    the editor); with `.forms-layer` hidden (visibleControls 42 -> 0) every fillable box is gone. BUT a
    read-only text widget is still painted on the canvas: with editors hidden its region is grey=5820/5820.
    Cause: pdf.js marks read-only widgets `hasOwnCanvas` (`pdf.worker.mjs: this.data.hasOwnCanvas =

  (editors hidden), `p65-956-fill.png`, `p65-956-geometry-100.png`, `p65-956-geometry-125.png`,
  `p65-956-blast-annot.png`, `p65-956-blast-selection.png`.
  NOT CLOSED: item (b) FAILS for read-only fields. Recommended follow-up (owner: frontend-dev): for a
  read-only widget either suppress the canvas /AP paint or drop the redundant disabled editor, so exactly one

- frontend-dev: FIX-READY (TFL-101 / Phase 65 chunk 2). `FieldEditor` (`src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx:125-148`)
  now returns `null` (no overlay surface) when `kind === "signature"` OR (`field.readOnly === true` AND the id is

## DEF-429: A sample opened from the welcome grid cannot be reopened from Recents

Actual: nothing opens; an error toast reads "Could not open file: form.pdf" and the
welcome screen stays. `src/renderer/App.tsx` (`onSampleClick`) stores the recent as

filesystem path, which does not exist, so the open fails. There is no `samples/` branch
in `openRequestedPath` or `openPdfFromPath` (only `src/renderer/utils/recentPath.ts`
knows the path is a sample, for display).

clicking it errors instead of reopening the document. MEDIUM: it degrades a supported
welcome-screen workflow (reopening from Recents) with a visible failure, but causes no
data loss or corruption.

Evidence: screenshots/pilot1_welcome_sample_recent_click.png (visible error toast).

History:
- qa: opened (Pilot 1 bug-hunt).
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (frontend-dev on TFL-19). Extracted the sample-open body out of
  `onSampleClick` into `openSampleByName(name)` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:2251-2289`) and made
  `onRecentClick` route a `splitRecentPath(entry.path).isSample` path into it
  (`src/renderer/App.tsx:2298-2315`), so a `samples/<name>` Recent row no longer goes through
  `openFromRequest`/`openPdfFromPath`. New unit spec
  `test/unit/renderer/bugDEF429_recentSampleReopen.test.tsx` (4 tests) passed; `npm.cmd run
  typecheck` exit 0. e2e left to qa; uncommitted for git-agent pending qa closure.
- qa: CLOSED (TFL-20). `npm.cmd run build` exit 0. Strengthened the wrong-oracle
  assertion in `e2e/pilot1_welcome_about_bughunt.spec.cjs` test `welcome sample recent
  row reopens the sample` (added `sampleTitle` truthy, `reopened === true`, no
  "Could not open file" toast, `pageErrors === []`). Focused e2e:
  `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/pilot1_welcome_about_bughunt.spec.cjs --grep=reopens`
  -> 1 passed / 1; probe `{"sampleTitle":"samples/form.pdf","toast":[],"welcome":0,"reopened":true,"pageErrors":[]}`.

  neighbour currently selects the virtual `samples/form.pdf` row (a sample, not a

- Status: CLOSED

## DEF-412: Phase 58 tab tear-out is disabled when the strip holds one tab, so a detached window can never hand its tab back

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 58

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, then launch: `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase58_tab_detach.spec.cjs`.
2. Open one bundled document (Open PDF -> report.pdf) so the tab strip holds exactly one tab.
3. Press the tab's `.tab-colour-chip`, drag down past the strip's bottom edge and release (measured: chip centre (354.8, 26.0), strip bottom y=43, pointer released at y=103; a 12px sideways nudge first, since AppHeader only promotes a drag after >6px horizontal movement).

Expected: a new app window with `#detached` in its URL opens showing the document, and the origin tab is removed (the document MOVED, not copied). Then a tab torn out of the detached window returns to the origin and the detached window closes (REQUIREMENTS.md Phase 58 success criteria 6 and 7).

Actual: no new window opens - `app.windows()` stays at 1, the origin tab count stays 1, and `.tab-list` never enters the drag state (`data-dragging-tab` and `data-tab-tearout` are absent throughout the gesture; `data-reorder` is absent even before it). Cause: `src/renderer/components/AppHeader.tsx` sets `reorderEnabled = (onMoveTab !== undefined || onDetachTab !== undefined) && !multiModeEnabled && tabs.length > 1` (lines 459-462), and the tear-out gesture is armed by that same `onTabListPointerDown` handler. With one tab the entire pointer-drag gesture is disabled, so tear-out can never start. This also makes criterion 7 unreachable: a freshly detached window holds exactly one tab (one adopt payload), so the same gate disables the return gesture there too - the round-trip can never complete.

Screenshot: screenshots/p58-detach-origin.png (origin window, one tab, after the failed gesture; the new-window and returned screenshots were not reached).

History:
- qa: opened (focused Phase 58 chunk 6 verification; `e2e/phase58_tab_detach.spec.cjs` fails at step 3 - no second window / no `#detached` URL; unit `phase58TabReorder` 32 + `tabWindows` 7 passed; `npm.cmd run typecheck` exit 0)
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying frontend-dev - TWO fixes in `AppHeader.tsx`: (1) the ARM gate is now `dragGestureEnabled = (onMoveTab !== undefined || onDetachTab !== undefined) && !multiModeEnabled` - the `tabs.length > 1` clause was removed and moved onto the REORDER COMMIT only (`onMoveTab` fires only when `tabs.length > 1 && target !== null && target !== startIndex`), so a single-tab strip can tear out; (2) the arm threshold now measures TOTAL movement (`Math.hypot(dx, dy) <= 6` -> return, with `startY` captured at pointerdown) so a straight downward tear-out arms. The tear-out affordance/decision no longer early-returns on a null drop target. Evidence: `phase58TabReorder` 36 (incl. single-tab detach + no-op + vertical-arm + sub-threshold tests) + `tabs` 25 + `appHeader` 25 = 86 passed; `verify` exit 0; `build:renderer` exit 0.)
- qa: retested and confirmed the downward tear-out opens a `#detached` window showing the moved document (origin 1 -> 0 tabs, second window `...index.html#detached`, `app.windows()` 1 -> 2) and the return round trip in the detached window closes it (`windows` back to 1) and hands the tab back to the origin (count back to 1, document showing). Spec gesture tightened to a PURELY DOWNWARD drag on `.tab-colour-chip` (mousedown, straight down to `strip.bottom + 60`, release, no sideways nudge) - the arm now fires on total movement > 6px. `npm.cmd run build` exit 0; `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase58_tab_detach.spec.cjs` 1 passed (5.3s): step 1 origin tabs=1 strip bottom=43; armed `data-dragging-tab=true`, midway `data-tab-tearout=true`; new window url `file:///.../dist/renderer/index.html#detached` tabs=["<ts>-report.pdf"]; origin tabs after ack=0; return gesture armed+tearout true, `detached closed event=yes windows=1`; origin tabs after return=["<ts>-report.pdf"]; surviving windows=1. Unit: `phase58TabReorder` 36 + `tabWindows` 7 = 43 passed. ## DEF-411: Phase 58 tab reorder activates the dragged tab, changing the active document

3. Drag the THIRD tab (form.pdf, the active one) leftward past the FIRST tab. Order becomes [form, long, report]; active stays form.pdf (correct).
4. Now drag a tab that is NOT first and NOT active (report.pdf, currently last) to the far right.

Expected: the order updates and the ACTIVE tab id / displayed document stay unchanged (REQUIREMENTS.md Phase 58 success criterion 4: "after a reorder the active document is unchanged"; the task's step 3: "drag must not re-activate or swap documents").

Actual: the order updates to [form, long, report] -> [form, report, long], but the active tab changes to the dragged tab (report.pdf). `tflexDiagnostics()` goes from `{activeTabId: <form>, activeDocBytes: 10722, pageCount: 1}` to `{activeTabId: <report>, activeDocBytes: 33028, pageCount: 34}`. Cause: the DEF-034 mousedown-activation contract fires on the pointerdown that arms the drag, so starting a drag on a non-active tab activates it before the reorder commits. The reducer's `move` action preserves `activeId`, but the activation is a separate path the reorder does not suppress/restore.

In `AppHeader.tsx` the arm path snapshots `dragStartActiveRef` (the active id) and `dragStartIndexRef` (the dragged tab's origin index); on a committed reorder (`finish(true)`) it calls `onActivate(startActive)` when the new exported predicate `shouldRestoreActiveOnReorder(startActive, draggingId, startIndex, targetIndex)` is true - i.e. a tab was active pre-drag, the dragged tab was NOT that active tab, and the release slot differs from the origin index. A plain click/tap never restores (no drag), dragging the already-active tab never restores, and a same-slot release never restores. The DEF-034 mousedown activation, the reducer, the CSS and `AnimatedTab.tsx` are untouched. After the array regex consumes `<0041> <0043> [<0041> <0042> <0043>]`, the fall-through `simpleRegex` in `parseToUnicodeCMap` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:7292`) also matches `<0041> <0042> <0043>` inside the brackets and overwrites 0041->C and 0042->D; 0043 keeps C from the array form -> `CDC`. Array-form CMaps are valid and common for Identity-H fonts, so this silently corrupts extracted text.
Screenshot: screenshots/adv-p57-c-array-valid.png

## DEF-403: undoing Flatten restores field values but collapses every field's rectangle to the default and leaves the flattened ink

- Status: CLOSED

3. `undo`.

Expected: undo restores the pre-flatten form exactly (field names, values, rectangles, and no flattened ink).
Actual: after flatten there are 0 fields and 958 bytes of page content / 10 `FlatWidget` draws. ## DEF-400: Toggling an optional-content layer cannot change the rendered page - `serializeDoc` clones the page OCG refs separately from the catalog `/OCProperties` OCG refs

- Status: CLOSED

2. Use the raw OCG fixture built in `e2e/phase57a_engineering.spec.cjs` (OCGs Walls/Pipes; page `/Resources /Properties << /MC0 5 0 R /MC1 6 0 R >>`; catalog `/OCProperties /OCGs [5 0 R 6 0 R] /D << /ON [5 0 R 6 0 R] /OFF [] /Order [...] >>`).
3. Serialize it through the engine's own `serializeDoc` path (`src/main/services/engine.ts:5296` -> `out.copyPages` at :5302, then `carryCatalogEntries`/`PDFObjectCopier` at :5013) - the same path `getDocumentBytes` (:1138) uses for the toggle refresh.
4. Re-parse the serialized bytes with `pdfjs-dist` and compare the optional-content config group ids with the page's marked-content OCG ids.

Expected: the page's `/OC /MC0 BDC` OCG resolves to the same object as the `/OCProperties /OCGs` entry, so moving it to `/OFF` hides its rectangle.
Actual: `copyPages` and `carryCatalogEntries` each use a fresh `PDFObjectCopier`, so the page `/Properties` gets one clone of each OCG while the catalog `/OCProperties` gets a second clone. Measured on the fixture: ORIGINAL bytes -> config group ids `['5R','6R']` == page OC op ids `5R/6R` (both visible); AFTER the `serializeDoc`-style clone -> config group ids `['8R','9R']` vs page OC op ids `4R/5R`, and PDF.js logs `Optional content group not found: 4R/5R` with `isVisible(...) === true` for both. PDF.js keys groups by object id (`pdf.worker.mjs` `parseMarkedContentProps` uses `optionalContent.objId`; `OptionalContentConfig.isVisible` returns `true` for an unknown id), so hiding a layer has NO effect on the rendered page. This breaks REQUIREMENTS.md phase-57 criterion 1 ("toggling one changes the rendered page") and was not reachable through the UI only because DEF-399 leaves the panel empty. The fixture itself is proven correct (both rectangles render on open; PDF.js matches ids on the original bytes).
Evidence: diagnostic commands in the QA report (both `pdfjs-dist` runs).
Test: e2e/phase57a_engineering.spec.cjs (render-delta leg not reachable until DEF-399 is fixed).

## DEF-398: A 1.9 MB PalmDOC record makes `decompressPalmDoc` allocate ~1 GB and block the main thread ~330 ms

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-111)
- Phase: 56

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper.
2. Open `test-fixtures/adv-p56/mobi-lz77-bomb.mobi` (1,974,116 bytes; one PalmDOC text record of repeated unit `0x009F` (length 34, distance 4) that expands to the 32 MB ceiling) through the real Open button.
3. Module level (`probe/probe-p56.cjs lz77` and `mobi`): `decompressPalmDoc` threw the typed `ConvertFailure('too-large', "The decompressed e-book text exceeds the 32 MB decompression ceiling.")` after 312-329 ms at peak RSS 986 MB.
4. App level (`probe/probe-app56.cjs doc:mobi-lz77-bomb.mobi`): the same typed `too-large` surfaced through IPC in 219 ms with no page error, and the app stayed usable.

Expected: the 32 MB decompression ceiling bounds CPU/memory; a file whose declared expansion is 32 MB should not transiently allocate ~1 GB.
Actual: `src/main/services/convert/mobi-parse.ts` `decompressPalmDoc` accumulates into `const out: number[]` (a packed element is ~8 bytes, so 32 M entries ~256 MB) and then `Uint8Array.from(out)` copies it, peaking at ~1 GB for a 1.9 MB input and blocking the synchronous main thread ~330 ms. It is bounded and typed (so not a crash), but it is a ~500x memory amplification and an OOM risk on a low-memory machine, and the in-flight `AbortSignal` is never observed mid-decompress. Fixture: `test-fixtures/adv-p56/mobi-lz77-bomb.mobi`. Logs: probe-stdout of `probe/probe-p56.cjs lz77|mobi` and `probe/probe-app56.cjs`.

History:
- qa: opened
- orchestrator: FIX-READY, relaying backend-dev verbatim. `decompressPalmDoc` (`src/main/services/convert/mobi-parse.ts:291`) now writes into a growing `Uint8Array` (starts at `min(cap, 64 KiB)`, geometric growth capped at the output cap) tracking a written length and returning a subarray — the `number[]` accumulator and the second full `Uint8Array.from(out)` copy are gone. Added an optional `AbortSignal` checked before the loop and every 16,384 units, throwing `ConvertCancelledError`; `readPartText` (`:445`) and `parseMobi` (`:483`) thread it and `adapters/mobi.ts:240` passes `ctx.signal`. Measured: `[DEF-398] LZ77 1.88 MB input -> 33554432 bytes output, heap delta 0.1 MB` (the old path held a heap `number[]`, so the new `< 200 MB` assertion fails against the old code). The bomb still returns the typed `too-large` and a pre-aborted signal throws `ConvertCancelledError`.
- qa: CLOSED. Retested on the fixed tree (dist rebuilt from source) with the adversary's own specimen. `mobi-lz77-bomb.mobi`: real Open button -> code-canned `too-large` toast in 318 ms, peak main RSS 210 MB with a delta of 54 MB over the 156 MB baseline (pre-fix transient ~986 MB / ~330 ms block); `window.tflex.convert.toDocument()` RESOLVED `{ok:false, code:'too-large', message:'The decompressed e-book text exceeds the 32 MB decompression ceiling.'}`. App stayed usable (report.pdf opened and rendered). Screenshot: screenshots/def-398.png. Test: e2e/def396_397_398_retest.spec.cjs.

## DEF-397: A 7.8 MB MOBI whose markup references one image 300,000 times drives unbounded memory growth and kills the app (no output cap in `inlineMobiImages`)

## DEF-396: A 2.5 KB EPUB whose chapter references one image N times OOM-crashes the main process (no output cap in `inlineEpubImages`)

- Status: CLOSED

2. Open `test-fixtures/adv-p56/epub-img-amp-1mb.epub` (2,464 bytes: one 1 MiB PNG referenced by 5,000 `<img src="pic.bin"/>` tags) through the real Open button.
3. Nothing caps the result; only V8's ~512 MB string length limit stops it, after allocating hundreds of MB to tens of GB. The same function is reached by the print adapter (`composeEpubBody`) and by `readingDocument`, so opening OR reading the book crashes. ## DEF-395: Comic reading view runs an uncaught React update loop; single/double and Close controls are not operable by a normal click

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 56

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper.
2. Open `test-fixtures/phase56/phase56-comic.cbz` (12 pages) through the real Open button.
3. Click the real `[aria-label="Open comic view"]` trigger, then click `[aria-label="Comic double page"]` (and/or `[aria-label="Close reading view"]`).

Expected: the comic viewport renders stably and every layout/close control responds to a normal click.
Actual: entering the comic reading view immediately logs an uncaught renderer error `Minified React error #185` ("Maximum update depth exceeded") - no click is needed, it fires at idle in the default single-page layout. A normal Playwright click on `[aria-label="Comic double page"]` never completes (actionability timeout 30 s), and a normal click on `[aria-label="Close reading view"]` times out the same way; after a failed click the renderer is busy enough that a subsequent `win.evaluate(...)` hangs. The layout switch itself is correct when the element's own DOM `click()` is invoked: `data-comic-layout` goes single -> double and `[data-comic-page]` 1 -> 2 (`P56_CI_COMIC_ACTIONS {"before":["0","1"],"after":["1","0"]}` proves the RTL reversal too), so the handlers work and the loop is in the comic body's render/measure path. Probable cause: `ReadingView.tsx` `ComicPage` passes a fresh inline `onPageSize` callback and `setDims({width,height})` a fresh object on every render, while `PageView`'s render effect (`src/renderer/components/PageView.tsx`, deps include `onPageSize`) re-runs and calls `onPageSize` again. The EPUB reading view does not show the error. Unit tests (`readingView.test.tsx`) run in jsdom and do not exercise the real `PageView`/pdf.js path, so this was not caught.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase56-comic-single.png, screenshots/phase56-comic-double.png

History:
- qa: opened
- orchestrator: FIX-READY, relaying frontend-dev verbatim. Root cause found: `ReadingView.tsx` `ComicPage` handed `PageView` a fresh inline `onPageSize` closure every render, while `PageView`'s render effect lists `onPageSize` in its deps (`PageView.tsx:825`) and calls it after resolving the page (`PageView.tsx:524`); that handler did `setDims({width,height})` storing a NEW object even when the numbers were unchanged, so `ComicPage render -> new onPageSize identity -> PageView effect re-runs -> setState(new dims) -> re-render` looped (React #185), wedging the renderer so a real click never reached the handler. Two secondary churn sources: `ComicBody` built a fresh `{width,height,fit}` viewport literal per page per render, and `measure()` stored a fresh `stageSize` object on every ResizeObserver tick. Fix (renderer-only; `PageView.tsx` NOT touched): `ReadingView.tsx:603-607` `setStageSize` functional update bails out when the rect is unchanged; `:619-622` one `useMemo` viewport object per `(width,height,fit)`; `:716-717` module-scope `noopActiveHitTop`/`noopAnnotation` replace per-render inline no-ops; `:738-747` `handlePageSize = useCallback(..., [])` identity-stable with a functional `setDims` bail-out. Evidence deps are now stable, so the effect no longer re-arms. Regression proof: restoring the inline `onPageSize` made the new test HANG (the loop); reverting made it green. Tests: `readingView.test.tsx` gains 3 tests (bounded `onPageSize` call count on mount + two ticks, single<->double page via a real bubbling `MouseEvent` through React's delegated system, Close unmounts). `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer` -> 423 files / 4493 tests passed; `npm.cmd run verify` -> conventions clean (308 files) + tsc clean; `npm.cmd run build:renderer` -> built.
- qa: CLOSED (FIX-READY retest). Rebuilt the working tree (`npm.cmd run build`; renderer + main) and reproduced the filed repro in the real dev build launched ONLY via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`; new spec `e2e/def395_retest.spec.cjs` passes. Real Open button on `test-fixtures/phase56/phase56-comic.cbz`, then real `[aria-label="Open comic view"]` click: comic view visible in 133 ms, then idle 5.14 s with NO `[pageerror]` and NO `Minified React error #185` / "Maximum update depth" entry (`openErrors:[]`). Real Playwright clicks (actionability enforced, no DOM `click()`): `[aria-label="Comic double page"]` completed, `data-comic-layout`=double with 2 `[data-comic-page]`; `[aria-label="Comic single page"]` completed, layout=single with 1 page; `[aria-label="Close reading view"]` completed and `[data-reading-view]` unmounted (count 0). Renderer not wedged: `win.evaluate(()=>2+2)` returned in 1 ms, and closing the tab then re-opening the same CBZ and re-entering the comic view worked (page 1, one page). Screenshots overwritten with the fixed build: `screenshots/phase56-comic-single.png`, `screenshots/phase56-comic-double.png`. Test corrected: `e2e/phase56_reading.spec.cjs` criterion 5 now uses real clicks for Next/Previous, single/double and Close (the DOM-click workaround is gone). Regression on the FINAL tree: `e2e/phase56_reading.spec.cjs` 11 passed (was 10 passed / 1 failed); `e2e/phase55_office.spec.cjs` 17 passed; `npm.cmd run verify:full` -> conventions clean (308 files) + tsc clean + 524 files / 6612 tests passed, exit 0.

## DEF-394: `.xlsx` export throws `Text length must not exceed 32767 characters` instead of returning a typed Result

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-108)
- Phase: 55

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper.
2. Open `test-fixtures/adv-p55/pdf-long-line-40000.pdf` (1,105 bytes; one page whose text layer is a single 40,000-character line with no newline and no two-consecutive-space run).
3. Invoke exactly what the export UI invokes — `window.tflex.export.xlsx(docId, {})` — and catch the result.

Expected: the writer's documented contract and the preload comment are `Promise<Result<ExportBuild, ExportErrorCode>>`, "never a throw" — a page whose text cannot fit a spreadsheet cell should either degrade that cell (as the image data URI path already does with its 30,000-char marker) or return a typed `err`.
Actual: `XLSX.write` throws `Error: Text length must not exceed 32767 characters` (node_modules/xlsx/xlsx.js `write_ws_xml_cell`); `buildXlsx` does not catch it and `exportXlsx` returns that rejected promise. In the app the call rejected with `Error invoking remote method 'export:xlsx': Error: Text length must not exceed 32767 characters`. The renderer's `OfficeExportDialog` catch surfaces a generic "XLSX export failed: ... Text length must not exceed 32767 characters" and the whole export fails; the `Page N` sheet AND the `Full text` sheet are both lost. Module-level: 32,767 chars -> OK; 32,768 chars -> throws. Not a crash and not data loss (the source PDF is untouched), but a violated typed-Result contract and a hard failure on input the app can produce.

History:
- qa: opened
- qa: CLOSED (FIX-READY retest). `e2e/def392_393_394_retest.spec.cjs` "DEF-394: export.xlsx on a 40k-char line resolves with a typed Result" passes against the real dev build (`dist/main` rebuilt from the working tree; launched ONLY via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`). Real Open button on `test-fixtures/adv-p55/pdf-long-line-40000.pdf`, then exactly what the export UI calls: `window.tflex.export.xlsx(docId, {})` with no options. Result: `{ resolved: true, ok: true, bytes: 82917, pagesWithoutText: [] }` in ~100 ms - a produced workbook with the 40,000-char line degraded to a cell. The raw `Text length must not exceed 32767 characters` throw is never surfaced. `clampCell` truncates any string cell to 32,767 chars with the `CELL_TRUNCATION_MARKER`, and `exportXlsx` wraps `buildXlsx` in a try/catch so a future synchronous SheetJS throw returns a typed `engine-error` err, never a rejected IPC promise. RSS 164 MB. Screenshot `screenshots/def-394.png`.

## DEF-393: A 569-byte ODT with nested repeated table cells expands exponentially in `odfToHtml`, blocking the main process ~30 s and allocating ~3.5 GB

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: adversary (ADV-107)
- Phase: 55

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper.
2. Open `test-fixtures/adv-p55/odt-table-bomb-d3.odt` (569 bytes; `content.xml` nests 3 levels of `<table:table><table:table-row><table:table-cell table:number-columns-repeated="1000">...` around one `<text:p>x</text:p>`; the parsed node count is tiny, well under `ODF_PARSE_LIMITS.maxNodes`) through the real Open button.
3. Poll the toast/DOM, then verify the app is still usable afterwards.

Expected: the documented ODF caps (`maxNodes` 200k, `maxDepth` 256, `maxTextChars` 16 MB) keep a hostile ODT bounded, so a sub-kilobyte file cannot allocate gigabytes. A malformed/pathological document gets a typed error.
Actual: the caps bound the PARSE but not the RENDER. `renderRows` emits one `<td>` per `table:number-columns-repeated` (clamped to 1000) and `renderCell` recursively renders a nested table inside each repeated cell, so the output is `1000^depth` cells with no ceiling. Module results: d2 (568 bytes) -> 10,033,024-byte HTML in 552 ms, 264 MB RSS; d3 (569 bytes) -> `RangeError: Invalid string length` after 34,825 ms, 3,575 MB RSS; d4/d6 -> same `RangeError` at ~32 s and 3,575 MB. In the app, opening the 569-byte d3 file blocked the main process: the user-facing error toast appeared at t=27 s ("The file could not be imported (\"odt-table-bomb-d3.odt\")."), and the app was usable afterwards. On a machine with less free memory than this 64 GB box, the ~3.5 GB allocation is an OOM risk of the same class as ADV-106.

History:
- qa: opened
- qa: CLOSED (FIX-READY retest). `e2e/def392_393_394_retest.spec.cjs` "DEF-393: odt-table-bomb-d3.odt fails fast, app stays usable" passes. Real Open button on `test-fixtures/adv-p55/odt-table-bomb-d3.odt` -> typed corrupt error toast `The file could not be read ("odt-table-bomb-d3.odt"). It may be corrupt or truncated.` at 339 ms (pre-fix ~27-35 s), peak main RSS 164 MB (pre-fix ~3.5 GB). The app stayed usable: a second real Open of `assets/samples/report.pdf` rendered (`.workspace canvas` present) and RSS settled at 166 MB. The fix adds an aggregate `maxRenderNodes` (200,000) / `maxRenderChars` (16 MB) budget; `chargeRender` is called once per emitted `<td>` inside the repeat loop, so the nested bomb throws `OdfRenderLimitError` (an `OdfParseError` subclass) before expanding, and the ODT adapter maps it to a typed `corrupt` `ConvertFailure`. Screenshot `screenshots/def-393.png`.

## DEF-380: A 14-byte cyclic-IFD TIFF drives UTIF.decode into an unbounded loop and OOM-crashes the main process

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: adversary (ADV-098)
- Phase: 54

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the real dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper.
2. `test-fixtures/adv-p54/tiff-cyclic-ifd.tiff` is 14 bytes: `49 49 2a 00 08 00 00 00 00 00 08 00 00 00` (little-endian header, IFD0 at offset 8, zero entries, next-IFD pointer at offset 10 pointing back to 8).
3. Run `node test-fixtures/adv-p54/a2-one.cjs tiff-cyclic-ifd.tiff 25000`, which launches the real dev build and calls `window.tflex.convert.toDocument` on the file.

Expected: a typed, readable failure (e.g. `corrupt`) back across IPC; at worst a timeout. A malformed 14-byte file must never be able to exhaust the main process.
Actual: no result was ever returned. The Electron main process grew its V8 heap, and at roughly 22 s of main-process uptime printed, repeatedly, `OOM error in V8: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` at ~4 GB. The renderer IPC then rejected with `Target page, context or browser has been closed`, and the app was gone (`usableAfter` dead). A second run with a 6 s deadline reproduced the same OOM. The main process runs an unbounded allocation loop until V8 OOMs and the whole application dies; no typed error reaches the renderer and a restart is required.

Root cause (verified in `node_modules/utif/UTIF.js:93-98`): `UTIF.decode` loops `while (true) { noff = _readIFD(...); ifdo = readUint(data, noff); if (ifdo == 0) break; }`. With the self-referential next-IFD pointer, `ifdo` is always 8, so `ifds.push(ifd)` grows without bound and the loop never terminates. `src/main/services/convert/adapters/tiff.ts:135` calls `UTIF.decode` inside a `try/catch` that can never fire on a loop.

Screenshot: none (process death, no window to capture). Log: test-fixtures/adv-p54/logs/cyclic.log

History:
- qa: filed from ADV-098 (Phase 54 adversary gate; accepted by the orchestrator as ACCEPTED -> DEF-380).
- qa: CLOSED (FIX-READY retest; the orchestrator relayed FIX-READY in the same run). `node test-fixtures/adv-p54/a2-one.cjs tiff-cyclic-ifd.tiff 25000` on the rebuilt dev tree -> `{"ms":6,"timedOut":false,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"corrupt","message":"The TIFF could not be parsed. The TIFF IFD chain is cyclic: offset 8 is visited more than once."},"usableAfter":true}`. A typed, readable `corrupt` error in 6 ms; the app stayed alive and no OOM (previously death at ~4 GB). `test/unit/main/convertTiffAdapter.test.ts` carries the specimen case (13 files / 167 tests green).

Saving a tagged PDF therefore silently untags it, and named destinations / the initial view are lost.

Distinct from DEF-378 (which carried `/Metadata`, `/OutputIntents`, `/OCProperties`, `/MarkInfo`, `/Lang`, `/ViewerPreferences`, `/Collection`, `/AF` and the `/Names /JavaScript` subtree). The page-reference-remap part is contracted as REQUIREMENTS.md Phase 57 feature G; `/StructTreeRoot` is recorded as FEA-023 (accepted deferral).

- qa: opened (Phase 54 DEF-378 run-close pass; reproduced in the running app on the current tree).
- orchestrator: REJECTED as a defect, with the work CONTRACTED rather than dropped -- the entry is not "will not fix", it is "will not be fixed as a Phase 54 defect", and the reason is written here so nothing is silent. Split by item: (a) `/Dests` named destinations AND `/OpenAction` initial view ARE going to be fixed -- they are contracted as REQUIREMENTS.md **Phase 57 feature G** ("Catalog round-trip completeness"), which requires carrying them across the rebuild by REMAPPING their page references through the page map `serializeDoc` already builds, and which requires a test that a destination-free document still serializes byte-stably; qa's evidence in this entry (`/Dests` and `/OpenAction` present in the source, absent in the saved catalog) is the acceptance case that feature is written around. (b) `/StructTreeRoot` is DEFERRED with a written reason as **FEA-023** (docs/FEATURE-BACKLOG.md): structure elements reference page objects and re-tagging them correctly -- remapping the page refs, validating the parent/child linkage and the `/MarkInfo /Marked` flag together -- is its own program, and a file that CLAIMS to be tagged while carrying a broken structure tree is worse for assistive technology than an honestly untagged one. (c) `/Names` wholesale is deliberately NOT carried and MUST NOT be: the Phase 54 fix cycle proved with a page-tree safety test that cloning `/Names` wholesale drags page-referencing named destinations into the destination context and risks the page tree, which is why the fix carries only its `/JavaScript` subtree -- qa's own evidence shows exactly that (`/Names` survives with `/JavaScript` and without `/Dests`). (d) `/AcroForm` is deliberately not carried because the engine owns form serialization through its own path, and hijacking the catalog entry would double-write the form. ## DEF-378: PDF/A and PDF/X validation of an opened document reports "none declared" and a spurious missing-output-intent error

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 54

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0); launch the dev app through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper.
2. Open `test-fixtures/phase54/pdfa-1b-ok.pdf` (stub `dialog.showOpenDialog` to return the path, then click Open PDF).
3. REVIEW dock -> "Validate document…" -> select PDF/A-1b -> Validate.
4. Read the inline report card.

Expected: the report names the declared level `PDF/A-1b`, reports `conforms: true` and zero errors (the fixture carries an OutputIntent with an embedded ICC profile, an embedded font and a `pdfaid` XMP packet).
Actual: the report reads `declared: "none declared"`, `conforms: false`, with one error `pdfa.output-intent` ("No /OutputIntents entry: a PDF/A target requires an OutputIntent with an embedded ICC destination profile."). The same happens for `pdfx-1a-cmyk.pdf` against PDF/X-1a: `declared: "none declared"`, one error `pdfx.output-intent`. The fixtures validate correctly when their bytes are passed straight to `validation.validateBytes` (the unit layer), so the loss happens on the app's opened-document path.

Root cause: `serializeDoc` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4516`) builds a fresh `PDFDocument.create()` and copies only the pages; it never carries the source catalog's `/Metadata` (XMP) or `/OutputIntents`. The validation IPC (`src/main/index.ts:722`) validates `engine.getDocumentBytes(docId)`, i.e. those re-serialized bytes, so the declaration and the output intent are gone before the rule set runs. This breaks Phase 54 criteria 5 and 6 for every document opened through the app.

Evidence: `e2e/phase54_imaging_validation.spec.cjs` `P54_C5A` -> `{"target":"pdfa-1b","conforms":"false","declared":"none declared","rules":[{"rule":"pdfa.output-intent","severity":"error"}]}`; `P54_C6A` -> `{"target":"pdfx-1a","conforms":"false","declared":"none declared","rules":[{"rule":"pdfx.output-intent","severity":"error"}]}`. A direct copy-pages-and-save of the same fixtures drops `hasMetadata` and `hasOutputIntents` to false.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase54-c5-pdfa-ok.png

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 54 phase validation; reproduced in the running app).
- orchestrator: FIX-READY -- relaying backend-dev: `serializeDoc` now carries the source catalog's `/Metadata` (the XMP packet, pdfaid included) and `/OutputIntents` (the ICC output intent) into the freshly created destination document, using pdf-lib's own `PDFObjectCopier.for(src.context, out.context).copy(...)` primitive, which deep-clones the object graph into the destination context with ref memoisation and cycle handling -- a raw `PDFRef` from the source context would be invalid there. `PDFRawStream.clone` carries both the dictionary and the raw bytes, so the XMP stream and the ICC stream survive verbatim. The carry is per-entry failure-isolated: a clone failure is skipped and the save proceeds exactly as it does today, proven by a test that forces the `/Metadata` clone to throw and asserts the save still succeeds and the output is byte-equal to the page-only control. Evidence: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/engine test/unit/main/validatePdfA.test.ts test/unit/main/validatePdfX.test.ts test/unit/main/validateExportGuard.test.ts` -> 5 files / 267 tests passed; new `test/unit/main/engineSerializeMetadata.test.ts` 8/8; `npm.cmd run verify` exit 0 (conventions clean, 283 files, tsc clean); `npm.cmd run build:node` exit 0. The bytes-equality assertions compare the round-tripped XMP and ICC bytes to the originals, and the Phase 54 acceptance case now reports `declared: 'PDF/A-1b'`, `conforms: true`, `violations: []`, plus PDF/X-1a CMYK `declared: 'PDF/X-1:2001'`, `conforms: true`. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this defect was the messenger for a broader bug -- because `serializeDoc` rebuilt every document from scratch, every save silently dropped the file's XMP metadata and output intent, i.e. real data loss for the archival and print audiences this program exists for, not merely a wrong validation report. Not CLOSED -- it awaits qa's retest.
- orchestrator: NOTE (not a status change) -- the same fix cycle produced an evidenced list of catalog entries `serializeDoc` still drops, and two of them are correctness bugs in their own right: `/Names /JavaScript` was dropped (so the PDF/A JavaScript rule could FALSELY PASS on any document opened through the app -- a validator that can falsely pass is worse than no validator) and `/OCProperties` was dropped (so optional-content layers are lost on save, which REQUIREMENTS.md Phase 57's layers panel and visibility-toggle criterion depend on). Both were fixed in a follow-up by carrying `/MarkInfo`, `/Lang`, `/ViewerPreferences`, `/OCProperties`, `/Collection` and `/AF` (none capable of holding a page reference) plus a SELECTIVE carry of only the `/Names /JavaScript` subtree, because cloning `/Names` wholesale would drag page-referencing named destinations into the destination context and risk the page tree. Still dropped, with reasons: `/StructTreeRoot` (tagged-PDF structure references page objects -- needs a real re-tagging pass), `/Names` wholesale and `/Dests` (they reference pages), `/OpenAction` (may hold a page destination), `/AcroForm` (the engine owns form serialization). Evidence: 267 targeted tests pass; the JS check is asserted on BOTH sides (a JS document now reports `pdfa.javascript` on the serialized bytes, a non-JS document reports none); the page-tree safety proof asserts the destination `/Names` keeps `/JavaScript` and NOT the source's `/Dests`, with the page count and page content bytes unchanged; `/OCProperties` round-trips with its OCG names and Order array intact.
- qa: CLOSED (Phase 54 DEF-378 run-close retest on the current dev tree, after `npm.cmd run build`). `e2e/phase54_imaging_validation.spec.cjs` `P54_C5A` -> `{"target":"pdfa-1b","conforms":"true","declared":"PDF/A-1b","rules":[]}`; `P54_C5B` -> `{"declared":"PDF/A-1b","conforms":"false","rules":[{"rule":"pdfa.output-intent","severity":"error"},{"rule":"pdfa.font-embedding","severity":"error"}]}` - both violations are REAL for this fixture (it genuinely carries no OutputIntent and a non-embedded base-14 font), and the previous run's spurious `declared: "none declared"` is gone; `P54_C5C` -> `{"variant":"blocked","rules":["pdfa.output-intent","pdfa.font-embedding"],"wrote":false}` (refused, no file written, correct list); `P54_C6A` -> `{"target":"pdfx-1a","conforms":"true","declared":"PDF/X-1:2001","rules":[]}`; `P54_C6B` -> `pdfx.device-rgb` naming `page(s) 1`, `ops {rg:1,k:0}` (no conversion). The full Phase 54 gate spec is 20/20 green. Screenshots inspected: screenshots/phase54-c5-pdfa-ok.png (Declared PDF/A-1b, "Conforms to the checked target") and screenshots/phase54-retest-js-positive.png.

An `<img>` anywhere counts as content, so an image-only markdown or HTML document does NOT warn (the honest boundary), while a headings-only or whitespace-only source does. ## DEF-374: every Phase 53 non-PDF import crashes with an unhandled TypeError and creates no tab

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 53

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build the current tree (`npm.cmd run build`) and launch TFlex (dev build).
2. Click the title-bar Open button (Ctrl+O) and pick any convertible non-PDF file, e.g. `test-fixtures/phase53/sample.txt` (repeat with `sample.md`, `sample.rtf`, `sample.csv`, `sample.html`).
3. Observe the renderer.

Expected: the file imports into a tab with a `[data-conversion-notice]` card (Phase 53 criterion 1).
Actual: an unhandled renderer TypeError `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'inner')` fires; no tab is created, no conversion notice, no toast. The app stays on the Welcome screen. Reproduced for all five formats and for the OS-open path (which shows the hook's fallback toast "Jovrel could not open the requested file.").

Root cause: `src/renderer/App.tsx` `openConvertedFromPath` extracts the engine method into a local and calls it unbound:
`const bytesApi = engineRef.current.getDocumentBytes; ... return bytesApi(id);`
`getDocumentBytes` is a prototype method on `RealEngineAdapter` (`src/renderer/engine/engineClient.ts`), so the unbound call loses `this` and `this.inner` throws. The unit test `phase53_convertImport.test.tsx` mocks `getDocumentBytes` as a plain function, so it never exercises this wiring.

Evidence: `e2e/phase53_format_import.spec.cjs` (criteria 1/2/3/7/8/10 and rows 5/6 fail with this pageerror). Pageerror stack: `at getDocumentBytes (index-*.js) at Object.getDocumentBytes ... at async Object.openConverted`.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase53-open-txt.png (Welcome screen, no tab after the .txt open).

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 53 phase validation).
- orchestrator: FIX-READY -- relaying frontend-dev: `openConvertedFromPath` now calls `engineRef.current.getDocumentBytes(id)` on the object instead of extracting the method into a local alias, so `RealEngineAdapter`'s prototype method keeps its `this`. The regression that hid it is closed too: `test/unit/renderer/phase53_convertImport.test.tsx` now uses a prototype-style engine mock whose method reads `this.inner`, plus a source pin asserting the call site is `engineRef.current.getDocumentBytes(id)` and not an extracted local. The developer demonstrated the check is load-bearing by temporarily reverting the fix to the unbound form and observing the new assertion fail (`Tests 1 failed | 19 passed`, exit 1), then restoring it. Evidence: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer` -> 415 files / 4389 tests passed, exit 0; `npm.cmd run verify` -> exit 0 (conventions clean, 266 files, tsc clean); `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase53_format_import.spec.cjs` -> 9 passed / 3 failed, including `ok 1 criterion 1: .txt/.md/.rtf/.csv/.html each import into a tab` (the crash is gone; the 3 remaining failures are separate findings, reported by qa in the retest). Not CLOSED -- it awaits qa's retest.
- qa: CLOSED (Phase 53 gate retest on the current dev tree). `e2e/phase53_retest_qa.spec.cjs` DEF-374 opened all five fixtures through the real Open dialog: each created a tab with `[data-conversion-notice]` and the correct source label, `pageErrors: []` for every case, `pageCount >= 1`. The gate spec's criterion 1 also passes (5/5 formats). Screenshots inspected: screenshots/phase53-retest-def374-txt.png and screenshots/phase53-retest-def374-html.png (tab + notice card + rendered content, no crash). The unbound `getDocumentBytes` call is gone (`engineRef.current.getDocumentBytes(id)`).

## DEF-375: the main Open dialog does not expose the Phase 53 grouped filters

The three PDF-only pickers were verified unchanged and still work: merge picker -> `[{"name":"PDF","extensions":["pdf"]}]`, insert-from-PDF picker -> `[{"name":"PDF","extensions":["pdf"]}]`, FDF import picker -> `[{"name":"FDF","extensions":["fdf"]}]`. ## DEF-372: re-opening the same encrypted file in a session re-prompts for the password (the session cache is keyed by a fresh engine doc id)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 52

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (dev build).
2. Open a synthetic AES-256 password-protected PDF (a real user password); enter the correct password at the prompt. The tab opens.
3. Open the SAME file again through the Open dialog.
4. Observe the password prompt appears again.

Expected: the Phase 52 verification item 2 expects "a second open of the same doc in the session does not re-prompt (the session cache)". The main-process session cache (`EngineService.docPasswords`) is documented to prevent a re-prompt for a later (re)load of the same document.

Actual: the UI re-prompts. The cache is keyed by the engine doc id, and the renderer mints a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` engine doc id on every open (`App.tsx` `openFromBytes`), so the cache never matches a UI re-open. The engine-level cache itself works: reloading the SAME doc id with no password succeeds (verified in the gate spec). REQUIREMENTS.md criterion 2 does not mandate cross-open caching, so this is a usability gap, not a requirement breach.

Screenshot: none

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 52 gate validation).
- qa: CLOSED (Phase 53 gate retest on the current dev tree; the fix was present in the tree but had no FIX-READY record, so the ledger and the code disagreed). `e2e/phase53_retest_qa.spec.cjs` DEF-372 opened a synthetic AES-256 fixture, entered the password, then re-opened the SAME path through the real Open dialog: `P53R_DEF372 {"firstTabs":1,"second":{"promptOpen":false,"openTabs":2}}` - no re-prompt, the second open lands as a second tab. `src/renderer/App.tsx` `openPdfBytesFromPath` now consults `sessionPasswords.recall(path)` before the open (the DEF-372 comment). Screenshot: screenshots/phase53-retest-def372.png (second open, no prompt). Note: a prior run's fix was never relayed to the ledger.

## DEF-368: the first Jovrel installer (1.41.0) inherited the TFlex install location and nested itself at C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: operator (live install), relayed through the orchestrator; filed by qa
- Phase: 49

Steps to reproduce:
1. Install the per-machine TFlex build so HKLM `Software\f890a78b-df18-5f38-8f11-e53795b72a9d` `InstallLocation` = `C:\Program Files\TFlex` (appId `com.tflex.app` -> NSIS GUID f890a78b-df18-5f38-8f11-e53795b72a9d).
2. Run the 1.41.0 Jovrel installer (perMachine, allowToChangeInstallationDirectory).
3. Inspect the install directory and the Add/Remove Programs entry.

Expected: the product installs to `C:\Program Files\Jovrel` (Phase 49 success criterion 1), replacing the TFlex install in place (criterion 2), with no stale TFlex directory left.

Actual: the installer lands at `C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel` and leaves `C:\Program Files\TFlex` (now containing only `Jovrel`) behind. The app runs and the shortcuts are correct, but the install-path criterion is broken and a stale parent remains.

Root cause (verified against the generated NSIS and the electron-builder templates, not guessed):
- `appId` deliberately stays `com.tflex.app`, so the install-info key is HKLM `Software\<GUID>` and `initMultiUser` reads it.
- `templates/nsis/multiUser.nsh` `initMultiUser` -> `setInstallModePerAllUsers` copies that key's `InstallLocation` into `$INSTDIR`; on an upgrade over TFlex that value is `C:\Program Files\TFlex`.
- `templates/nsis/assistedInstaller.nsh`'s `instFilesPre` then runs `${StrContains} $0 "${APP_FILENAME}" $INSTDIR`; `APP_FILENAME` is `Jovrel`, the inherited path does not contain it, so `StrCpy $INSTDIR "$INSTDIR\${APP_FILENAME}"` appends `\Jovrel`.

Raw registry / filesystem evidence (operator machine; read-only re-confirmed by qa):
- HKLM `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\f890a78b-df18-5f38-8f11-e53795b72a9d`: `DisplayName = Jovrel 1.41.0`, `DisplayVersion = 1.41.0`, `InstallLocation = C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel`, `UninstallString = "C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel\Uninstall Jovrel.exe" /allusers`.
- HKLM `Software\f890a78b-df18-5f38-8f11-e53795b72a9d`: `InstallLocation = C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel`.
- `C:\Program Files\TFlex` contains exactly one child, `Jovrel`; `C:\Program Files\Jovrel` does not exist.
- Shortcuts are correct: `Start Menu\Programs\Jovrel.lnk` and `Public\Desktop\Jovrel.lnk` -> `C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel\Jovrel.exe`.

Fix (1.41.1): `electron-builder.nsh` adds a `customInit` macro (inserted by `installer.nsi` immediately after `initMultiUser`) that resets a `$INSTDIR` under the legacy `$PROGRAMFILES64\TFlex` root to `$PROGRAMFILES64\Jovrel`, plus a leftover cleanup in `customInstall` that removes `$PROGRAMFILES64\TFlex\Jovrel` only when it holds BOTH `Jovrel.exe` AND `Uninstall Jovrel.exe`, then non-recursively removes the (now-empty) `$PROGRAMFILES64\TFlex`. A user-chosen custom path outside the TFlex root is preserved.

Screenshot: none

History:
- qa: opened (filed from the operator's live 1.41.0 install evidence, relayed by the orchestrator).
- qa: CLOSED (release-gate verification of the 1.41.1 installer from source + artifact; the operator's elevated install is the only remaining live confirmation). Evidence on the 1.41.1 tree:
  - `test/unit/main/phase49InstallDir.test.ts` -> 7 passed, including the live `makensis -PPO` preprocess of the real `electron-builder.nsh`.
  - An independent QA `electron-builder --win nsis` rebuild (scratch output; `release/` untouched) produced `Jovrel-Setup-1.41.1-x64.exe` at exactly the shipped size 173,348,601 bytes; its generated installer script `!include`s `...\TFlex\electron-builder.nsh` and inserts `!insertmacro customInit` immediately after `!insertmacro initMultiUser`.
  - QA `makensis -PPO` expansion of the real `.nsh`: `StrCpy $0 "$PROGRAMFILES64\TFlex"` / `StrLen $1 $0` / `StrCmp `$2` `$0`` ... `StrCpy $INSTDIR "$PROGRAMFILES64\Jovrel"`; cleanup `IfFileExists `$0\Jovrel\Jovrel.exe``, `IfFileExists `$0\Jovrel\Uninstall Jovrel.exe``, `RMDir /r "$0\Jovrel"`, `RMDir "$0"` (non-recursive, no `RMDir /r "$0"`).
  - `release/Jovrel-Setup-1.41.1-x64.exe` sha512 (independently recomputed by qa) `hVVm1XZ5M7kKBYMXvYwYUWpX8gVuTRlfZX4HO5LWMaKXXEexL8/DyDBO6/5yTURfiKdhx/DXO5IvW99hIrQcOg==`, size 173,348,601, equals `latest.yml`; version 1.41.1.
  - The operator's machine meets the cleanup preconditions (nested dir holds `Jovrel.exe` + `Uninstall Jovrel.exe`). Remaining operator-only confirmation: run the 1.41.1 setup elevated and confirm `C:\Program Files\Jovrel\Jovrel.exe`, ARP `InstallLocation = C:\Program Files\Jovrel`, and both `C:\Program Files\TFlex\Jovrel` and the emptied `C:\Program Files\TFlex` gone.

## DEF-366: the Phase 48 bar clamp puts a bottom-edge annotation's action bar into the comment box's zone, so Confirm/Cancel/Delete are covered and unclickable

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 48

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0), then `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase48_gate.spec.cjs -g "annotation bars clamp"`.
   (Manual: open `report.pdf`, REVIEW > Annotate > Rectangle, drag a rectangle flush to the page's bottom edge, then click it to select it.)
2. Select the bottom-edge rectangle. The selection opens the comment box (Phase-28 behaviour) as well as the action bar.

Expected: the action bar (Confirm / colour / Cancel / Delete) stays inside the page and its buttons are clickable - Phase 48 success criterion 3 / feature C ("every control must stay inside the visible canvas/viewport").

Actual: the bar is inside the page, but the comment box is bottom-anchored just above the annotation and overlaps almost the entire bar (the Phase 48 clamp flips the bar above the annotation when there is no room below, which is exactly the comment box's zone). `document.elementFromPoint` at the Delete button's centre returns the comment box, and a real mouse click at that point does not delete the annotation. Raw measurements (page-relative CSS px):
- rect flush at the page bottom, 100% (page 612x792): bar top=656.0 bottom=689.1; comment-box top=564.8 bottom=684.7 (overlap 656-684.7 = ~29 of the bar's 33px); Delete centre (768.2, 633.2) -> `DIV|ann-comment-form`; real click left the rect count unchanged (1 -> 1).
- rect at the bottom-right corner, 100%: bar top=666.0 bottom=699.1; comment-box top=534.8 bottom=654.7; Delete centre -> `BUTTON|ann-comment-submit`.
- ellipse flush at the page bottom, 100%: bar top=656.0 bottom=689.1; Delete centre -> `DIV|ann-comment-form`.
- rect flush at the page bottom, 110% (page 673.2x871.2): bar top=725.2 bottom=758.3; Delete centre -> `DIV|ann-comment-form`.
- note at the page bottom, 100%: bar bottom=786.1, clickable (no comment box mounted at that moment), so 4 of the 5 bottom-edge cases are blocked.

Root cause: `commentBoxPlacement` computes its clearance from a bar that sits BELOW the annotation (`barTop = ring.top + ring.height + 4`) and, when there is no room below, bottom-anchors the card just above the ring; the Phase 48 clamp now flips the bar ABOVE the ring too, so the two collide. `AnnotationOverlay` passes only `otherAnnBounds` as `avoid`, so the card cannot see the action bar. The pre-fix bar was simply off-page (the operator's original report); the clamp moved it into the card's zone without coordinating the two.

Screenshot: screenshots/phase48-gate-rect-bottom.png

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 48 gate; independent e2e re-measure in `e2e/phase48_gate.spec.cjs`).
- qa: CLOSED (FIX-READY retest on the rebuilt tree; `e2e/phase48_gate.spec.cjs` -> 3 passed). The card now derives from the bar's ACTUAL box (`selectionActionBarBox`), so it sits on the bar's far side. Re-measured page-relative CSS px, all `insidePage:true`, `elementFromPoint` at the Delete centre resolves to the Delete BUTTON, and a real click deletes:
  - rect-bottom-100 (page 612x792): bar top=656.0 bottom=689.1; comment-box top=528.1 bottom=648.0 (clear of the bar by 8px); Delete centre (768.2,633.2) -> `BUTTON|...--delete`; real click 1 -> 0.
  - rect-corner-100: bar top=666.0 bottom=699.1; comment-box top=538.1 bottom=658.0; Delete centre (952.6,643.2) -> `BUTTON|...--delete`.
  - ellipse-bottom-100: bar top=656.0 bottom=689.1; comment-box top=528.1 bottom=648.0; Delete centre (621.3,633.2) -> `BUTTON|...--delete`.
  - note-bottom-100: bar top=753.0 bottom=786.1; no comment box mounted; Delete centre (952.6,730.2) -> `BUTTON|...--delete`.
  - rect-bottom-110 (page 673.2x871.2): bar top=736.2 bottom=769.3; comment-box top=608.4 bottom=728.3; Delete centre (983.2,634.7) -> `BUTTON|...--delete`.
  Zero out-of-view / unclickable offenders. Evidence: `e2e/phase48_gate.spec.cjs` item-3 run log.

## DEF-365: the Google sign-in popup still does not close on the loopback landing - the completion rule never fires because the listener clears the active callback URL first

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 47

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the packaged 1.40.0 build (`TFLEX_PACKAGED_EXE` = the fresh win-unpacked TFlex.exe).
2. Open the top-right account entry, then click "Continue with Google".
3. The popup opens on the auth host and redirects to `accounts.google.com` (the natural sequence; a real account is needed to go further).
4. Drive the popup to the flow's OWN minted loopback URL (the landing the provider's redirect produces) - e.g. `e2e/phase47_google_completion.spec.cjs` reads the `callbackURL` from the `sign-in/social` request body and calls `loadURL` on the popup.

Expected: the popup closes when the flow lands on the loopback callback (the Phase 47 completion rule), and the trace records `popup-complete` + `popup-closed`.

Actual: the popup stays open. The trace shows `loopback-hit` (path `/oauth/callback`), then `popup-navigate` to the exact minted loopback URL, then `exchange-cookies` / `exchange-get-session` / `exchange-failed` - but NO `popup-complete` and NO `popup-closed`. Root cause: `OAuthCallbackService.handle()` calls `respond(res, 200, SUCCESS_PAGE)` then `this.finish('ok')`, and `finish` -> `closeActive()` sets `this.active = null` synchronously. The popup's `did-navigate` fires later, so `deps.getLoopbackUrl()` (`oauthCallback.currentCallbackUrl()`) returns null and `isLoopbackCompletionUrl(url, null)` is false. The matcher only works while the flow is still active. Diagnostic proof: driving the popup to the same origin+path with a WRONG token (listener refuses 403, flow stays active) DOES close the popup and traces `popup-complete` + `popup-closed`; the correct-token path does not. This is the operator's original blocker, still present in 1.40.0.

Screenshot: none (trace evidence in `e2e/phase47-completion.log`).

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 47 release-gate verification on the packaged 1.40.0 build; `e2e/phase47_google_completion.spec.cjs` test 1 fails, test 2 diagnostic passes).
- qa: CLOSED (FIX-READY retest on the REBUILT 1.40.0 artifacts; `TFLEX_PACKAGED_EXE` = the fresh `%TEMP%\opencode\tflex-dist-1400b\win-unpacked\TFlex.exe`). `e2e/phase47_google_completion.spec.cjs` -> 2 passed. The correct-token path now traces `popup-open, popup-redirect x4, popup-navigate, loopback-hit, exchange-cookies, popup-navigate, popup-complete, popup-closed, popup-cookies, exchange-get-session, exchange-failed`; the window count returns to 1 (the popup closed on its own) and the exchange still runs. The retained minted URL (`lastCallbackUrl` + 30 s grace, cleared on popup close / new flow) is the fix. Evidence: `e2e/phase47-completion-rerun.log`.

## DEF-363: the icon guard's import extractor drops the first icon after a preceding named import, so the app-wide sweep misses shared icons (a different-action `Hash` pair remains)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 43

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0).
2. Replicate the guard's `importedIcons` regex (`/import\s+(?:type\s+)?\{([\s\S]*?)\}\s+from\s+["']lucide-react["']/g`) on `src/renderer/components/Inspector.tsx`: the captured names are `["useMemo } from 'react';\r\nimport type { ReactElement","ReactNode } from 'react';\r\nimport { Hash","PanelRightClose","PanelRightOpen","X"]` — `Hash` is polluted and not detected.
3. Run the corrected app-wide sweep (per-import `[^}]*` extraction): 55 lucide files / 134 distinct icons / 69 shared.

## DEF-359: Palette reports a stage-native pin as "pinned to the dock" in stages whose dock filters it out

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-097)
- Phase: 42

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0); seed a temp userData dir with a copy of the operator's real `%APPDATA%\tflex\settings.json` (carries `dockPins: ["watermark"]`) and launch the dev app through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` helper; open `report.pdf`.
2. Walk every stage (Ctrl+1..4), read the Action Dock verb/pin lists, then open Ctrl+K in each stage and read the Watermark row's `data-palette-pinned` / `data-palette-pin-state` / `data-palette-pin-stage`.
3. In EDIT (Ctrl+2) open Ctrl+K, search "watermark", click its pin toggle, read the notice, and re-read the persisted `dockPins`.

Expected: the Phase-40 item-6 / DEF-353 contract — the palette's pin toggle reflects what the dock is actually showing, and the two surfaces never disagree about the same tool. With Phase 42's one-home filter the dock hides a stage-native pin outside its stage, so the palette must stop reporting that tool as pinned in those stages (or state that it is pinned in its own stage), and a toggle in a foreign stage must name the dock the action actually touched.

Actual (pre-fix): `isPinVisibleInStage` was applied only in `ActionDock`; the host's `isPaletteToolPinned` (`dockPins.includes(id)`) was unchanged, so the palette reported the tool pinned in stages whose dock filtered it out. With `dockPins: ["watermark"]` the dock correctly showed Watermark only in REVIEW, but the palette row had `data-palette-pinned=true` and state `pinned` in ALL FOUR stages. Pressing that toggle in EDIT reported "Unpinned Watermark from the dock" although the EDIT dock never contained it; pinning from EDIT reported "Pinned Watermark to the dock" while the EDIT dock was unchanged (the pin actually lands in REVIEW).

Raw (post-fix): `e2e/def359_palette_pin_verify.spec.cjs` — 2 passed. Per-stage Watermark row with the operator's real `dockPins:["watermark"]`:
- PAGES: dockHasWatermark=false; row `data-palette-pinned="false"`, `data-palette-pin-state="pinned-elsewhere"`, `data-palette-pin-stage="review"`, aria-label "Unpin Watermark from the Review dock".
- EDIT: identical to PAGES.
- REVIEW: dockHasWatermark=true; row `data-palette-pinned="true"`, `data-palette-pin-state="pinned"`, no `data-palette-pin-stage`, aria-label "Unpin Watermark from the dock".
- DELIVER: identical to PAGES.
Watermark renders in exactly REVIEW across the four docks. Unpin/re-pin from EDIT: persisted `dockPins` before `["watermark"]`; unpin notice "Unpinned Watermark from the Review dock", row flips to `unpinned`, persisted `[]`; re-pin notice "Pinned Watermark to the Review dock", row returns to `pinned-elsewhere`, persisted `["watermark"]` — a real state change each way, no phantom message.

History:
- qa: opened (adversary ADV-097).
- fix: `buildPaletteRows` scopes the marker to the active stage via `isPinVisibleInStage` (`pinned` = in the current dock, `pinnedStage` = the tool's own stage when the current dock filters it out); `palettePinStateFor` / `palettePinDockName` drive the toggle state and the notice copy, and `CommandPalette` passes `activeStage`.
- qa: CLOSED -- retested on the rebuilt dev tree. `e2e/def359_palette_pin_verify.spec.cjs`: 2 passed. The palette marker agrees with the dock's visible contents in every stage (pinned iff the dock shows it), names REVIEW as the home in the three foreign stages, and the foreign-stage unpin/re-pin notices name the Review dock and make a real persisted change.

## DEF-356: Ctrl+S on a CLEAN on-disk document rewrote the file although the toolbar Save is disabled

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW

- Phase: 40

Steps to reproduce:

History:
- qa: opened (Ctrl+S observation, Phase 40 post-gate).
- fix: `saveIntentFor` (src/renderer/state/saveGuard.ts) resolves a clean on-disk document to `clean` and App's `onSave` returns without writing; a modified document resolves to `save`.
- qa: CLOSED -- retested on the rebuilt dev tree. `e2e/phase40_def351_356_verify.spec.cjs` DEF-356: 6 passed overall; the clean Ctrl+S left the file byte-identical (SHA 9b39af69e81ee8a5, mtime and size unchanged) and the modified Ctrl+S wrote a new SHA (7129733769f60ac8) and returned the document to clean (Save disabled). The modified case is the control proving the accelerator path really saves, so the clean no-op is not a false pass.

## DEF-353: The palette pin icon can disagree with the dock when an id is present in both `dockPins` and `dockUnpinned`

Steps to reproduce:

## DEF-350: verify:full gate flake - engine getDocumentBytes byte-equality test fails when the two serializations straddle a one-second boundary

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 39

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run verify:full` on the Phase 39 tree (the release-gate run), repeatedly.
2. Intermittently, `test/unit/main/engine.test.ts > EngineService - getDocumentBytes > returns re-parseable bytes that match save output (round-trip)` fails at line 1327 (`expect(same).toBe(true)`): the bytes `getDocumentBytes` returns are not byte-identical to the bytes `save()` wrote.

Expected: the two serializations compare byte-identical, so the test is deterministic.
Actual: pdf-lib stamps `/ModDate` with the current time on every save (`updateInfoDict` in pdf-lib `PDFDocument.js` calls `setModificationDate(new Date())`; PDF date strings are second-resolution). `getDocumentBytes` and `save()` each call `serializeDoc` -> `out.save()`, so when the two calls straddle a one-second boundary the `/ModDate` differs and the byte comparison fails. Observed once in the release-gate run (exit 1, `1 failed | 5131 passed`), then green twice: the isolated file run (`npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/engine.test.ts` -> 237 passed) and the immediate `verify:full` re-run (396 files / 5132 tests passed, exit 0). The DEF-349 fix touches only renderer layout files, so the engine path is unaffected.
Screenshot: n/a (test-only). Logs: e2e/phase39-verifyfull-rerun.log (failed run) vs e2e/phase39-verifyfull-rerun2.log (green re-run).

History:
- qa: opened (observed during the Phase 39 release-gate `verify:full`; intermittent, gate passed on rerun).
- qa: CLOSED -- retested the backend-dev fix on the current tree. `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/engine.test.ts` run 3 times: 237 passed / 237 passed / 237 passed (1 file passed each run, 0 failed). Assertion-strength check (git diff of `test/unit/main/engine.test.ts`): the fix only wraps the two serializing calls in `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })` + `vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'))` (restored in a `finally`); the byte-for-byte comparison is untouched -- `savedView[i] !== gotView[i]` over every byte with `expect(same).toBe(true)`, plus the `saved.byteLength === r.value.byteLength` length check. A genuine engine regression (any content-stream/page-tree difference) would still fail it; only the `/ModDate` second-boundary flake is removed. No product code changed.

## DEF-338: Multi Mode - opening a document into pane B lays the page out at the full-stage fit-width (204% for the payslip) and flashes an oversized grey placeholder before snapping to the half-pane fit-width (69%)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 38

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0); launch the dev app through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen.
2. Open `test-fixtures/squiggly-native.pdf` (or any fixture) via the title-bar Open control (mocked OS dialog); wait for the page.
3. Click the title-bar Multi Mode toggle `[data-header-multi-mode]`; pane B shows its empty state.
4. Click pane B's `[data-pane-open]` and pick `C:\Users\tanzi\Downloads\TanzimulIslamPaySlip20260930.pdf` (the operator's payslip, used IN PLACE - never copied into the repo).
5. Watch pane B during the open.

Expected: pane B lays the page out at its own half-pane fit-width from the first painted frame; the page (or its placeholder) never exceeds the pane; the zoom readout goes straight to the half-pane fit-width (~69%).

Actual: pane B's page slot is first laid out at the FULL-STAGE width (~1214px, the single-pane document width) and the pane's zoom readout shows 204% (fit-width computed against the full stage). The `.page-placeholder` shimmer (light grey `#e5e7eb`) is painted at that oversized slot, filling the whole pane as a grey slab, while the pane B thumbnail already shows the payslip. The slot then converges 1214 -> 454 -> 434 -> 422 -> 414 -> 413px over ~160-240ms (each step cancelling the in-flight render), and the page finally paints at 69%. The zoom readout jumps 204% -> 69%.

Raw measurements (CDP `Page.startScreencast`, full-res 1280x900, `e2e/def338_repro.spec.cjs`): 35 frames captured across the open; frames open-12..open-23 (12 consecutive frames) show pane B as a uniform grey placeholder slab; open-24..open-34 show the rendered payslip. Pane B zoom pill reads "204%" in open-12 and "69%" in open-23. Per-frame in-page rAF probe (`e2e/def338_probe.spec.cjs`): pane B slot width sequence [1214, 454, 434, 422, 414, 413], canvas backing sequence [1214x1717, 454x642, 434x614, 414x585, 413x584], `.page-placeholder` present for 9 frames (t=146..305ms).

Scope matrix (`e2e/def338_scope.spec.cjs`, same probe):
- Normal fixture `report.pdf` into pane B: slot [1204, 412, 404, 403], canvas backing [612x792, 1204x1558, 412x533, 404x522, 403x521], placeholder 8 frames (167..403ms). REPRODUCES.
- Payslip 20260930 into pane B: slot [1214, 454, 434, 422, 414, 413], placeholder 9 frames (146..305ms). REPRODUCES.
- Sibling payslip 20260731 into pane B: slot [1214, 442, 427, 418, 413], placeholder 8 frames (113..259ms). REPRODUCES.
- Payslip in SINGLE mode: slot [612, 950, 940] (grows from a smaller initial value to the correct full-width fit), placeholder 4 frames (146..235ms). A brief placeholder flash at the correct size, NOT the oversized slab.
- Payslip as pane A when Multi Mode turns on: slot [940, 403, 413], placeholder 0 frames. No glitch (the already-painted frame is kept).
- Focus switch to/from pane B, scroll, zoom step: 64/32/30 frames, all stable, no glitch.

So the glitch is specific to opening a document INTO pane B (the pane's DocumentView measures its scroller before the multi-mode split constrains it), not to the payslip.

Structural facts about the payslip (read-only, in place, `e2e/def338_inspect.cjs`): 1 page, MediaBox 595x842 (A4), /Rotate 0, resources only /Font + /ProcSet; no XObjects, images, inline images (BI/ID/EI = 0), tiling patterns, shading, transparency groups, soft masks, annotations or AcroForm; content is 18,163 decoded bytes of text/vector (198 q / 197 Q, 126 re, 115 W n, 83 BT/ET, 70 Tj, 14 TJ); two embedded Type0 CID LiberationSans subsets. The "large image / XObject / pattern / transparency" suspects are all absent.

Console/error evidence: no renderer errors, no React errors, no unhandled rejections. The only console line is `Canvas2D: Multiple readback operations using getImageData are faster with the willReadFrequently attribute set to true`, emitted by the QA harness's own `getImageData` sampler, not the product.

Root-cause hypothesis (proven vs suspected):
PROVEN: pane B's fit-width scale is computed against the full-stage width on the first layout pass. `DocumentView.effectiveScale` = `(viewportBox.w - CONTENT_PADDING_PX*2) / fitAnchor.w` (`src/renderer/components/DocumentView.tsx:1516-1519`), and `viewportBox` is set from `scrollerRef.current.clientWidth` in the mount effect and a ResizeObserver (`DocumentView.tsx:1737-1749`). For the payslip, 1214/595 = 2.04 = the 204% readout; the final 413/595 = 0.69 = 69%. The slot/canvas/zoom sequences above are the direct measurement of that scale being recomputed as the pane width converges.
SUSPECTED (not yet proven at source level): the pane B scroller reports the full stage width on its first measurement because the pane's DocumentView mounts before the multi-mode split constrains the pane's content box (a mount-before-layout race); the ResizeObserver then corrects it through several steps. This is a layout/scale race, NOT the DEF-274 canvas-backing-store clear class: the visible canvas is never cleared to blank (the placeholder covers it), and the canvas is re-rendered at each new scale via the existing scratch-canvas swap.

Severity: MEDIUM -- a visible, jarring flash on every document opened into pane B (the page appears at ~3x its correct size as a grey slab, and the zoom readout jumps 204% -> 69%), on a core Multi Mode workflow. No data loss and the page settles correctly, so not HIGH.

Screenshots: screenshots/def-338-paneB-glitch-204.png (payslip into pane B, glitch frame: grey placeholder slab, zoom 204%), screenshots/def-338-paneB-settled-69.png (same open settled: payslip rendered, zoom 69%), screenshots/def-338-normal-fixture-glitch.png (report.pdf into pane B, placeholder slab), screenshots/def-338-single-mode-glitch.png (payslip single mode: placeholder at the correct 158%, no oversized slab), screenshots/def-338-paneA-transition.png (payslip as pane A, no glitch). Harnesses: e2e/def338_repro.spec.cjs, e2e/def338_probe.spec.cjs, e2e/def338_scope.spec.cjs, e2e/def338_evidence.spec.cjs; frame analyzer e2e/def338_analyze.cjs; structural inspector e2e/def338_inspect.cjs.

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 38 item 5, feature E; operator-reported: "open TanzimulIslamPaySlip20260930.pdf from downloads folder in the 2nd window in multi view. The page glitches violently." Reproduced on the dev build after `npm.cmd run build` exit 0.)
- qa: retested on the rebuilt tree (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0). The VIOLENT full-stage glitch is FIXED: the pane B slot never reaches the full stage width (max 525px vs the 1214px slab before) and the zoom readout never shows 204%. `e2e/def338_repro.spec.cjs` -> 1 passed; pane B canvas backing 403x570 (not 1214x1717). BUT the strict criterion is NOT met, so it stays OPEN: `e2e/phase38_def338_payslip.spec.cjs` (operator's exact scenario, payslip IN PLACE) measured 3 placeholder frames WIDER than the settled fit (slot widths 525/465/409 vs the settled 403) and a zoom ramp 88% -> 78% -> 69% -> 68% -- the readout does not go straight to the correct fit. Residual root cause: the pane's document area first fits before its 150px thumbnail strip mounts, so the first fit is the strip-less pane width (88%) and then reflows to the with-strip fit (68%). Settled state is correct (payslip rendered, 68%); screenshot screenshots/phase38-def338-payslip-paneB.png; raw samples e2e/phase38-def338-payslip-samples.json.

The stability gate holds the first fit until the scroller box is stable. Residual (report.pdf into pane B still steps 403->393): judged imperceptible -- the widest frame is a blank placeholder at 66% and the page paints only at the settled 393/64%, so no page resize is visible (screenshots/def338-residual-report-widest.png, -after1.png, -after2.png, -settled.png).

## DEF-312: Phase 36 dock Pin/Unpin menu is positioned off-viewport (fixed-position inside the transformed dock) — pinning is unusable

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH

Actual: `.action-dock-menu` is `position: fixed` (styles.css) but is a descendant of `.action-dock`, which carries `transform: translateX(-50%)`. Measured live (e2e/phase36_chunk3_dock_gate.spec.cjs P36-C3-C): menu rect `{"left":1074,"top":1663,"right":1222,"bottom":1728,"vw":1442,"vh":903}` (and `top:1624` for every later open) — `insideViewport=false` on every open; Playwright reports "element is outside of the viewport". Screenshot: n/a (the menu is off-screen; the DOM rect + Playwright's viewport refusal are the evidence)

Severity: HIGH — the pins feature (Phase-36 criterion 7, "pins survive a restart") cannot be driven from the UI at all.

Evidence / command output:
- `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase36_chunk3_dock_gate.spec.cjs -g P36-C3-C` -> `[P36C3-C] pin menu rect={"left":1074,"top":1663,...,"vh":903} insideViewport=false` (repeated on every open).
