## DEF-309: launchApp(extraArgs) wedges the dev app before any window exists

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa (diagnosed during the Phase 36 chunk-1 gate)
- Phase: 36

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0).
2. Launch the dev app through the canonical helper with any non-empty extra arg, e.g. `launchApp(['--disable-gpu'])` (same for `--host-resolver-rules=MAP * 127.0.0.1`, `--force-prefers-reduced-motion`).
3. Observe `app.isReady()` is true and the main process logs its startup lines (e.g. the update feed), but `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` stays 0; the next `app.evaluate` never returns and `app.firstWindow()` times out after 30 s. `launchApp([])` reaches one window in ~2 s.

Expected: the app launches with the extra switch applied and reaches a window exactly like a bare launch.
Actual: no window is ever observable; the main process is blocked. Any arg-passing launch is silently broken (this cost `e2e/phase31_whats_new.spec.cjs` its DNS-block coverage under DEF-308 and left `e2e/anim_audit.spec.cjs` A6 red).
Harness/Logs: `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` built the dev argv as `[...extraArgs, projectRoot, --user-data-dir=..., ...extraArgs]` (extraArgs both before the app path AND appended again). `src/main/open-path.ts` `extractFileArgument(argv, isPackaged=false)` starts at index 2 and returns the first non-switch token, so a switch before the app path makes it return the app directory; `handleOsOpenPath` then calls the synchronous modal `dialog.showErrorBox('Cannot open file', ...)` (src/main/index.ts:131-135), blocking the main thread before the window is observable. Diagnostic log: `[diag] t=5ms ready=true wins=0` then the next evaluate hangs (test timeout 60 s). Reproduced with `--disable-gpu`; a variant with extraArgs before the app path and NO duplicate also wedges, so the position is the cause (the duplicate was a second, independent bug).
Screenshot: n/a

## DEF-302: Page zoom in/out reads as a rubber-band: the slot layout jumps instantly while only the page transform animates

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: operator (2026-09-22, reported to the orchestrator)
- Phase: 35

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0) and launch the dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen (`.sample-card`).
2. Open `test-fixtures/report.pdf` (34 pages); wait for `.pdf-page canvas`; settle 1.5 s.
3. Install the frame sampler: a rAF loop recording, per frame, the `.page-slot[data-page="1"]` layout box (offsetTop/offsetHeight), the `.pdf-page[data-page="1"]` computed transform scale, the canvas backing store + CSS size, the scroller `scrollTop`, the mounted/slot counts and the rAF delta; plus a MutationObserver on the page-1 `.textLayer` (the sharp raster blit) and an `animationstart` listener.
4. Click `button[aria-label="Zoom in"]` (198% -> 200%), sample ~900 ms; then click `button[aria-label="Zoom out"]` (200% -> 175%), sample ~900 ms.
5. Repeat with the FLIP paused at 60 ms / 125 ms for the screenshots.

Expected: the zoom step animates smoothly - the page content and its surrounding flow geometry move together, with no positional jump and no rubber-band.

Actual: the slot layout box resizes INSTANTLY in the same frame the transform animation starts, while only the page's transform animates over 250 ms, so the page rubber-bands inside an already-resized box and every neighbouring page / scroll position jumps immediately. Raw timeline (page 1, report.pdf, 198% -> 200%): baseline `slotH=1568 pageH=1568 scale=1 canvasW=1212 canvasCssW=1212px scrollTop=0`; frame 3 after the click (dt=17 ms) `slotH=1584 pageH=1584 scale=0.9902 canvasW=1224 canvasCssW=1224px flip=1`; the FLIP runs 46-279 ms (15 frames) with `scale 0.9902 -> 1`. Zoom-out (200% -> 175%): frame 3 `slotH=1386 pageH=1386 scale=1.143 canvasW=1071 canvasCssW=1071px flip=1`, FLIP 49-282 ms, `scale 1.143 -> 1`. The animation itself is smooth (max rAF delta 21 ms, zero frames >32 ms), so the jerkiness is the layout/visual mismatch, not dropped frames. On a 25% step (200% -> 250%, `from=0.8`, `slotH=1980`) the default `transform-origin: 50% 50%` starts the page content 198 px below its final position and grows it to fill - a large positional jump at the start. Hypothesis verdicts: (a) layout jumps instantly while only the transform animates - HOLDS (the cause); (b) raster re-render lands mid-animation - the text-layer rebuild lands at 39/77 ms of the 46-279 ms animation, but the double-buffer keeps the previous frame stretched (`canvasRectW` tracks 1212->1213->1214...), so NO flash / double image; (c) only some pages animate - NO, both mounted pages (1 and 2) start the FLIP at dt=63 ms (only 2 of 34 pages are mounted; the rest are empty slots); (d) scroll re-anchored mid-animation - NO, `scrollTop` stayed 0 throughout (page 1 at top; not tested while scrolled); (e) duration/easing mismatch or restart - NO, duration 250 ms = `--motion-duration-standard`, the scale curve is eased (zoom-out 1.143->1.141->1.136->1.124->1.103... = slow-fast-slow, matching `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)`), and exactly one `animationstart` per page per step; (f) virtualization re-mounts slots mid-zoom - NO, mounted stayed 2 / slots 34 with no remount. Root cause: `src/renderer/components/zoomFlip.ts` + the `tf-page-zoom-flip` keyframe animate only the `.pdf-page` wrapper's transform while `DocumentView` lays the `.page-slot` out at the NEW size immediately (the design comment says animating width/height would thrash layout), so the flow geometry and the visual page are decoupled for the 250 ms.

Screenshot: screenshots/def302-zoom-mid-in-60ms.png, screenshots/def302-zoom-mid-in-125ms.png, screenshots/def302-zoom-mid-out-125ms.png (page content mid-scale; no flash/blank/double image; the page is white paper on a light background so the slot gap is not clearly visible at these zoom levels). Harness: e2e/phase35_zoom_diag.spec.cjs (2/2 pass); log e2e/phase35_zoom_diag.log

History:
- qa: opened. Reproduced on the current dev build (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0) via `e2e/phase35_zoom_diag.spec.cjs` (2/2 pass). Raw frame timeline and hypothesis verdicts above.
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying frontend-dev - the animation is now a real FLIP that tracks the LAYOUT: a pure `zoomFlipInvert` computes, for the wrapper's pre-zoom rect (`first`) and its post-layout rect (`last`), `sx = first.width/last.width`, `sy = first.height/last.height`, `dx = first.left - last.left`, `dy = first.top - last.top`, applied about the element's TOP-LEFT (`transform-origin: 0 0`) as `translate(dx,dy) scale(sx,sy)` and animated to identity over the motion token (the old centre-origin scale-only effect was removed). The capture (`First`) happens synchronously in `zoomTo`/ctrl-wheel only when the ladder step actually changes the scale, and one `useLayoutEffect` then corrects the scroll anchor FIRST (so `Last` is measured against corrected geometry) and applies the per-page class+vars. Scroll-anchor rule: anchor the topmost page whose top is at or above the scroller's top edge, record its offset before and re-apply `scrollTop += (after - before)` after layout - verified on a scrolled document (anchor stayed at -50px, scrollTop 1450->1620). Non-animating slots still reflow instantly (accepted, matching native browser zoom) but every animated page's content now tracks its new box exactly, so the step reads as one motion. Reduced motion / Animations-off still suppress the animation while keeping the anchor correction. ## DEF-303: Maximizing from the minimized state is ~3x slower than from restored, and the app's window-state/caption update lags ~344 ms behind the window

- Status: CLOSED

2. Open `test-fixtures/report.pdf`; wait for `.pdf-page canvas`; settle 1.5 s.

Install the main-process probe (re-registers `window:maximize`/`window:minimize` with an arrival timestamp; wraps `win.maximize/restore/minimize`; listens to maximize/restore/resize/move; polls `isMaximized/isMinimized/isVisible/getBounds` every 5 ms) and the renderer probe (resize listener, ResizeObserver on `.document-scroller`, `settings.changed` echo listener, rAF frame sampler of the page-1 width / slot height / canvas backing store and the `.app-maximized` class).

6. Direct maximize-from-minimized: minimize, wait 1.2 s, call `win.maximize()` from main (the taskbar-preview maximize control), 3x.

Expected: maximizing from the minimized state returns the window and its content promptly, with no app-side stall and no state/caption lag.

Actual: the app-side maximize is fast and consistent; the delay the operator reports is dominated by the OS window-state transition, not by the renderer. So: (1) the window maximize itself is fast (~37 ms to the OS maximize event, ~64 ms to the content re-layout/re-raster) and the many-page fixture adds nothing; (2) maximizing DIRECTLY from minimized is ~3x slower (~155 ms to the OS maximize event, ~193 ms to content) - the extra ~120 ms is the OS/Electron window-state transition (`win.maximize()` on a minimized window), which the app does not control; (3) the only app-side lag is the window-state/caption update at ~344 ms (restored) / ~467 ms (direct), dominated by the 300 ms `GEOMETRY_DEBOUNCE_MS` in `src/main/window.ts` plus the async settings write + `settings:changed` echo (`src/main/index.ts` `onGeometryChanged` -> `SettingsService.save` -> `broadcast` -> `App.tsx` `setWindowMaximized`), so the app's own maximize control / `.app-maximized` class still shows the un-maximized state for ~300 ms after the window is already maximized. No intermittency was observed: the spread is tight across 13 runs (5 report + 5 scanned + 3 direct); no multi-hundred-ms or random window-maximize delay reproduced. The dominant contributor is therefore the OS window-state transition (main process), not the renderer's resize/re-raster work (~64 ms) and not a synchronous layout.

## DEF-301: In-app print dialog's printer selection silently reverts to the system default on reopen

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-077)
- Phase: 35

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0) and launch the dev build through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen (`.sample-card`).
2. Open `test-fixtures/report.pdf`; wait for `.pdf-page canvas`.
3. Click `[data-print]` to open the Print dialog; select "Microsoft Print to PDF" in `[data-print-printer]`; click `[data-print-cancel]` to close.
4. Reopen Print (`[data-print]`) and immediately select "Microsoft Print to PDF"; poll the select value every 75 ms for ~3 s while counting main-process `getPrintersAsync` calls. Repeat the reopen once more.

Expected: the chosen printer stays chosen; the pick must survive the async printer-list resolution, so a virtual-PDF job is produced inside TFlex through its own Save-As dialog (Phase 35 success criterion 3).

Actual: on a reopen the hook still holds the previous activation's `printers` state, so the options render immediately (stale) and the selection is made before the fresh `getPrintersAsync` resolves; when it resolves the printer-load effect calls `setDeviceName(preferred)` (the system default) and silently overwrites the pick. QA measurement (third reopen): selected `Microsoft Print to PDF` at t=8 ms, silently reverted to `Canon TS3100 series` (the system default) at t=86 ms with `getPrintersAsync` call count 3. Reproduced on the third reopen (timing-dependent; the second reopen did not revert in this run). With the default selected, `printJob` takes the non-virtual branch and would route the job to the physical default printer instead of producing the PDF inside TFlex. Pre-existing Phase-30 logic (`PrintDialog.tsx` at HEAD) relocated by Phase 35 into `src/renderer/components/usePrintControls.ts` (printer-list effect deps `[active, listPrinters, seed]`, `printers` state persisting across activations).

## DEF-283: Print: the movable dialog is not re-clamped when the window shrinks, leaving Print/Close off-screen and unclickable

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-069)
- Phase: 33

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build (`npm.cmd run build`) and launch through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen (`.sample-card`).
2. Open `test-fixtures/report.pdf` (34 pages) through the title-bar Open control (mocked OS dialog); wait for `.pdf-page canvas`.
3. Click `[data-print]` to open the Print dialog; wait for `[data-print-printer]` and for `[data-print-confirm]` to be enabled.
4. Drag the dialog by its header `[data-print-drag-handle]` hard toward the bottom-right (e.g. +6000,+6000 px). At 1440x900 the drag clamp holds it fully inside: `.print-dialog` rect right 1440 / bottom 900, offRight 0.
5. WITHOUT reopening the dialog, shrink the WINDOW (not the dialog) via `BrowserWindow.setSize` to 1100x760, then 900x620, then 700x560, waiting ~900 ms each.
6. After each shrink, read the `.print-dialog` rect and `[data-print-confirm]` rect against `window.innerWidth`/`innerHeight`, and attempt a `trial: true` click on `[data-print-confirm]` (never a real print).
7. Drag the header back to the left to test recovery.

Expected: Phase 33 requires the dialog to be "clamped so it always stays fully inside the window" and "the controls keep working after a move". After a window resize the panel should still be fully inside the viewport (re-clamped), so Print/Close remain reachable.

Actual: The clamp is evaluated only during a drag (`onHeaderPointerMove` -> `nextDragOffset` with the anchor captured at drag start, `src/renderer/components/printDialogDrag.ts`; `src/renderer/components/PrintDialog.tsx:199-203`). There is no `resize` listener and `applyDragOffset` never re-clamps, so the stored `translate3d` offset survives while the viewport shrinks. Measured in this retest (drag at 1440x900, then successive shrinks without reopening):
- 1100x760: `.print-dialog` `{left:550, top:64, right:1270, bottom:760}` vs viewport 1100x760 - offRight 170; `[data-print-confirm]` `{left:1191, right:1253}`; `trial: true` click times out (not actionable).
- 900x620: rect `{left:450, top:64, right:1170, bottom:620}` vs 900x620 - offRight 270; Print not actionable.
- 700x560: rect `{left:376, top:64, right:1044, bottom:560}` vs 700x560 - offRight 344; Print not actionable.
Baseline at 1440x900 after the same drag is clean (offRight 0, Print actionable). `isVisible()` stays true at every size (Playwright visibility ignores viewport clipping), so only the trial click reveals the unreachability.

Recoverability: YES - grabbing a visible part of the header and dragging left recovers the panel (at 700x560 it moved to `{left:0, top:0, right:668, bottom:496}`, Print actionable again). Note the header's own centre can be off-screen once clipped (at 700x560 the header spans 376..1044, centre 710 > viewport 700), so the user must grab the visible left part - the panel is recoverable, but the footer controls are dead until they do, which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

Screenshot: screenshots/def283-clipped-1100x760.png, screenshots/def283-clipped-900x620.png, screenshots/def283-clipped-700x560.png
Harness: e2e/retests/def283_repro.spec.cjs (1 passed, asserting the defect); log e2e/def283_repro.log

History:
- qa: opened
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying frontend-dev - a `window` `resize` listener registered only while the dialog is open re-applies the clamp to the stored offset against the live viewport and the dialog's live rect, so a shrink can no longer leave the panel outside; the clamp maths was extracted as `clampDragOffset(offset, dialogRect, viewport)` in `src/renderer/components/printDialogDrag.ts` so the resize path and the drag path share the same rule (including the inverted-range case where the panel is larger than the viewport, which pins to the min edge); `nextDragOffset` and the drag path are untouched; the listener is cleaned up on close/unmount. Evidence: new `def283_dialogResizeClamp.test.tsx` 6 tests (shrink re-clamps a previously valid offset; each edge; a sub-panel viewport pins to the min edge; a viewport grow is a no-op; the component re-clamps on a resize event; the listener is added once and removed on unmount); `npm run verify` exit 0; `build:renderer` exit 0.)
- qa: CLOSED. Rebuilt (`npm.cmd run build`, exit 0) and retested the FIXED behaviour through the canonical `launchApp`: opened `test-fixtures/report.pdf`, opened the Print dialog at 1440x900, dragged the header hard to the bottom-right (drag offset 360,32), then shrank the WINDOW without reopening. Measured `.print-dialog` rects vs the live viewport: 1100x760 -> `{left:380, top:64, right:1100, bottom:760}` offRight 0 / offBottom 0; 900x620 -> `{left:180, top:64, right:900, bottom:620}` offRight 0 / offBottom 0; 700x560 -> `{left:32, top:64, right:700, bottom:560}` offRight 0 / offBottom 0. `[data-print-confirm]` was actionable (trial click) at the baseline and at all three sizes; a recovery drag left the panel at `{left:0, top:0, right:668, bottom:496}` and still actionable. The panel is re-clamped fully inside the viewport at every shrink, so Print/Close stay reachable. Command: `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/retests/def283_repro.spec.cjs` -> 1 passed. The spec was INVERTED (not retired) into a regression guard asserting the fixed behaviour - it keeps the proven drag/shrink harness and now fails if the re-clamp regresses; the old defect-asserting form failed by design (`clippedSizes=0/3`, assertion "dialog pushed past the viewport" failed), confirming the fix. Unit guard `def283_dialogResizeClamp.test.tsx` 6 passed.

## DEF-279: Multi Mode: a Windows case-variant path defeats the same-file pane guard and the open dedupe, and a later save silently discards the other pane's saved edit

- Status: CLOSED

Steps to reproduce:

2. Copy `test-fixtures/report.pdf` (34 pages) into a temp directory as `...-p32-samefile.pdf`. The case-variant path `...-P32-SAMEFILE.PDF` names the same file on Windows (`fs.existsSync` = true). Temp copies only - never a `test-fixtures/` file.
3. Open the exact-case path through the real title-bar Open control (mocked OS dialog). Tab count 1.
4. Open the SAME file with the case-variant path.
5. Activate the first tab, click `[data-toolbar-multi-mode]` (pane A = the exact-case tab), then pick the case-variant tab into pane B from the empty pane's pick list (`[data-pane-pick]`).
6. Data-loss half: focus pane A, select page 1 in its rail section, click "Delete this page" (A 34 -> 33), Save A (Ctrl+S; file on disk = 33 pages), then Save B (Ctrl+S; file on disk = 34 pages).

Expected: Phase 32's fixed design decisions: opening a file that is already open dedupes to the existing tab, and assigning/opening the document already shown in the other pane is REFUSED with a clear message ("That file is already shown in the other pane." / "That document is already shown in the other pane."). The same document must never occupy both panes, and any path Windows treats as the same file must not bypass either rule.
Actual: both comparisons are raw string equality - the open dedupe is `t.filePath === source.path` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:1301`) and the pane guard is `otherPath !== filePath` (`paneAssignPathError`, `src/renderer/state/multiMode.ts:129`). A case-variant path bypasses both:
- The case-variant open created a SECOND tab (tabs 1 -> 2, `.toast-text` count 0), and pane B's pick list offered and accepted that tab. Both pane headers then name the same file (`...-p32-samefile.pdf` / `...-P32-SAMEFILE.PDF`, both 34 pages), pane B is not empty, and the shared rail shows two DISTINCT engine doc ids for the one on-disk file (`a9dde8ec-b95b-40b2-972b-b34c470a2b98` / `2f0017bb-30cc-4399-87a8-9d5fbfa0d516`), with no message.
- Data loss: pane A deleted page 1 and saved 33 pages to the file; pane B then saved its 34-page copy over the same path, silently discarding pane A's saved edit. On-disk page count observed: 34 -> 33 (Save A) -> 34 (Save B). The user is never warned that two panes write to one file.
Severity justification: the same document in both panes breaks a Phase 32 invariant and the save half silently discards a saved edit; no corruption of unrelated content and no crash, so MEDIUM per the orchestrator's ADV-068 disposition.

Screenshot: screenshots/adv-p32-samefile-save.png, screenshots/adv-p32-samefile-casevariantfilename.png

It is wired into BOTH halves of the open dedupe - the `tabsReducer` `open` case (`src/renderer/state/tabs.ts`, which is what actually collapses a duplicate open) and App's `dedupeTarget` lookup - AND into the pane guard (`paneAssignPathError`). ## DEF-275: A malformed `update:statusChanged` payload blanks the entire renderer and cannot be recovered without a relaunch

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-066)
- Phase: 31

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build the dev app (`npm.cmd run build`) and launch it through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen (`.sample-card`).
2. Open Help -> About by sending the real main->renderer menu payload `menu:action {action:'about'}` from the main process; wait for `[data-about-dialog]:visible`.
3. Push a malformed state over the real main->renderer channel `update:statusChanged` with `{kind:'available', version:'99.0.0', notes:[null, 123, {a:1}, 'kept string']}`.
4. Measure the blast radius: `#root` child count, `.sample-card` presence, `body.innerText`.
5. Attempt recovery: send `{kind:'checking'}` and then the About `menu:action` again.

Expected: the renderer treats the payload as untrusted at the IPC boundary - a non-string element, a non-array `notes`, or a non-primitive `version` renders as text or is ignored, and the About dialog stays mounted; at worst the incoming block shows its empty state.

Actual: all three lethal shapes throw during render and React unmounts the whole root - `#root` child count 0, `.sample-card` gone, `body.innerText` empty; the window is a blank white page. Re-sending the About action does NOT bring anything back; only a relaunch recovers.
- `notes:[null, 123, {a:1}, 'kept string']` -> React error #31 (objects are not valid as a React child); `rootKids=0`, `reopensAbout=false`.
- `notes:'just a string'` -> `n.notes.map is not a function` (AboutDialog.tsx:273); `rootKids=0`, `reopensAbout=false`.
- `version:{a:1}` -> React error #31 (AboutDialog.tsx:268); `rootKids=0`, `reopensAbout=false`.
Shapes that do NOT reproduce (controls): `notes:{note:'x'}` (no `length`) shows the incoming empty state and the dialog survives (`rootKids=1`, `reopensAbout=true`); `version:123` renders as text and the dialog survives.

5. Probe `whatsNewHistory` directly against the bundled `src/shared/whatsNew.ts` module.

Expected: the empty state is shown for a version with no changelog entry (criterion 3), and "Earlier releases" lists only releases OLDER than the running version.

Actual: with running version `1.2`, the section shows "No release notes for this version." and then "Earlier releases: v1.23.0, v1.22.0, v1.21.0" - all three are NEWER than 1.2. `whatsNewHistory` (whatsNew.ts:93) ignores the running version entirely: it returns `WHATS_NEW.slice(1)`, i.e. array positions 2..N - positional, correct only while the running version happens to be the newest entry. Harness: test-fixtures/adv-p31/empty-state-probe.cjs; module probe test-fixtures/adv-p31/module-probe.cjs.

The release gate additionally asserts `WHATS_NEW[0].version === package.json`'s version (with a constructed failure path for a newer top entry). The renderer passes `info.version` at both call sites (the typecheck break that change created is fixed). Evidence: `test/unit/main/whatsNew.test.ts` 17 passed (6 history cases incl. a mid-list running version and no-entry -> []), `aboutDialogWhatsNew.test.tsx` 16 passed, `aboutDialog.test.tsx` 35 passed; `npm run verify` exit 0; `build:renderer` exit 0.)

## DEF-274: Rotating a page blanks that page's thumbnail to white (canvas clear -> async repaint), ~0.1 s to >3 s

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: operator (2026-09-21, reported to the orchestrator)
- Phase: 2

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build the dev app (`npm.cmd run build`) and launch it through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen.
2. Open `test-fixtures/report.pdf` (34 pages) via the Open PDF button (dialog stubbed by `openSamplePath`); wait for `.page-slot[data-page="1"] canvas.pdf-page-canvas` and `.thumb-item[data-page="1"] canvas.thumb-canvas`; settle ~1.8 s.
3. Click the toolbar rotate-clockwise control `[data-toolbar-rotate-cw]` once and watch page 1's thumbnail in the left rail (and the page view).

Expected: The rotated page and its thumbnail update smoothly; the thumbnail keeps its previous frame until the new one is painted, with no blank/placeholder flash.

Actual: The page-1 thumbnail canvas is cleared to blank white and only repainted asynchronously. Measured on the dev build (2026-09-21) with a 16 ms in-page sampler (`e2e/def_rotate_flicker.spec.cjs`, log `e2e/def_rotate_flicker_final.log`), clicking `[data-toolbar-rotate-cw]` five times:
- Rotate 1 (0->90): thumb painted (ink=99) at t=16 ms; cleared to white at t=101 ms; still white at the last sample t=1637 ms.
- Rotate 2 (90->180): thumb white t=16..105 ms, repainted by t=154 ms.
- Rotate 3 (180->270): no blank captured at 16 ms cadence.
- Rotate 4 (270->0): thumb white t=83..110 ms, repainted by t=155 ms.
- Rotate 5 (0->90): the thumb canvas was still all-white 3.0 s after the click (settle read: canvas 189x244, all four sampled pixels `[255,255,255,255]`).
So it reproduces on most rotates, and the blank lasts from ~90-150 ms up to >3 s; the page's own thumbnail is the one affected (thumbs 2-4 stay painted).

Answers to the sampled questions:
(a) Page view: it does NOT go through `.page-placeholder` (constant 0) and the page canvas never read white-blank in the 16 ms sampler; instead it keeps the PRE-rotate frame for ~150 ms then swaps to the rotated frame (screenshot -2 at 146 ms still upright, -3 at 266 ms rotated). One earlier frame showed the page area fully white at ~169 ms, but that was not reproduced under the corrected probe, so the page view reads as a delayed swap rather than a page blank.
(b) Thumbnail: no `.thumb-placeholder` is shown (constant 0) - the canvas is cleared to opaque white, i.e. a blank canvas, not a placeholder.
(c) Thumbnail strip: no re-layout and no scroll - `.thumb-item[data-page="1"]` rect stayed 193x196@120 and `.thumb-scroller` scrollTop stayed 0 across every sample.
(d) Settle time: ~90-150 ms on 90->180 / 270->0, but >3 s on 0->90.
(e) Every rotate or only the first: most rotates; the 0->90 case is the longest-lived.

Selectors observed changing: `.thumb-item[data-page="1"]` gains/loses `thumb-rot-90|180|270`; `canvas.thumb-canvas` inside it is cleared to white (width/height stay 189x244); `.page-slot[data-page="1"] canvas.pdf-page-canvas` is resized (1210x1565 <-> 1565x1210) and `.page-slot[data-page="1"]` swaps size. `.thumb-placeholder` and `.page-placeholder` never appear. This is the same clear->async-repaint class as DEF-222 (Phase 18), but on the rotate path: the engine op calls `refreshDocProxyFor` which swaps the pdf.js `doc` proxy, the thumb render effect re-runs and sets `canvas.width = geom.bufferWidth` (clearing the canvas) before the async `pdfPage.render` completes.
Screenshots: screenshots/def-rotate-flicker-1.png (baseline, upright page + painted thumb 1), -2.png (146 ms: page still pre-rotate/upright), -3.png (266 ms: page rotated, thumb 1 blank white landscape), -4.png (2984 ms, no further click: thumb 1 STILL blank white). Harness: e2e/def_rotate_flicker.spec.cjs.

History:
- qa: opened
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying frontend-dev - root cause corrected: for thumbs the geometry does NOT change on rotate, so the white came from `canvas.width = geom.bufferWidth` being assigned UNCONDITIONALLY (assigning `width` clears the backing store even when the value is unchanged) while pdf.js repainted asynchronously; the old code ALSO double-rotated the thumb (pdf.js applied `/Rotate` and the wrap applied `.thumb-rot-N`), so rotated thumbs were clipped. Fix: the frame now renders into a per-run OFFSCREEN scratch canvas and only on `task.promise` resolution are the visible canvas's width/height/CSS size assigned and the frame blitted - in one task, so no paint can land on a cleared canvas; the thumb now requests `rotation: 0` and the wrap's existing `.thumb-rot-N` transform is the single rotation owner; the page view keeps its last bitmap and applies a translate+rotate transform that maps onto the new slot box, dropping it in the same task as the blit (reduced-motion / Animations-off skips the transform). The DEF-222 cleanup rule and the offscreen-slot eager release are untouched. Evidence: new `test/unit/renderer/def274_rotateSmoothSwap.test.tsx` (5 tests) plus the existing pageView/rotation/sideRail suites - 26 passed / 5 files; `npm run verify` exit 0; `build:renderer` exit 0.)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-21 FIX-READY retest on a fresh build, `npm.cmd run build` exit 0). Re-ran `e2e/def_rotate_flicker.spec.cjs` (same 16 ms in-page sampler, 5 consecutive rotates of `test-fixtures/report.pdf` page 1 via `[data-toolbar-rotate-cw]`, enhanced with the five required assertions) -> `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/def_rotate_flicker.spec.cjs` 1 passed / 0 failed (18.9 s). (1) NO blank frame: 0 blank/white thumb samples across all five rotates (101/86/99/100/101 post-click samples; thumb ink held at 99 on every sample, never 0), vs the original white at t=101 ms and still white at t=1637 ms on rotate 1 and still white at +3.0 s on rotate 5; late +2.9 s read thumb ink=124, painted. (2) Settle to correctly-oriented thumb + page: R1 34 ms, R2 40 ms, R3 32 ms, R4 35 ms, R5 34 ms, all stable to the end of sampling. (3) No double rotation / no clipping: the thumb bitmap's normalised ink box is identical on every rotate ([0.265,0.098,0.471,0.111]) and matches the un-rotated page view's box ([0.263,0.091,0.474,0.122]); aspect spread 1.0; the wrap class is the single rotation owner (`thumb-rot-90/180/270`/none/90) and agrees with the page view orientation at every step (page canvas 1565x1210 landscape at 90/270, 1210x1565 portrait at 0/180). (4) Page view: the pre-rotate frame no longer sits ~150 ms - a translate+rotate turn transform is applied at t=15-24 ms on all five rotates and the new frame is blitted (canvas dims flip) at 32-40 ms; the page canvas is painted throughout (ink 30-40, pageWhiteBlank=0) with no placeholder. (5) Screenshots `screenshots/def-rotate-flicker-fixed-1..4.png` inspected: -1 baseline upright page + painted upright thumb; -2 at rotate 90 both the page view and the thumb show the page turned (content vertical at the right), thumb painted (no white); -3 at rotate 180 the thumb shows the title upside down at the bottom of the thumb while the page content sits below the fold (correct for 180); -4 at rotate 90 after five rotates both page and thumb are correctly turned and the thumb is painted. Thumb and page view agree at every orientation. No stray processes after the run.)

Actual: the case settled after 135 ms with `{"ok":false,"reason":"Invalid deviceName provided"}` — it PASSED validation, created the hidden window and called `webContents.print`, and only failed at the bogus device. The `bad-image` check only tests `typeof !== 'string'` or `''` (so `images:[null]`, `images:['']` and `images:[42]` are rejected in <=1 ms, but any non-empty string passes). The print document then contains a broken `<img>`, so the job fails at the driver or prints blank pages, and the only signal (`success`) is not tied to the image being valid.
Screenshot: none. Harness: `test-fixtures/adv-p30-matrix.cjs`.

- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying backend-dev - `bad-image` now calls a new `isValidPageImage` that requires a `data:image/(png|jpeg|jpg|webp);base64,` URL whose payload base64-decodes AND carries a known image signature (PNG/JPEG/WEBP magic bytes). `'not-a-data-url'`, the undecodable `'data:image/png;base64,AAAA'`, wrong MIME, a missing `;base64,` and an empty payload are all rejected before any window is created. ## DEF-269: `printJob` with an empty, omitted or non-string deviceName never settles, leaks one hidden BrowserWindow per call, and keeps the app alive after the visible window closes

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: adversary (ADV-061)
- Phase: 30

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build the dev app (`npm.cmd run build`) and launch it through the canonical `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` `launchApp`; wait for the welcome screen (`.sample-card`).
2. From the renderer call `window.tflex.printJob({ images: [<1x1 PNG data URL>], settings: { deviceName: '' } })` and race it against an 8 s timeout.
3. Repeat with the `settings` key omitted entirely, with `settings: null`, and with `settings: { deviceName: 12345 }`.
4. Count `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` in the main process before, after each call, and 3 s later; inspect each window's `isDestroyed()`, `isVisible()` and `webContents.getURL()`.
5. Leak one hidden window, close the visible window with `win.close()`, wait 5 s and query the main process again.
No physical printer is targeted: the empty/omitted device resolves to the system default, which on this box is the virtual "Microsoft Print to PDF".

Expected: an empty, absent or non-string `deviceName` is rejected up front with a typed reason (`bad-device`) before any window is created, or `printJob` is bounded (timeout plus window destruction on EVERY path) so a driver that never calls back cannot leak a hidden window or keep the app alive. AGENTS.md fail-loud: no silent default-device print.

Actual: every call hangs — `{"settled":false,"result":"TIMEOUT"}` at 8 s — and each leaks one hidden window. `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` grew 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 across five calls, every leaked window `destroyed:false, visible:false` with the temp print HTML loaded (`file:///C:/Users/.../tflex-print-*.html`), and none was ever destroyed. The quit consequence is real: after one leak, closing the visible window left `appAlive=true, windows=1` — the app never quits because `window-all-closed` cannot fire while the hidden window exists. A non-string `deviceName` (12345) takes the same hanging path.
Screenshot: none (non-visual). Harnesses: `test-fixtures/adv-p30-leak.cjs`, `test-fixtures/adv-p30-quit.cjs`.

History:
- qa: opened (reproduced independently on the dev build; `node test-fixtures/adv-p30-leak.cjs` -> five TIMEOUTs, `FINAL windows 6`, all leaked windows `destroyed:false, visible:false`; `node test-fixtures/adv-p30-quit.cjs` -> `AFTER_LEAK windows 2`, `AFTER_VISIBLE_CLOSE appAlive=true windows=1`. 8 s bounded observation window; leaked windows cleaned up via `hardClose`, which destroyed all six and closed normally in 248 ms.)
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (relaying backend-dev - two parts: (1) `validatePrintPayload` now rejects a missing/empty/whitespace-only/non-string `deviceName` with the new typed reason `bad-device-name`, so no window is created for that class at all; (2) `printJob` is bounded - `PRINT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` resolves `{ ok: false, reason: 'print-timeout' }` when the driver never calls back, and a single `finally` with a `destroyOnce()` guard destroys the window exactly once on success, driver failure, timeout and thrown error, so no hidden window can outlive a job. Evidence: `test/unit/main/print.test.ts` 58 passed incl. the never-callback timeout and the destroy-exactly-once assertions; `npm run verify` exit 0.)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-21 FIX-READY retest on a fresh build, `npm.cmd run build` exit 0). `node test-fixtures/adv-p30-leak.cjs` -> all five calls settle in 1-14 ms with `{"ok":false,"reason":"bad-device-name"}` (`deviceName:""` 14 ms, no-settings 2 ms, `deviceName:12345` 1 ms, repeats 2 ms), `FINAL windows 1 events 1` (no hidden window created; `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` unchanged across calls), `closed normally in 153ms`. `node test-fixtures/adv-p30-quit.cjs` -> `AFTER_LEAK windows 1`, `AFTER_VISIBLE_CLOSE appAlive=false windows=-1` (app quit cleanly, no stray window). `node test-fixtures/adv-p30-matrix.cjs` -> `settings:null` 4 ms and `settings omitted` 0 ms both `bad-device-name`, `WINDOWS_AFTER 1`, `closed normally in 133ms`. The 120 s timeout path was not waited out; it is covered by `test/unit/main/print.test.ts` (58 passed incl. "resolves print-timeout and destroys the window exactly once when the driver never calls back"). No leaked windows or running app left behind.)

Severity LOW — the impact needs a burst of clicks within ~1ms immediately after a move; at normal speed the style applies (`realisticBoldStuck=true`).

CALLOUT ANCHOR: id unchanged, one undo restored the anchor, `at` shifted by `(27.82, 17.70)` with the box `rect` untouched, colour burst kept the moved anchor, reopen identical. ## DEF-261: `verify:full` is non-deterministically red — the DEF-098 jump test's wall-clock frame simulation outruns the 1200ms fallback window under suite load

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 29 (release gate 1.23.0)

Steps to reproduce:
1. From the repo root run `npm.cmd run verify:full` on a loaded machine (this run: vitest reported `setup 289.16s`, `environment 471.64s` for a 33.60s test run).
2. Read the failure: `test/unit/renderer/bugDEF098_jumpTargetSticky.test.tsx` > "click thumb 10 -> currentPage=10 immediately; stays 10 through the smooth scroll; settles at 10".
3. Re-run only that file on an idle machine: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/bugDEF098_jumpTargetSticky.test.tsx`.

Expected: `verify:full` is deterministically green — it is the mandatory release gate (`AGENTS.md` PUSH GATE, `.github/workflows/verify.yml`).

Actual: the gate is red. `Test Files 1 failed | 269 passed (270)`; `Tests 1 failed | 3505 passed (3506)`; `AssertionError: expected 7 to be 10 // Object.is equality` at `bugDEF098_jumpTargetSticky.test.tsx:374` (the second `await animate(h.scroller, 6, 900)` block). The isolated re-run is green: `1 passed`, `5 passed` (5.06s), including the failing case verbatim. Root cause (test fragility, not product behaviour): the helper `flushRaf` waits a real `window.setTimeout(resolve, 25)` and `animate` advances 6 frames per call, so the test simulates ~450ms of scroll while the product's DEF-058 jump lock uses a real 1200ms fallback window; under suite CPU contention the simulated frames stretch past 1200ms of wall-clock time, the fallback timer fires mid-flight, and `currentPage` is recomputed from the scroll position (7) instead of staying pinned to the click target (10). No product regression is implied: the same assertion passes in isolation, and the jump path was not touched by Phases 25-29.
Evidence: `npm.cmd run verify:full` output (1 failed / 3505 passed, 270 files); isolated `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/bugDEF098_jumpTargetSticky.test.tsx` -> 5 passed.
Screenshot: none (unit-run output is the evidence).

History:
- qa: opened (2026-09-21; 1.23.0 release gate, GATE 0 red. Not marked HIGH because the failure is test-only and does not reproduce in isolation; it blocks the release gate non-deterministically, which is why the gate sequence was stopped here.)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-21; 1.23.0 release-gate retest - fake timers + one virtual clock). Original failure condition (GATE 0 red under suite load) is gone: `npm.cmd run verify:full` green - Test Files 270 passed (270), Tests 3506 passed (3506). Focused retest of `test/unit/renderer/bugDEF098_jumpTargetSticky.test.tsx`: 3 isolated runs -> 1 passed / 5 passed each (2.90-2.97s); 1 run under load (10 concurrent busy CPU workers) -> 1 passed / 5 passed (4.06s; tests 1.71s vs 0.92s idle, so the host was measurably contended). The fragility is removed at the source: `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setTimeout","clearTimeout","requestAnimationFrame","cancelAnimationFrame"] })` puts the frame simulation, the component's rAF scroll handling and the product's real 1200ms `JUMP_LOCK_FALLBACK_MS` window on the same virtual clock, so the simulated scroll can no longer outrun the fallback window when the machine is busy. Test-only change; no product code touched. Both the isolated and loaded runs are green, matching the recorded root cause (test fragility, not product behaviour).

## DEF-260: The colour picker's pink / teal / gray swatches are silently dropped (renderer and engine named-colour sets diverge)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 28

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (canonical `launchApp`); open `assets/samples/report.pdf`.
2. Arm the Rect tool (`armAnnotationTool(win, 'rect')`) and drag a rectangle on page 1.
3. Click the rectangle to select it; the action bar shows `Confirm | [colour box] | Cancel | Delete`.
4. Click `[data-ann-color-box]`, then click the **pink** swatch (`[data-palette-built-in="pink"]`).
5. Read `window.tflexDiagnostics().engineState.annotations[0].color` and the box's `data-color-current`.
6. Repeat with `teal` and `gray`, then with `blue` (control).
7. Second symptom: arm the Rect tool, set the armed tool colour to pink via the toolbar dropdown `[data-ann-color]`, then drag a new rectangle on the page.
   Reproduced by `e2e/phase28_29_verify.spec.cjs -g C3b` (1 failed; see the `C3b-picks` / `C3b-create-pink` log lines).

Expected: each offered swatch applies to the selected annotation (Phase 28 C3: "picking a colour changes the selected annotation's colour"), and a new annotation drawn with that tool colour is created carrying it.

Actual: pink, teal and gray do nothing. Measured (page-1 rect, initial `#2563eb`): pink -> `engine #2563eb`, `box #2563eb`; teal -> `#2563eb`; gray -> `#2563eb`; blue -> `engine blue`, `box #3b82f6`. The same three colours are dropped in any click order (a 9-colour sweep in both forward and reverse order drops exactly pink/teal/gray; the other six apply). On the create path, arming pink and dragging leaves the annotation count unchanged (1 -> 1) with `activeTool: "rect"` - a silent no-op.
Root cause: the renderer palette (`src/renderer/annotations/model.ts` `ANNOTATION_COLORS`) offers yellow/orange/red/**pink**/purple/**teal**/green/blue/**gray**, but the engine's named set (`src/main/services/annotations.ts` `ANN_COLOR_RGB` / `ANN_COLORS`, mirrored by `AnnColor` in `src/shared/types.ts`) is yellow/green/blue/red/orange/purple/cyan/magenta/white. `editAnnotation` keeps the old colour when the name is unknown (`ann.color = isValidColorValue(payload.color) ? payload.color : ann.color`, annotations.ts:582) and `normalizeAnnotationPayload` throws on create, so both legs fail silently. The toolbar dropdown path is unaffected (renderer-only tool state), which is why this only surfaces on the engine-backed paths.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase28-verify-comment-box.png shows the action-bar colour box used by this repro.

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 28 C3 validation; a 9-colour sweep drops pink/teal/gray in both directions, and a pink-armed create places nothing)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-21 FIX-READY retest; `e2e/retests/def260_retest.spec.cjs`, 2 passed, 46.0s). Action-bar colour box picks: pink -> engine `pink`, box `#ec4899`; teal -> `teal` / `#14b8a6`; gray -> `gray` / `#64748b`. Full canonical 12-swatch sweep (yellow,green,blue,red,orange,purple,cyan,magenta,white,pink,teal,gray) forward AND reverse: 12/12 applied each way, 0 dropped. Create path: arming the rect tool with pink and drawing created a new rect with `color: "pink"` (count 1 -> 2; previously a silent no-op). P28 C3 re-confirmed: bar buttons `[ann-rect-confirm(587.7), colour box(651.5), ann-rect-cancel(673.5), ann-rect-delete(731.3)]`, no Edit text/button; a single click opens the picker; the toolbar dropdown (`data-ann-color`) moved the armed swatch `#2563eb -> #ec4899` while the SELECTED annotation stayed `blue`. Guard: `npm run test:unit -- test/unit/main/annotations.test.ts` 129/129 passed, including the drift guard `expect([...ANN_COLORS]).toEqual([...ANNOTATION_COLOR_NAMES])` which fails if the engine and canonical lists ever diverge. Screenshot `screenshots/def260-retest.png` shows the 12-swatch Built-in picker open over a selected blue rect.

## DEF-258: Edit-mode text-run commit silently drops character spacing (and every other Phase-21 style field)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 27

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (canonical `launchApp`); open `assets/samples/report.pdf`.
2. Click `button[aria-label="Edit content"]`, then `[data-edit-tool="text"]`.
3. Click a text run (e.g. the page-1 title `TFlex Technical Report`); the panel opens in text mode with `[data-txt-text]` showing the run's text.
4. Set `[data-txt-character-spacing]` to `6`.
5. Type into `[data-txt-text]` (append ` X`) so the Phase-26 session renders `[data-edit-run-preview]`, then blur the field to commit.
6. `Save As` and decode the saved page content stream.
   Reproduced by `e2e/phase27_fonts_spacing.spec.cjs -g C1d`.

Expected: the run preview loosens (it does: computed `letter-spacing: 11.3137px` = 6 pt x page scale) and the committed run bakes `6 Tc` into the page content stream, per Phase 27 criterion 1 ("live for ... edited text runs; ... survives save/reopen (round-trip asserted in the baked stream by the `Tc` operator)").

Actual: the run text IS committed (saved stream contains `<54466C657820546563686E6963616C205265706F72742058> Tj` = "TFlex Technical Report X") but the saved file contains NO `Tc` operator. The panel's spacing is silently discarded on commit. Root cause: `src/renderer/App.tsx` `handleEditTextRun` (lines ~2373-2381) forwards only `page`/`rect`/`newText`/`font`/`size`/`color`/`oldRect` to `engine.editTextRun`, even though `EditTextRunPayload extends TextStyleFields` and the engine emits `Tc` whenever `charSpacing` is present (proven by `e2e/phase27_fonts_spacing.spec.cjs -g C1c` and `test/unit/main/engine.test.ts` "Phase 27: character spacing (Tc)"). The same drop affects `bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`align`/`lineHeight`/`baselineShift`/`highlight`/`list`/`indent` on this path.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase27-c4-compose.png (spacing works for text boxes); the C1d run leg has no persisted artifact because the operator is dropped.

History:
- qa: opened (Phase 27 validation, C1d; preview shows 6 pt tracking but the baked stream has no `Tc`)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-21 Phase-27 close-out retest; `e2e/retests/def258_retest.spec.cjs`, 2 passed, 18.0s). Non-default leg: select the page-1 run `TFlex Technical Report` through the text tool, set char spacing 6 + bold + align right, append ` X`, blur -> the captured wire payload (recorded at the main-process `engine:editTextRun` IPC handler) is `{"page":1,"rect":{"x":183.288,"y":65.232,"width":244.224,"height":24},"newText":"TFlex Technical Report X","font":"Helvetica","size":12,"color":{"r":0,"g":0,"b":0},"align":"right","bold":true,"charSpacing":6}`; the saved page content stream carries exactly one `6 Tc` inside a BT/Tj text object and embeds `Helvetica-Bold`; after Save As + reopen the text layer shows the edited run and the file still decodes `6 Tc`. Default leg: an unstyled run commit sends the legacy minimal payload `{page,rect,newText,font,size,color}` (no style keys) and the saved streams contain 0 `Tc` operators. Phase 27 C1d now passes (8/8).

## DEF-257: A committed Edit-mode text box loses its `.edit-box` surface after Edit-mode close/reopen (unmovable)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 26

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (canonical `launchApp`); open `assets/samples/report.pdf`.
2. Click `button[aria-label="Edit content"]` (Edit mode), then `[data-edit-tool="box"]`.
3. Drag a box on page 1. The panel's `[data-txt-text]` field focuses (Phase 26).
4. Type `DEF257 BOX` into `[data-txt-text]` and blur the field to commit the session.
5. Probe `document.querySelectorAll('.edit-box').length` and `window.tflexDiagnostics().engineState.textBoxes.length` -> both 1.
6. Click `button[aria-label="Edit content"]` to close Edit mode, then click it again to re-open it; wait for `[data-edit-toolbar]`.
7. Probe the same two counts.
   Reproduced by `e2e/retests/def257_repro.spec.cjs`.

Expected: the committed box stays selectable/movable in Edit mode after the close/reopen, i.e. `.edit-box` is still rendered from the per-tab edit registry (the engine keeps the box).
Actual: `[DEF257|AFTER-REOPEN] {"editBoxes":0,"engineTextBoxes":1,"engineText":["DEF257 BOX"]}`. The engine still owns the box (visible and saved), but the renderer registry was emptied, so no `.edit-box` surface exists. Clicking the box in Edit mode hits nothing (`hitTextBox` misses) and starts a NEW drag-to-create instead of selecting/moving the existing box. Root cause: `DocumentView`'s text-target-change effect runs `delete-text-box` for a target with `isNew === true`; the Phase-26 `isNew` flag is never cleared when the session commits a new box (`commitTextSession` -> `onCommitTextBox`), so closing Edit mode drops the committed box from `edit.textBoxes`.
Evidence: `[DEF257|BEFORE] {"editBoxes":1,"engineTextBoxes":1}` -> `[DEF257|AFTER-REOPEN] {"editBoxes":0,"engineTextBoxes":1}`. Content is not lost (engine + save intact), hence MEDIUM not HIGH.
Screenshot: none (DOM/engine counts are the evidence; `npx playwright test e2e/retests/def257_repro.spec.cjs`).

History:
- qa: opened (2026-09-20; Phase-26 validation, repointed phase21 C4 back-to-text step surfaced it)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-20 retest; `e2e/retests/def257_repro.spec.cjs`, 1 passed, 12.3s). Place/type/commit -> `[DEF257|BEFORE] {"editBoxes":1,"engineTextBoxes":1,"id":"d543dbe6-...","left":590.2}`. Isolation probe (tool off/on while Edit stays open, so the reopen rehydration cannot mask a dropped mirror): `[DEF257|AFTER-TOGGLE] {"editBoxes":1,"engineTextBoxes":1}` — the committed box is no longer treated as an abandoned placement. Close/reopen: `[DEF257|AFTER-REOPEN] {"editBoxes":0,"engineTextBoxes":1,"boxToolPressed":"false"}` (tool reset to "off" by design). Re-arm `[data-edit-tool="box"]`: `[DEF257|AFTER-ARM] {"editBoxes":1,"ids":["d543dbe6-..."],"engineIds":["d543dbe6-..."]}` — exactly one surface, same id. Select: `[DEF257|AFTER-SELECT] {"editBoxes":1,"toolbar":1,"selected":1}` — click selects, no new box. Move: `[DEF257|AFTER-MOVE] left 590.2 -> 650.2px (+60), engineRect.x 183.6 -> 215.4pt (+31.8)`. Save As -> reopen: `[DEF257|REOPENED] {"engineTextBoxes":1,"texts":["DEF257 BOX"]}`. `[DEF257|CONSOLE-DELETE-LINES] []` — no `delete-text-box`/abandoned log. Design nuance: reopening Edit mode resets the per-tab tool to "off" intentionally (a stray text tool must not leak into the next session), so the box needs a re-arm before its `.edit-box` surface renders.

## DEF-254: Selecting an annotation on a page other than 1 closes the text-properties panel when a neighbouring page mounts

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 24

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (canonical `launchDev`), open `test-fixtures/annot-text-roundtrip-1727.pdf` (a multi-page PDF with a textbox annotation on page 4).
2. Scroll to page 4.
3. Single-click the committed `VERIFY TB 1727` textbox.
4. (Also reproduces via `e2e/phase24_annotation_styles.spec.cjs` C3, which uses the same fixture and a real `win.mouse.click`.)

Expected: the text-properties panel opens and stays open, reflecting the annotation's stored style (Phase-24 criteria 1/2/3).
Actual: the panel opens, then closes ~350ms later. rAF probe (`e2e/retests/diag_phase24_failures.spec.cjs`, C3): t=6 `panel=true open="true"` `activePages=["4"]` `layerPages=["2","3","4"]`; t=104 `open="false"` and `layerPages=["3","4","5"]` (page 2 unmounted, page 5 mounted during the panel's 248px reflow); t=323 `panel=false`. The real-mouse spec shows the same: panel true at t=17ms, false at t=363ms. Root cause: every mounted page's `AnnotationOverlay` reports `onSelectAnnotation(selectedAnn)` from its effect (`AnnotationOverlay.tsx:473-475`); a page overlay that mounts during the reflow reports `null`, clobbering the host's single `selectedAnn`, so `selectedAnnText` flips false and the panel closes. Page 1 selection is unaffected because no new page mounts.
Screenshot: screenshots/diag-c3-page4.png, screenshots/phase24-c3-legacy.png

- qa: opened (2026-09-20; Phase-24 re-verification; `e2e/phase24_annotation_styles.spec.cjs` C3 fails 2/4)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-20 Phase-24 close-out retest; `e2e/retests/def_254_255_retest.spec.cjs`). Stated repro passes: a real `win.mouse.click` on the page-4 legacy textbox held the panel open for all 96 rAF frames with 0 `panel=false` frames after open (panel true from t=17ms, active page ["4"], mode annotation) while a neighbouring page mounted/unmounted in the same window (layerPages changed from ["2","3","4"]); a blank click on page 4 still closed the panel and deselected (panel=false, active=false). Phase-24 spec C3 now passes.

## DEF-252: Placing an annotation text box/comment glitches the page and the follow-up click on it does not register

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 21

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (canonical `launchApp`), open `report.pdf`.
2. Arm the annotation Text box tool (or Callout / Note) - the text-properties panel opens.
3. Place the annotation on page 1 and click its Confirm.
4. Immediately single-click the placed annotation.

Expected: the text-properties panel stays open, the page does not move, and the click on the just-placed annotation selects/keeps it selected.
Actual (pre-fix): the one-shot tool disarmed in the same cycle as the commit, `textPanelOpen` dropped false, the panel's 248px exit transition reflowed the page canvas, and the user's follow-up click on the placed annotation landed on a transitional coordinate - the screen "glitched for a bit" and the click did not register. Root cause (orchestrator, code): `textPanelOpen = ... || annTextToolArmed || selectedAnnText`; the disarm dropped the armed branch while the not-yet-echoed annotation left `selectedAnnText` false for a frame.
Screenshot: screenshots/def252-no-glitch.png

## DEF-250: The CI verify workflow fails on every push - `test/unit/main/ocr.test.ts` asserts a font-dependent tesseract outcome

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 22

Steps to reproduce:
1. Push any commit to origin (or open a PR) - the `verify` workflow runs on `windows-latest`, Node 24, `npm ci`, then one `npm run verify:full` step.
2. Read the failing job log.

Expected: `verify:full` is green on the runner (the workflow is the release gate; a red run blocks every push and emails the operator).
Actual: the run fails on exactly one test - `test/unit/main/ocr.test.ts` - with `AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0` at `ocr.test.ts:431` (the old `expect(suspects.value.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` in the tesseract integration case). git-agent's diagnosis: the failure is byte-identical on 1.15.0 / 1.19.0 / 1.20.0, so it is not a regression from any recent change; the runner's system fonts make tesseract read the synthetic "TFLEX OCR WORKS" raster confidently (zero words below the 60 threshold), while the same test passes locally where the font rasterises differently. The assertion depended on the runner's font, not on TFlex behaviour.
Evidence: git-agent CI diagnosis (one failing test, identical across three versions, `ocr.test.ts:431`); workflow `.github/workflows/verify.yml` (windows-latest, Node 24, `npm ci`, single `verify:full` step).

History:
- qa: opened (2026-09-20; CI failure reported by the operator via the workflow email)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-20 FIX-READY retest; `test/unit/main/ocr.test.ts` no longer asserts the font-dependent count). `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/ocr.test.ts` -> 21 tests, 1 file, 21 passed. The old `expect(suspects.value.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` is replaced by `expect(Array.isArray(...)).toBe(true)` + the per-suspect below-threshold invariant, so the tesseract integration case asserts only structural properties; the mapping contract now runs deterministically in `EngineService.ocrSuspects — controlled recognition (deterministic)` from a stubbed tesseract-shaped word list (42/59 -> suspects; 60/95 -> not; 0/30 all suspects; 99 none) driving the full engine path (ocrRecognize -> ocrSuspects -> undo). Negative control (read, not edited): an inverted comparison would make `expect(suspects.value.length).toBe(2)` + `toEqual(['TELEX','CLEAR'])` + `not.toContain('EXACT'/'SHARP')` fail (the inverted filter yields ['EXACT','SHARP']). CAVEAT: CI green can only be proven by the next push - the operator will see the failure email stop.

## DEF-243: Ctrl+Shift+S saves in place instead of opening Save As

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 22

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (canonical `launchApp`); open a writable PDF (a temp copy of `report.pdf` via the mocked Open dialog).

3. Press Ctrl+Shift+S.

Actual: no Save As dialog opens. The renderer's global keydown handler (src/renderer/App.tsx:6259-6265) matches `e.key === 's'` with Ctrl but does NOT exclude Shift, so it calls `onSave` and `preventDefault()`; the document is silently saved IN PLACE over the source file (toast "Saved <file>.") and Save returns to the disabled/clean state. The app-menu popover item "Save As... Ctrl+Shift+S" DOES open the dialog, so only the keyboard accelerator is broken. Diagnostic: `[diag|after Ctrl+Shift+S] {"dialog":false,"saveDisabled":true,"saveTitle":"Saved — no changes to save","toast":["Saved 1789824453281-report.pdf."]}` vs `[diag|after menu Save As] {"dialog":true,"saveDisabled":true}`.
Screenshot: screenshots/phase22-diag-saveas.png

History:
- qa: opened (2026-09-19, Phase-22 validation). HIGH - breaks Phase 22 criterion 3 and a user asking to save a COPY silently overwrites the original. Minimal fix: add `!e.shiftKey` to the Ctrl+S branch (mirroring the Ctrl+Z branch's guard) so the native menu accelerator handles Ctrl+Shift+S.
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-20 FIX-READY retest; `e2e/retests/def_243_246_retest.spec.cjs` DEF-243a/243b, 6/6 suite pass). Ctrl+S on a 33028-byte copy of `report.pdf`: source size 33028 -> 23795, mtime 1789550984915 -> 1789831160308 (in-place write), Save returns disabled with "Saved — no changes to save". Ctrl+Shift+S on a fresh 33028-byte copy: `[data-save-as-dialog]` opened, confirm wrote the copy (23795 bytes) at the mocked path, and the source was byte/mtime-identical (size 33028, mtime 1789550984915 before AND after) - no in-place overwrite. Screenshot screenshots/def243-saveas-dialog.png.

## DEF-224: The image placement's SE resize handle is half-clipped so only its inner quadrant is draggable

- Status: CLOSED

- Found by: qa (class sweep, 2026-09-18)

Steps to reproduce:

3. Drag a rect just below a text line; pick `test-fixtures/red.png` in the file chooser. The placement commits.
4. Click the `.edit-image-placement` body to select it; the four corner handles (`.edit-image-handle-se` etc.) mount at -5px outside the box.
5. Probe with `elementFromPoint` at the SE handle's OUTER corner quadrant (~3px outside the placement's SE corner, i.e. `placement.right + 3, placement.bottom + 3`).
6. Drag from that outer quadrant by +70/+50 and release.

Expected: The SE handle is fully hit-testable - `elementFromPoint` at the outer corner quadrant returns `.edit-image-handle-se` (not the placement or the page host) - and a drag from that outer quadrant resizes the placement and commits to the engine.

Actual: Pre-fix (1.18.0 tree), `.edit-image-placement` carried `overflow: hidden`; the handle is 10x10 at `right:-5px; bottom:-5px`, so its outer 5x5 half was clipped and the outer-corner point hit-tested to the host div - only the inner quadrant was draggable. Fix (source-verified, `src/renderer/styles.css:7034-7066`): the placement no longer clips (`overflow: hidden` removed; `.edit-image-placement-img` rounds its own corners instead). Post-fix verification on the INSTALLED 1.18.1 build (spec `e2e/release_1_18_1_installed.spec.cjs`, test 5): outer-corner `elementFromPoint` returned class `"edit-image-handle edit-image-handle-se"` (`isHandle=true`); drag from that outer quadrant grew the overlay 509x40 -> 579x90 and the resize committed - the saved/reopened file carries the image at the new rect (dark 52,110).
Screenshot: screenshots/release-1181-handle.png (SE handle fully visible, protruding outside the placement corner)

History:
- qa: opened (found in the class sweep 2026-09-18; pre-fix outer-corner `elementFromPoint` returned the host div, not `.edit-image-handle-se` - the placement's `overflow: hidden` clipped the handle's outer half. LOW - only the inner quadrant of the SE handle was draggable; resize still worked from there.)
- qa: CLOSED (verified on the installed 1.18.1 build - outer-corner `elementFromPoint` returned `.edit-image-handle-se` (`isHandle=true`); drag from the outer quadrant grew the overlay 509x40 -> 579x90 and the resize committed; reopened file image at the new rect dark 52,110. Spec `e2e/release_1_18_1_installed.spec.cjs` test 5, 5/5 passed.)

## DEF-223: Moving an image placement in Edit mode is a silent no-op - the saved PDF keeps the image at its original rect

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 18

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (dev build via the canonical `launchApp` helper, no executablePath). Open the bundled report.pdf sample; scroll to page 2 (dense paragraph).
2. Arm Edit mode (`[data-toolbar-edit-toggle]`) -> click `[data-edit-tool="image"]`.
3. Drag a rect on the page just below a text line; pick `test-fixtures/red.png` in the file chooser. The image placement appears and its engine op commits.
4. Drag the `.edit-image-placement` body +110/+90 CSS px; release. The overlay moves.
5. Inspect the OLD and TARGET rects, then Save As to a temp path, close the tab, reopen the saved file and inspect both rects again.

Expected: The image relocates to the dragged position; the old rect is masked and the target rect carries the image, in the live canvas and in the saved/reopened file (the same contract the text-run and text-box move paths meet).

Actual: The overlay moves but the engine never receives the move. Measured on the dev build (2026-09-18), spec `e2e/class_sweep_def221_222.spec.cjs` (test A1c), fixed canvas-px rects:
- DOM overlay: `.edit-image-placement` before `{x:380,y:608.4,w:509,h:40}` -> after `{x:490,y:698.4,w:509,h:40}` (the drag is recognised and the mirror moves).
- Engine/proxy: MutationObserver on all 34 `.thumb-canvas` across the drag = 0 mutations; no toast. The doc proxy is never rebuilt, i.e. no engine op fired.
- Reopen: Save As -> close -> reopen. OLD rect dark 4,914 -> 4,914 (live) -> **20,360** (reopened = the full red image is still at the original rect); TARGET rect dark 2,967 -> 2,967 -> 2,967 (underlying text unchanged, no image). The move is lost from the saved file.
- Band ABOVE the image is byte-stable (4,193 -> 4,193 -> 4,193), so this is not the DEF-221 mask-anchor class.
Mechanism (source-verified, `src/renderer/edit/EditOverlay.tsx`): the image-move branch resolves `placement = placementsForPage.find(...)` (line 835) and `placementNow = edit.placements.find(...)` (line 838) - both are the CURRENT placements after the drag - then early-returns on `rectsClose(newRect, placement.rect)` (line 841), which compares the new rect with itself. `onCommitImageEdit` is never called. The resize branch (lines 854-860) has the identical self-comparison; resize was not measured in this sweep.
Screenshot: screenshots/class-sweep-a1c-after.png (overlay moved down), screenshots/class-sweep-a1c-reopen.png (reopened file has the image back at the original rect)

History:
- qa: opened (2026-09-18; Class-sweep pre-1.18.1. A1c image-move path: overlay moves, engine gets no op (0 thumb mutations), reopened file keeps the image at the old rect (20,360 dark) and leaves the target empty (2,967). Band above stable, so not Class A. Source: EditOverlay.tsx:835-841 self-compares the placement rect and returns before committing. HIGH - the user's move is silently lost on save.)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-18 retest, post-fix `EditOverlay.tsx` imageDrag.startRect). Spec `e2e/class_sweep_def221_222.spec.cjs` B1/B2 (+ A1c) all pass. MOVE: overlay mirror `{x:380,y:608.4}` -> `{x:490,y:698.4}` (+110/+90); old rect dark 4,914 -> 4,914 (live, canvas is the pre-edit render by design) -> 0 (reopened, nearWhite=20,360/20,360 = fully white); target 2,967 -> 2,967 -> 20,360 (image); band above 4,193 stable; frame strips around the old rect byte-identical to before (hashes equal), so the white mask is exactly the old rect - no padding, no neighbour erasure. RESIZE (SE handle +70/+50): overlay 509x40 -> 579x90; reopened old 20,360 (image), new 52,110 (image), region beyond the new rect unchanged 71->71; above 4,193 stable. Flash: 0 thumb width/height-zero mutations, 0 zero-width/zero-painted main-canvas frames on both commits. Screenshots: screenshots/def-223-retest-{before,after,reopen}.png. Class A INCONCLUSIVE from the pre-1.18.1 sweep is now resolved: editImage's mask is clean (old rect only). Note: image placements have no live proxy refresh (the DOM overlay is the live surface; the canvas shows the edit after save/reopen) - pre-existing behaviour, not a move failure.)

## DEF-221: Moving a text run in Edit mode leaves an empty box at the original location after Confirm

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa (operator-reported)
- Phase: 18

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (dev build via the canonical `launchApp` helper, no executablePath). Open the bundled report.pdf sample from the welcome card; scroll to page 1.
2. Arm Edit mode (`[data-toolbar-edit-toggle]`) -> `.edit-toolbar` mounts; click `[data-edit-tool="text"]`.
3. Double-click a body text run on page 1; the inline editor opens (`.edit-inline-editor[data-edit-editor="edit"]`) pre-filled with "A study in PDF orchestration and performance.".
4. Drag the editor grip `[data-edit-drag-handle]` ~+150/+120 so `[data-edit-confirm]` flips to "true"; click `[data-edit-confirm="true"]`.
5. Inspect the run's ORIGINAL location, then Save As to a temp path, close the tab, reopen the saved file and inspect it again.

Expected: The run relocates to the new position and the original location is clean - no residual white box and no erased neighbouring content. A plain in-place edit (no move) must leave no leftover.

Actual: After Confirm the ORIGINAL run location is left as a pure-white rectangular mask. Measured on the dev build (2026-09-18), spec `e2e/def221_222_leftover_thumb_flicker.spec.cjs`:
- DOM probe ~1.2s after Confirm: every candidate overlay is GONE - `[data-edit-box-eraser]` exists=false, `.edit-textrun-selection`=false, `.edit-text-hover`=false, `.edit-box`=false, `.edit-inline-editor`=false. (Pre-Confirm the eraser sat at the original rect {x:546,y:483,w:549,h:26}, computed background rgb(255,255,255), border `0px none`, opacity 1 - it can paint, but it unmounts correctly.) So the leftover is NOT a renderer overlay.
- Page-1 canvas pixel probe at the ORIGINAL run rect (fixed canvas px [302,290,548,26], immune to the post-edit layout shift caused by the "Undo last change" strip): BEFORE meanRGB [204,204,204], near-white 9,791/14,248, dark-glyph 2,867; AFTER meanRGB [255,255,255], near-white 14,248/14,248, dark-glyph 0. Uniformly white where glyph pixels were -> a white patch.
- Dense-paragraph probe (page 2, run "orchestration layer correctly handles multiple page streams. Strategic orchestration is" at y=551.7): BEFORE run-band dark 4,458 and the band immediately ABOVE the run dark 3,287; AFTER run-band dark 0 AND above-band dark 0. The mask is taller than the run (it extends up by the new text's font ascent) and erases the line above as well - the white box is punched through the paragraph.
- BAKED vs RENDERER: Save As -> close tab -> reopen the saved file. The original location is STILL uniformly white (fixed-px meanRGB [255,255,255], near-white 14,248/14,248, dark 0) and no DOM overlay exists. The white box is BAKED into the PDF (baked=true).
Mechanism: `engine.editTextRun` with the DEF-151 `oldRect` (src/main/services/engine.ts:1772-1816) draws a white rectangle (`drawRectangle`, fill rgb(1,1,1), no border) at `maskRect = payload.oldRect`, padded by the new text's font ascent/descent + PAD=2. That white mask is the "empty box"; it is part of the re-serialized PDF bytes, so it survives save+reopen. The renderer's `.edit-box-eraser` is only a transient cover and unmounts after the proxy refresh.
Screenshot: screenshots/def-221-before.png (run present before the move), screenshots/def-221-leftover-box.png (original location pure white after Confirm), screenshots/def-221-leftover-box-reopened.png (still white in the reopened saved file), screenshots/def-221-dense-after.png (white gap + neighbouring line partially erased on a dense paragraph)

## DEF-222: The thumbnail panel flickers when a text-run edit is confirmed

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: qa (operator-reported)
- Phase: 18

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (dev build via `launchApp`); open report.pdf; scroll to page 1.
2. Arm Edit mode (`[data-toolbar-edit-toggle]`) -> click `[data-edit-tool="text"]`.
3. Double-click a body text run; drag `[data-edit-drag-handle]` +150/+120 (so `[data-edit-confirm]`="true"); click `[data-edit-confirm="true"]` and watch the thumbnail panel.

Expected: The thumbnails update without a visible blank/flash.

Actual: Confirming the edit blanks and repaints every rendered thumbnail. Measured on the dev build (2026-09-18), same spec:
- MutationObserver on all 34 mounted `.thumb-canvas` nodes: at t=116ms after the Confirm click the 5 RENDERED canvases (idx 0..4) had `width=0` AND `height=0` set (bitmap released), then restored to `width=189`/`height=244` at t=119ms - one wave, 20 attribute mutations (5 zero-width + 5 zero-height + 5 restores). The rAF poll independently saw the page-1 thumb canvas at `width=0` for ~1 frame (189->0@116ms, 0->189@131ms).
- Node identity is unchanged: 34 `.thumb-canvas` nodes before and after, 34/34 the SAME nodes, 0 replaced, and `.thumb-placeholder` stays constant at 29 (no placeholder appears). So the flicker is a canvas clear->async repaint on the SAME nodes, not an unmount->placeholder.
- The 5-shot screenshot burst of `.thumb-scroller` at ~200ms cadence (screenshots/def-222-thumb-0..4.png) is identical in all 5 - the flash lasts ~3ms (blank) to ~15ms (observed), shorter than the cadence.
Mechanism: `ThumbCanvas`'s effect (src/renderer/components/SideRail.tsx:913-992) depends on `[shouldRender, doc, page, width]`. When the edit commit calls `refreshDocProxyFor` and swaps the pdf.js `doc` proxy, the effect cleanup sets `canvas.width=0; canvas.height=0` (lines 987-990) to release the bitmap, and the new effect only repaints after `await doc.getPage(page)` resolves - so every rendered thumbnail is blank in between. It fires ONCE, coinciding with the proxy rebuild.
Screenshot: screenshots/def-222-thumb-0.png .. def-222-thumb-4.png (5-shot burst, no visible blank at that cadence)

History:
- qa: opened (2026-09-18; operator-reported. Dev-build repro via e2e/def221_222_leftover_thumb_flicker.spec.cjs. MutationObserver: all 5 rendered `.thumb-canvas` zeroed at t=116ms, restored t=119ms; same nodes, no placeholder. Transient blank/repaint of the thumbnail canvases when `refreshDocProxyFor` swaps the doc proxy. LOW - cosmetic, no document change, ~3-15ms.)
- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-18; FIX-READY retest passed via e2e/def221_222_leftover_thumb_flicker.spec.cjs, dev build. MutationObserver on all 34 `.thumb-canvas` during Confirm: zeroWidthSets 0, zeroHeightSets 0 (previously 5 zero-width + 5 zero-height + restores = 20 mutations; now 10 mutations, all non-zero restore sets width=189/height=244 at t=113-114ms). rAF probe (136 frames): zeroW 0, width constant 189, clearedFrames 0, minOp 1600/1600 -> the page-1 canvas is never zeroed or blanked in any sampled frame. Node identity 34/34 same, 0 replaced, `.thumb-placeholder` constant 29. True unmount: closing the tab removes every thumb canvas (remaining 0); the explicit width/height zeroing record was not captured across the unmount (the canvas ref detaches before passive cleanup) but with the nodes gone no backing store is retained. Flash not capturable; def-222-retest.png shows all thumbnails painted. Screenshots: def-222-retest.png, def-222-thumb-0..4.png.)

## DEF-220: Tiled watermarks scale superlinearly - 100 tiled stamps cost ~101 s of blocked IPC and a ~50 MiB file

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-044)
- Phase: 18

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (dev build via the canonical launchApp helper).
2. Open the 34-page sample report.pdf (source file 33,028 bytes).
3. Apply 100 tiled text watermarks through the engine API: `window.tflex.engine.addWatermark(docId, {type:'text', text:'WM<i>', size:24, tile:true})` for i=0..99, then `getWatermarks` and `saveAs`. Harness: `node test-fixtures/tools/adv041_perf.cjs 100 24 1` (control: `node test-fixtures/tools/adv041_perf.cjs 10 24 1`).

Expected: A document has a bounded number of watermarks and a bounded placement count, with a typed limit error instead of an unbounded op; file-size growth stays proportional.
Actual: Reproduced on the current tree (2026-09-18). No watermark-count cap and no placement cap: all 100 `addWatermark` calls return `ok` (0 failures), 3,400 (watermark,page) content streams. Measured:
- 10 tiled @24 pt: apply 1,032 ms, save 241 ms, saved file 6,039,275 bytes (~5.8 MiB).
- 100 tiled @24 pt: apply 100,587 ms (checkpoints: 10 -> 1,081 ms, 20 -> 3,947 ms, 30 -> 8,842 ms, 40 -> 15,762 ms, 50 -> 24,731 ms, 60 -> 35,499 ms, 70 -> 48,596 ms, 80 -> 64,238 ms, 90 -> 81,638 ms, 100 -> 100,586 ms - clearly superlinear as each addWatermark re-scans prior marker streams), getWatermarks 33 ms, save 2,173 ms, saved file 52,239,404 bytes (~49.8 MiB, ~1,582x the 33,028-byte source).

## DEF-218: A provided-but-invalid watermark page range is silently dropped, so the watermark is applied to every page

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-042)
- Phase: 18

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex; load the 34-page sample report.pdf into a fresh engine document.
2. For each value below, call `window.tflex.engine.addWatermark(docId, {type:'text', text:'RG', range:<value>})` (fresh document per case): [0,0], [3,2], [1.5,3], ["1",2], [1,2,3], [NaN,2], [-5,-1], plus controls [1,9999] (out-of-bounds), [1,1] and [5,6] (valid). Harness: `node test-fixtures/tools/adv041_wm_api.cjs ranges`.

Expected: A range that is present but invalid (start < 1, inverted, non-integer, non-numeric, NaN, wrong length) must reject the payload with a typed engine-error, so the caller does not silently get a different scope than requested.
Actual: Reproduced on the current tree (2026-09-18). Every malformed range is silently dropped by `normalizeWatermarkSettings` (fallback `[1, 34]`) and the watermark is baked irreversibly onto all 34 pages, returning `ok` each time (document marked modified, getWatermarks pages = 1..34):
- `[0,0]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `[3,2]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `[1.5,3]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `["1",2]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `[1,2,3]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `[NaN,2]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `[-5,-1]` -> ok, pages 1..34
- `[1,9999]` -> rejected `out-of-range` ("addWatermark: range [1,9999] out of bounds for 34 pages") - the only check that fires
- `[1,1]` -> ok, page 1; `[5,6]` -> ok, pages 5-6 (valid controls)
Screenshot: N/A

- qa: CLOSED (2026-09-18; retest - `node test-fixtures/tools/adv041_wm_api.cjs ranges`: [0,0], [3,2], [1.5,3], ["1",2], [1,2,3], [NaN,2], [-5,-1] each return typed engine-error "addWatermark: settings are invalid" with applied:false and 0 watermarks (nothing stamped); [1,9999] still returns the separate out-of-range error "addWatermark: range [1,9999] out of bounds for 34 pages"; valid controls honour exactly their pages - [1,1] -> pages [1], [5,6] -> pages [5,6].)
- backend-dev: FIX-READY (2026-09-18; covered by the same validation-contract fix as DEF-217 - a present-but-invalid `range` now rejects the whole payload instead of being dropped, so a mistyped range can no longer silently stamp every page.
