Root cause: `src/renderer/edit/EditOverlay.tsx` `TextBoxView` renders only the box surface + resize handles (no `.edit-box-toolbar`). Only `PlacementToolbar` (the image tool) provides a Delete/Remove button; the box tool has no action bar wired to remove a committed box from the registry / engine.
History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth on installed v1.7.10; box selected => `selected:true`, no `.edit-box-toolbar` / delete button in the box chrome).
- qa: retested on installed v1.7.11 (FileVersion 1.7.11, exe 05:42 newer than all src). Clicking Delete removes the box: the rendered `.edit-box` for that id count = 0 AND the engine registry `EngineState.textBoxes` no longer holds it. Text boxes are an engine-side placement registry (addTextBox / moveTextBox / deleteTextBox + `EngineState.textBoxes`). Screenshots screenshots/def-136-box-toolbar-delete-edit.png, def-136-after-delete.png. CLOSED.

## DEF-135: Moving an Add-box text box that covered text erases that text (white-mask artifact)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14 (v1.7.10)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.10 binary = 0dab4cb source).
2. Open report.pdf, toggle Edit (toolbar "Edit content"), choose "Add box".
3. Drag a rectangle directly over the title run "TFlex Technical Report"; type "MY BOX"; Ctrl+Enter to commit.
4. Drag the box body (e.g. 120px right / 120px down) to move it to a new spot.

Expected: Moving a text box moves the box (and its text) to the new spot, leaving the page content it covered intact.
Actual: The box moves, but the area where the box originally sat is permanently masked with a white rectangle — the title "TFlex Technical Report" is visually erased (blank) even after the box moves away. The string stays in the pdf.js textLayer (so it remains selectable in the DOM), but the painted page no longer shows it. Screenshot: screenshots/def-137-after-move.png (title gone where the box was; "MY BOX" sits at the new spot).
Root cause: `EditOverlay.tsx` `onPointerUp` textBoxMove path -> `onCommitTextBoxMove` -> the host re-bakes the box through the engine's `editImage` mask-and-draw contract (white `drawRectangle` over `oldRect`), which erases whatever content was under the box's ORIGINAL rect. This is the same mask-and-draw limitation as DEF-116/124 (mask, don't strip) now surfaced when moving a box over real content — content under a moved box's old position is lost from the visible page.
History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth on installed v1.7.10; box placed over the title, moved 120px, title area masked/erased).
- qa: retested on installed v1.7.11 (FileVersion 1.7.11, exe 05:42 newer than all src). Place an Add-box directly over the title "TFlex Technical Report", commit ("MY BOX"), then drag the box 120px right / 120px down. The title REGION of the page-1 canvas keeps dark-fraction 0.2178 BOTH before and after the move (pixel-identical — NO white-mask artifact), and the "TFlex Technical Report" span stays in the textLayer; the title is visibly intact. Text boxes are now an engine-side placement registry (addTextBox pushes a `TextBoxModel`, no pdfDoc mutation; moveTextBox updates the rect; drawn ONCE at the FINAL rect at save), so moving a box never masks the content under its old rect. Save + re-parse with pdf-lib: valid 34-page PDF. Screenshot screenshots/def-135-after-move.png. CLOSED.

Expected: The signature keeps the dragged position (the move is applied live); a click should not discard an in-progress move.
Actual: The click reverts the placement back to its PREVIOUS (committed) position — left 200 / top 200 — and the drag result is lost. The new position is not applied; the user must click Confirm, but any incidental click on the placement discards the move. Screenshots: screenshots/def-135-after-drag.png (moved to 320,260) and screenshots/def-135-after-click.png (reverted to 200,200).
Root cause: `SignaturesOverlay.tsx` `onPointerDownPlacement` calls `setPendingMoveRect(null)` at the very top (line ~219) on EVERY new pointerdown on a placement, including a plain click. That clears the held (uncommitted) `pendingMoveRect` before the drag/commit can happen, so the placement re-renders at the committed `p.rect` and the move is discarded.
History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth on installed v1.7.10; placement rect 200,200 -> drag -> 320,260 -> click -> 200,200).
- qa: retested on installed v1.7.11 (FileVersion 1.7.11, exe 05:42 newer than all src). Place a typed signature at rect 200,200 and Confirm. Drag 120px right / 60px down -> the placement rect becomes 320,260 (the move is applied LIVE, visible before confirm). Click the placement WITHOUT pressing Confirm -> rect STAYS 320,260 (no revert; dxFromInitial=120). Click Confirm -> the new position 320,260 is committed. Root cause fixed: `onPointerDownPlacement` no longer clears a held `pendingMoveRect` that belongs to the SAME placement (the `SIG_CLICK_TOLERANCE_PX` = 4 click path preserves it), so a post-drag click no longer snaps the signature back. Screenshots screenshots/def-134-after-drag.png, def-134-after-click-no-revert.png, def-134-after-confirm-commit.png. CLOSED.

## DEF-133: After inserting a blank page, drawing an annotation on pages 2/3 silently places it on the wrong page

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14 (v1.7.10)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.10 binary = 0dab4cb source).
2. Open report.pdf (34 pages), Tools palette -> "Insert pages", blank mode, "Insert at page" = 2, Insert (pageCount 34 -> 35).
3. Scroll to the visible page 2 (the new blank) and confirm the page order is correct: engineState.pageOrder becomes [0,34,1,2,...] — the new blank IS page 2. (The page-order claim does NOT reproduce; see note.)
4. Arm the Pen (annotation toolbar "Pen" / data-tool="ink") and draw a stroke on visible page 2; then draw a Rectangle on visible page 3.

Expected: The ink stroke / rectangle appears on the page the user drew on (visible pages 2 and 3).
Actual: No annotation appears on the page that was drawn on. The engine state records 1 annotation (`engineState.annotations.length === 1`), and the stroke actually renders on the LAST visible page (page 35) — a pen stroke drawn on visible page 2 lands on visible page 35; a rect drawn on visible page 3 lands on page 2. The user's mark is silently placed at the wrong position in the document. Screenshot: screenshots/def-133-pen-misplaced.png (ink drawn on page 2; appears on page 35).
Root cause: `DocumentView.tsx` renders `<PageView pageNumber={sourcePage} ...>` where `sourcePage = visibleToSourcePage(visiblePage, engineState.pageOrder)` (the pdf.js SOURCE page, origIdx+1). `PageView.tsx` passes `page={pageNumber}` (the source page) to `<AnnotationOverlay>`, which stamps the created annotation's `page = sourcePage`. The engine's `annotations.createAnnotation` (`src/main/services/annotations.ts:246`) treats `payload.page` as the VISIBLE page and computes `origIdx = order[visiblePage - 1]`. After a reorder these differ (visible page 2 -> source page 35 / origIdx 34), so the annotation is stored on the WRONG origIdx and rendered on the wrong visible page.
NOTE: The report's "LAST page gets moved to position 2 and the NEW page lands at position 3" page-order claim is NOT reproduced — `pageOrder[1]` === 34 (the new blank), i.e. the blank correctly becomes page 2 and the original last page stays at the end. The defect is the annotation page-number mismatch, which makes drawing tools appear broken on pages 2/3.
History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth on installed v1.7.10; page order correct, but ink on visible page 2 -> page 35, engine annotations = 1).
- qa: retested on installed v1.7.11 (FileVersion 1.7.11, exe 05:42 newer than all src). Insert blank at position 2 -> pageCount 34->35, pageOrder [0,34,1,2,...], the new blank IS visible page 2, unique 35 (insert-blank regression clean, no duplicate). Arm the Pen and draw a stroke on VISIBLE page 2; arm the Rectangle and draw on VISIBLE page 3: engine annotations = [{kind:ink,page:2},{kind:rect,page:3}] — the pen lands on visible page 2 and the rectangle on visible page 3 (was page 35 / page 2). Committed ink is rendered on the visible page-2 slot. Root cause fixed: PageView now threads BOTH `page` (the VISIBLE index, used by every overlay to create content) and `sourcePage` (the pdf.js proxy index, used only by `doc.getPage(sourcePage)` to render), so an overlay no longer stamps the SOURCE page number into the annotation. Screenshot screenshots/def-133-pen-correct-page.png. CLOSED.

## DEF-132: Frameless window cannot be moved by dragging the title bar

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14 (v1.7.10)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.10 binary = 0dab4cb source). The window is created with `frame: false` (no native title bar).
2. Attempt to move the window by pressing and dragging anywhere on the top title bar (the brand / tab strip / empty caption area).

Expected: The window behaves as a normal draggable Windows window — dragging the caption strip moves it (and Aero Snap works at the screen edges).
Actual: The window cannot be moved by dragging the title bar. Sampling the computed `-webkit-app-region` across the title bar yields `draggablePx = 0` and `noDragPx = 60480` — every pixel of the 1442x44 title bar resolves to `no-drag`; the full-width `.titlebar-slot` (1264px, flex:1) and the `.app-header` inside it are both `-webkit-app-region: no-drag`. With `frame: false` there is also no native caption area to grab, so the window has no mouse-drag affordance at all. Screenshot: screenshots/def-132-titlebar-region.png.
Root cause: `src/renderer/styles.css` — `.titlebar { -webkit-app-region: drag }` (line 312) is defeated by `.titlebar > * { -webkit-app-region: no-drag }` (line 317-319), which applies `no-drag` to the `.titlebar-slot` (the direct child that fills the whole bar width) and `.titlebar-controls`/`.titlebar-menu`. The `.app-header` inside the slot also declares `-webkit-app-region: no-drag` (line 282). Because the slot spans the entire bar (the only free drag surface is the leftover padding, which is zero-width given the slot is `flex: 1 1 auto`), there is effectively no draggable caption region. Combined with `frame: false` (src/main/window.ts:64) there is no native caption either — so the window is immovable by mouse.
History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth on installed v1.7.10; region map: titlebar-slot and app-header both no-drag, dragPx=0).
- qa: retested on installed v1.7.11 (FileVersion 1.7.11, exe 05:42 newer than all src). The `.titlebar` computes `-webkit-app-region: drag`; `.titlebar-slot` and `.app-header` both resolve to `drag` (the DEF-132 `.titlebar > * { no-drag }` rule is gone — only interactive children opt out via scoped `.titlebar-menu-*` / `.titlebar-control*` / `.app-header button,input,select,textarea` rules). Region map over the 1442x44 bar: dragPx=46836, noDragPx=13644, so 72.7% of the caption strip is draggable (was dragPx=0). The frameless window is now movable by dragging the caption strip. Screenshot screenshots/def-132-titlebar-draggable.png. CLOSED.

- Phase: 14 (v1.7.7)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.7, rebuilt + reinstalled 11:24 PM).
2. Open report.pdf (34 pages).
3. Tools palette -> "Insert pages", mode "Blank page". The field help says: `Page number where the new content lands. Use end to append. 1 means "before page 1"; {totalPages + 1} means "appended after the last page"`.
4. Enter `1` and observe the placed page; then re-insert with `2` and observe.

Expected: Following the hint, entering `1` should make the blank page the FIRST page (before page 1), and entering `2` should make it the SECOND page (page 2).
Actual: Entering `1` makes the blank page the SECOND page (pageOrder `[0,34,1,2,...]`), and entering `2` makes it the THIRD page (pageOrder `[0,1,34,2,...]`). Every numeric position is off by one from the hint: the engine treats the value as "insert AFTER page N" (`afterIndex = N-1` -> `insertAt = N`), so position `N` lands the new page at rank `N+1`. Only the `end` sentinel and the `{totalPages+1}` extreme clamp to a correct append. A user following the written hint (e.g. "insert after page 1" -> entering `2`) gets the page one slot later than intended.

Root cause: InsertPagesDialog.tsx `parsed.position = N - 1` is passed as the engine `afterIndex` (0-based index AFTER which to insert), and `_insertBlankPageImpl` (engine.ts:1284) does `insertAt = afterIndex + 1`. The dialog's user-facing hint describes the value as "the rank the new content lands", which contradicts the engine's "after page N" contract. (The DEF-114 `end`/append fix is unaffected and still correct.)

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth on installed v1.7.7; the "insert after page 1" flow is asserted in e2e/retests/release_gate_117_verify.spec.cjs B7 via position "1", and the off-by-one was characterized against position "1" and "2").
- qa: closed (retested on installed v1.7.9, exe 02:56 newer than all src). The position value now uses rank semantics — the page number the new content BECOMES — so the hint and the placement agree, and the off-by-one is gone: e2e e2e/retests/def_123_131_verify_1.7.9.spec.cjs DEF-129 inserted blank at "1" -> blank becomes page 1 (order0 [34,0,1,...], order[0]=34); DEF-130 inserted at "2" -> blank becomes page 2 (order0 [0,34,1,...]). Slot 0 maps to the engine afterIndex -2 PREPEND sentinel (valid in blank mode, no "cannot insert before page 1" guard) and the dialog min is now 1. DEF-114 append sentinel (end/empty -> -1) unchanged. Pinned by test/unit/renderer/defDEF121_122_insertRefreshGuard.test.ts (slot-to-afterIndex translation + dialog min=1). Unit suite green: 187 files / 2369 tests. Screenshot screenshots/def-129-position1.png. CLOSED.)

## DEF-117: Modal dialogs cannot open — React #310 (Rules of Hooks) from the B3/B6 backdrop refactor; whole UI unmounts to a black window

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14 (v1.7.7 regression)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.7, rebuilt 22:45, exe newer than all src).
2. Open report.pdf (34 pages).
3. Click the "Sign" toolbar button (`button[aria-label="Sign tool"]`).

Expected: The Signature manager modal (`.sig-manager`) opens so a signature can be drawn, typed, or a saved one picked and armed for placement.
Actual: The renderer throws `Minified React error #310` ("Rendered more hooks than during the previous render") and the ENTIRE app UI unmounts to a black window (screenshots/def-117-sign-flow-broken.png) — no modal, no toolbar, no page. The identical #310 fires when any other modal-opening control is clicked (Export to Word, Insert pages, Crop pages, Recognize text, Save-As, Optimize, Merge, Split, Stamp, Flatten, etc.), so it is not specific to Sign.

Root cause: The B3/B6 fix re-wired every modal backdrop through the shared `useBackdropClose` hook (src/renderer/components/modalBackdrop.ts). In 21 dialogs the hook is called AFTER the component's `if (!open) return null;` early return (e.g. SignatureManagerModal.tsx:72-77, DocxExportDialog.tsx:132-138, CropPagesDialog.tsx:168-174, InsertPagesDialog.tsx:156-162, OcrDialog.tsx:293-297). That violates the Rules of Hooks: when `open` flips false→true the hook count grows by one (`useRef` inside `useBackdropClose`), so React throws #310. The error is uncaught (no error boundary) and React unmounts the whole root, leaving a black window.

Affected dialogs (21, all with the hook after `if (!open) return null;`): SignatureManagerModal, DocxExportDialog, CropPagesDialog, InsertPagesDialog, OcrDialog, DeletePageDialog, RenumberPagesDialog, ReplacePagesDialog, SaveAsDialog, OptimizeDialog, AuditSpaceDialog, MergeDialog, SplitDialog, ExportDialog, TextExportDialog, CreateFromImagesDialog, StampDialog, CommentExportDialog, CommentImportDialog, CloseTabPromptDialog, FlattenConfirmDialog.

Impact: This blocks the v1.7.7 verification of B1 (sign placement + re-click handles), B3/B6 (DOCX/Crop/Insert dialog stays open on a text-selection drag-out; genuine backdrop click still closes), B4 (OCR suspects panel as a top bar + no overlapping white text after OCR), B7 (insert blank page after page 1 shows exactly 35 thumbnails with no duplicate / stray "Page 17"), B8a (crop mode-switch no flicker) and B8b (per-page crop crops only the adjusted page). None of those flows can be exercised because the modal they live in never mounts. Repro note: B1/B3/B6/B7/B8a/B8b all timeout at `waitForSelector` for their dialog/modal, and each is accompanied by React #310 in `pageerror`.

Screenshot: screenshots/def-117-sign-flow-broken.png (black window after the Sign click; the #310 was captured in the renderer `pageerror`). Same black-window result captured at screenshots/gt-bug10-restored.png vicinity (any dialog open) and temp probes (b4_ocr.png).

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth reproduction on installed v1.7.7, rebuilt 22:45). Reproduced via the Sign toolbar button, the Tools-palette Sign entry, a direct `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('tflex:sign-button'))`, and the Export-to-Word tool — all yield React #310 and a black-unmounted UI. The `useBackdropClose` hook is placed after `if (!open) return null;` in all 21 dialogs above; before the B3/B6 change these dialogs used a plain non-hook `closeOnBackdrop` (e.g. `git diff` on SignatureManagerModal.tsx shows `useRef` now added after the early return).
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.7 (reinstalled 11:24 PM, exe 23:24 newer than all src) via e2e/retests/release_gate_117_verify.spec.cjs (10 tests, all PASS). Source-level check: all 21 dialogs now place `useBackdropClose` BEFORE the `if (!open) return null;` guard (verified by scanning each dialog: hook line < early-return line). Runtime: opened Sign, DOCX, Crop, Insert and OCR dialogs in sequence — each mount (`.modal-backdrop` present, app not black) and `pageerror` captures ZERO React #310/#520 hook errors across the whole run. The entire DEF-117-blocked surface is now exercisable and verified: B1 (sign re-click shows select handles), B3/B6 (DOCX + Insert stay open on a text-selection drag-out; a genuine backdrop click still closes), B4 (OCR suspects panel renders as a full-width TOP BAR at z-index 40 above the tools palette 30, y=145, not behind it), B7 (insert blank after page 1 -> 35 pages, no duplicate, blank at rank 2, save+reopen valid), B8a (crop mode/page switch keeps the canvas node stable, no opacity-0 flash, no jump to 612x792), B8b (per-page crop crops only page 1 — toast "Cropped 1 page." + page 1 renders smaller than unadjusted pages 2/3), B8c (undo after a page op visually reverts), B10 (maximize/restore icon distinct from minimize). CLOSED.

## DEF-120: Undo (Ctrl+Z) after a page-mutating op does not refresh the pdf.js proxy — visual stays stale

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14 (v1.7.7 fix)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.7, rebuilt 22:45).
2. Open report.pdf.
3. Rotate page 1 via the toolbar "Rotate clockwise" button; confirm the page paints landscape.
4. Press Ctrl+Z.

Expected: The page visually reverts — the pdf.js proxy repaints the pre-rotate state (portrait).
Actual: Before the fix, the engine's undo reverted the model but the renderer's pdf.js `doc` proxy was never rebuilt, so the canvas kept painting the PRE-undo bytes and the page stayed stale.

Root cause: `App.onUndo`/`onRedo` updated the engine UI mirror (`setEngineUiFor`) but never called `refreshDocProxyFor`, so the visible page did not reflect the reverted engine state.

History:
- qa: opened (B8c ground-truth)
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.7 (rebuilt 22:45). The undo-refresh mechanism is now exercised: rotate page 1 -> `engineState.rotations[0]` 0 -> 1 and the page canvas swaps 1156x1496 -> 1496x1156 (proxy refreshed, paints rotated page); Ctrl+Z -> `rotations[0]` back to 0, `modified` false, `canRedo` true, and the canvas swaps back to 1156x1496 (proxy refreshed, visual reverts). The `onUndo`/`onRedo` handlers now invoke `refreshDocProxyForRef.current` after `setEngineUiFor` (pinned by test/unit/renderer/bugB8c_undoRedoProxyRefresh.test.ts). NOTE: the named crop/delete variants are separately blocked by DEF-117 (their dialogs cannot open); the undo proxy-refresh itself is verified and working. CLOSED.

## DEF-116: Edit-text leaves the original run in the PDF — old title remains searchable/selectable after the edit

- Status: REJECTED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.6 build).
2. Open report.pdf, click the Edit toggle, then the "Edit text" tool.
3. Click the "TFlex Technical Report" title run so the inline editor opens pre-filled.
4. Replace the text with "ZZZ REPLACEMENT TEXT 123" and press Ctrl+Enter to confirm.

Expected: The edited run is replaced — the old "TFlex Technical Report" text is removed from the document, so it is no longer selectable/searchable/copyable and no longer present in the saved file.
Actual: The canvas paints the NEW title (DEF-108 is fixed), but the engine edits by MASKING the old run with a white rectangle and DRAWING the new text on top (`engine._editTextRunImpl`). The original "TFlex Technical Report" string stays in the PDF content stream; after the proxy refresh the live `.textLayer` still contains a visible-size stale span for "TFlex Technical Report" (x594,y327,w461,h45) at the SAME location as the new span (x594,y325,w515,h36). Selecting/copying the title area surfaces the hidden old title, and the saved PDF still contains the original run. (The app's own search index is rebuilt from the proxy and does NOT match the old title, so in-app Ctrl+F is correct; the issue is the document's own content.)
Root cause: `_editTextRunImpl` (engine.ts:1645) masks the old rect with `page.drawRectangle({color: rgb(1,1,1)})` instead of removing the original glyphs; pdf-lib's drawRectangle does not delete the underlying text operators, so pdf.js still extracts the masked old run into the textLayer.
Screenshot: screenshots/def-108-after-commit.png (shows new title live; the stale old-title span is in the textLayer), also screenshots/probe-108-search-old.png

History:
- qa: opened (discovered during DEF-108 retest on installed v1.7.6)
- orchestrator: REJECTED - pdf-lib has no content-stream tokenizer; stripping old text operators is a hand-rolled ~500-line high-risk rewrite. Mask-and-redraw is visually correct (old text hidden, only exposed by selection/extraction). Documented as v1 limitation; native dependency (qpdf/pdfcpu) is a future-phase item.

## DEF-114: Insert blank page with "end"/empty position lands at the FRONT, not the end

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.5 build).
2. Open report.pdf (34 pages).
3. Open the Tools palette -> "Insert pages".
4. Leave mode as "Blank page" and type `end` into the "Insert at page" field (the field help says `end` = append; clearing the field maps to the same sentinel). Click Insert.

Expected: The blank page is appended as the LAST page (page 35); the existing 34 pages keep their order.
Actual: The blank page is inserted as the FIRST page of the visible order. `tflexDiagnostics().engineState.pageOrder` becomes `[34,0,1,2,…,33]` (the newly added blank origIdx 34 at index 0), and the view/rail render a scrambled result (blank page at the front, two blank-looking thumbs, a mislabeled "Page N"). Note the engine page count is correct (34 -> 35); this is NOT a literal two-page duplication, but an incorrect placement that scrambles the document. Inserting with the DEFAULT numeric position ("35") works correctly (pageOrder ends with 34).
Root cause: InsertPagesDialog.tsx maps `end`/empty to `position:-1` ("appended at end"), but onInsertPagesConfirm (App.tsx:3019) passes that value straight to `engine.insertBlankPage(docId, position, …)`; engine `_insertBlankPageImpl` (engine.ts:1215) treats `afterIndex = -1` as "insert before the first page" (`insertAt = 0`). Two different -1 contracts collide.
Screenshot: screenshots/gt-bug7-after.png (also gt-bug7-before.png, gt-bug7-insert-dialog.png)

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth reproduction on installed v1.7.5)
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.6 (exe 1:05 PM, newer than src). Blank mode + position `end`: engineState pageCount 34 -> 35, modified=true, pageOrder=[0,1,...,33,34] — first=0 and last=34 (the new origIdx-34 blank page is the FINAL element, not the front). `_insertBlankPageImpl` now maps afterIndex<0 to `doc.order.length` (append). CLOSED.

## DEF-113: Add Box text is not rendered in the live view after confirming

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14

Steps to reproduce:

Expected: The committed text box renders its text on the page in the live document view.
Actual: The editor closes and the engine `modified` flag flips to true, but the new text is NOT rendered — the pdf.js textLayer contains no element with "HELLO BOX ADDED 456" and the page canvas still shows the pre-edit content. The edit only becomes visible after a save/reopen (the engine wrote it, the live view is stale).
Root cause: App.tsx `handleAddTextBox` (line 1785) calls `engine.addTextBox` + `noteOpApplied` but never rebuilds the renderer pdf.js `doc` proxy (unlike the OCR path which calls `refreshDocProxyFor` in `onOcrConfirm`). The DocumentView continues to render the pre-edit document.

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth reproduction on installed v1.7.5)
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.6 (exe 1:05 PM, newer than src). The proxy IS now rebuilt (handleAddTextBox calls refreshDocProxyFor), so the box text DOES appear in the live canvas — but only "HELL" of the committed "HELLO BOX ADDED 456" renders. Committed textarea value was verified as the full "HELLO BOX ADDED 456"; the `.textLayer` after commit contains a single span "HELL" (visible SIZE_BIG, x548,y568,w161,h64) and no span with the full string; the DOM has no element with the full text; engine `annotations=[]`. Root cause is now the default font size for a new box, `EditInlineEditor`/`EditOverlay` `size = Math.round(textTarget.rect.height * 0.8)` (capped at SIZE_MAX=72), which is enormous for a box whose height is large; `wrapTextToWidth` hard-breaks "HELLO" -> "HELL"+"O" when "HELLO" exceeds the box width, and the box height only fits that first fragment line, SILENTLY DROPPING the rest of the user's text. Content is lost in the committed box. REMAINS OPEN (severity raised to HIGH — committed content silently dropped).
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.6 (rebuilt 17:29). Add box in report.pdf, type "HELLO BOX ADDED 456" + Ctrl+Enter: the editor closes (count=0) and the FULL committed text renders live — the `.textLayer` contains a single span "HELLO BOX ADDED 456" (boxTextVisibleFull=true, joined=true, truncatedOnly=false; no lone "HELL" fragment). Screenshot screenshots/def-113-after-commit.png shows the full string on the page at a normal legible size. The oversized default box font is gone — the box no longer hard-breaks and drops content. CLOSED.

Expected: The editor stays mounted — a click on its own chrome is not an outside click. Context windows should only close on an explicit close/Cancel.
Actual: Pressing the "Font" label span closes the editor (`[data-edit-editor]` count -> 0); it is treated as an outside click. The textarea's onBlur fires because focus leaves the textarea to the body (relatedTarget null), the blur guard only bails when the new focus target is inside `.edit-inline-editor`, and a non-focusable label has no focusable target, so it commits/cancels and unmounts.
Root cause: EditInlineEditor.tsx `onTextareaBlur` (line 133) + the toolbar bar's non-focusable labels. There is no text-drag-outside / bar-press guard equivalent to InsertPagesDialog's B17 `backdropDownRef`. (Note: a text highlight-drag that starts inside the textarea and releases OUTSIDE the editor did NOT close it in the same test — the bar chrome press is the deterministically-reproducing path.)
Screenshot: screenshots/gt-bug6-after-bar-click.png (also gt-bug6-editor-open.png, gt-bug6-after-drag-outside.png)

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth reproduction on installed v1.7.5)
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.6 (exe 1:05 PM, newer than src). Pressing (mousedown/up) on the editor's own "Font" label (non-focusable chrome) leaves `[data-edit-editor="edit"]` mounted (count=1 after press); a positive control on the explicit Cancel button closes it (count=0). The editor now guards bar chrome via `insidePressRef` set on the editor's `onPointerDown`. CLOSED.

## DEF-109: Edit inline editor size (arrow/spinner) control is inert

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.5 build).
2. Open report.pdf, click the Edit toggle, then the "Edit text" tool, and click a text run so the inline editor opens.
3. Focus the "Font size (pt)" number input. Press the up-arrow key, and also click the native spin-arrow zone.

Expected: The size value increments via the keyboard up-arrow and the spinner arrows.
Actual: The value stays at 19 after ArrowUp and after a spin-arrow click (`before=19, afterArrowUp=19, afterSpinClick=19`); the only way to change it is to select-all and type a new number (fill('48') -> 48). The editor stays open after these interactions (so it is not the outside-click path).
Root cause: EditInlineEditor.tsx line 214 sets `onMouseDown={(e): void => e.preventDefault()}` on the size `<input type="number">` (the Bug-9 focus guard). preventDefault on mousedown suppresses the native spinner/arrow auto-increment (and Chromium's arrow-up on a focused number input), so the arrows do nothing; direct typing bypasses mousedown and works.
Screenshot: screenshots/gt-bug2b-size-control.png

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth reproduction on installed v1.7.5)
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.6 (exe 1:05 PM, newer than src). Focus the size input: ArrowUp increments 19 -> 20; the native spinner up-arrow increments 19 -> 20 -> 21 when clicked on the top-right hit zone; the editor stays mounted throughout. The `onMouseDown preventDefault` was removed from the number input. CLOSED.

## DEF-108: Edit-text confirm does not render the updated text in the live view

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 14

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (installed v1.7.5 build).
2. Open report.pdf, click the Edit toggle, then the "Edit text" tool.
3. Click the "TFlex Technical Report" title run so the inline editor opens pre-filled.
4. Replace the text with "ZZZ REPLACEMENT TEXT 123" and press Ctrl+Enter to confirm.

Expected: The title on the page updates to the new text in the live document view.
Actual: The editor closes and the engine `modified` flag flips to true, but the live pdf.js textLayer still reports the old run ("TFlex Technical Report" present, "ZZZ REPLACEMENT TEXT 123" absent). The canvas continues to paint the original text; the edit only appears after a save/reopen.
Root cause: App.tsx `handleEditTextRun` (line 1759) calls `engine.editTextRun` + `noteOpApplied` but never rebuilds the renderer pdf.js `doc` proxy (contrast the OCR path, `onOcrConfirm`, which calls `refreshDocProxyFor`). The DocumentView keeps rendering the stale pre-edit proxy.
Screenshot: screenshots/gt-bug2a-before-commit.png, gt-bug2a-after-commit.png

History:
- qa: opened (ground-truth reproduction on installed v1.7.5)
- qa: re-verified on installed v1.7.6 (exe 1:05 PM, newer than src). Edit the title to "ZZZ REPLACEMENT TEXT 123" + Ctrl+Enter: the editor closes (count 0), `modified` = true, the canvas paints the NEW title, and the live `.textLayer` contains "ZZZ REPLACEMENT TEXT 123" (newVisible=true). `handleEditTextRun` now rebuilds the pdf.js proxy via `refreshDocProxyFor`. CLOSED. (NOTE: the original masked run still remains as hidden text in the PDF/textLayer — filed separately as DEF-116.)

## DEF-081: Broken application layout (zero-height workspace)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex production build (`npm run build && electron .`).
2. Observe the application window.
3. Attempt to open a PDF or interact with the Welcome screen.

Expected: The Welcome screen or Workspace fills the window below the title bar.
Actual: The `app-main` container has 0px height. The window area below the title bar is empty (showing the black background of the `.app` container). The `Workspace` element is marked as "hidden" by Playwright because its container has no size.
Root cause: `.app` grid template is `auto auto 1fr`. Row 1 is `TitleBar` (32px). Row 2 is `app-main` (auto). Row 3 is empty (1fr). Since `AppHeader` is a child of `TitleBar` rather than a sibling, there is no element to occupy Row 2 or expand Row 3 correctly.

## DEF-432: Phase 61 tear-out releases the strip's scroll container - overflowing strips jump and the dragged tab stops tracking the pointer

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-129, Phase 61 diff-pass)
- Phase: 61

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, then `node test-fixtures/adv-p61/probe.cjs spill` (canonical
   `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`; fresh `--user-data-dir`).
2. Open `assets/samples/report.pdf`, `long.pdf`, `form.pdf`, then add tabs via the strip
   `+` (`[data-new-tab]`) until the strip overflows - 31 tabs gives `.tab-list`
   `scrollWidth` 1686 vs `clientWidth` 1656 (10px scrollbar).
3. Scroll `.tab-list` to its maximum (`scrollLeft` 30), start a drag from a visible
   non-active tab's colour chip, and move the pointer straight DOWN (`dx` 0) past the
   tear-out threshold (strip bottom 44 + 24).

Expected (Phase 61 criterion 1): while the pointer leaves the strip the dragged tab's
box follows the pointer on both axes, and the `overflow: visible` release only stops the
clipping - the strip's layout stays put.

Actual: when tear-out arms (`data-tab-tearout="true"` on both `.tab-area` and
`.tab-list`), `overflow` flips `auto` -> `visible`. Because `.tab-list` is ALSO the
strip's horizontal scroll container (`src/renderer/styles.css:1875`, `overflow-x: auto`),
releasing overflow destroys the scroll container: `scrollLeft` snaps 30 -> 0 and the
scrollbar thickness 10 -> 0 in the same frame. Every non-dragged tab jumps one frame
(dx +30, dy +10), the strip snaps back on release, and the dragged tab stops tracking
the pointer by exactly `(scrollLeft, scrollbarThickness)` (held at x 1790.7 the box
landed at left 1754.2; held at y 104 the top landed at 101). With 3 tabs (no overflow)
the same probe tracks within 0px, which is why `e2e/phase61_tab_tearout.spec.cjs` (3
tabs) passes.

Root cause: `src/renderer/styles.css:2236-2239` releases `overflow` on `.tab-list`, the
same element that owns the strip's horizontal scroll. A scroll container cannot carry
`overflow: visible`; the clip must be released on a wrapper that is not the scroller, or
the scroll state captured and restored around the release.

Impact: a visible strip jump plus a pointer-tracking error on every tear-out started
from an overflowing (many-tab) strip - breaks Phase 61 criterion 1 in exactly the
overflow case Phase 59 was written for. Silent in the 3-tab spec.

Evidence: `adv_p61_spill.log`; `screenshots/adv-p61-spill-rest.png` and
`screenshots/adv-p61-spill-tearing.png`. Full analysis: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-129.

History:
- adversary: opened (ADV-129, Phase 61 diff-pass, TFL-67).
- orchestrator: ACCEPTED (TFL-44) -> DEF-432, routed to frontend-dev.
- orchestrator: FIX-READY (TFL-44) - brief to frontend-dev: stop releasing `overflow` on
  the `.tab-list` scroller (move the un-clip to a non-scroller layer or float the dragged
  tab out of the scroller) so an overflowing strip does not jump and the dragged tab
  tracks the pointer; add `e2e/phase61_tearout_overflow.spec.cjs` reproducing the
  overflow case and keep the 3-tab spec green.
- qa: CLOSED (TFL-70, Phase 61 phase-close). `npm.cmd run build` EXIT 0; `npm.cmd run
  test:e2e -- e2e/phase61_tearout_overflow.spec.cjs` -> 1 passed. Run log confirms
  `afterScrollLeft=30` (unchanged from `scrolled.scrollLeft`), `afterScrollbar=10`
  (unchanged), every non-dragged tab `dLeft=0.00 dTop=0.00` (<=2px), and the dragged tab
  `dx=0 dy=63` with `left=492.17` vs `expectedLeft=492.17`, `top=71` vs `expectedTop=71.00`
  (<=2.5px, both axes). Evidence: screenshots/p61-tearout-overflow.png. Neighbour checks
  green: phase60 unit 8/8, phase60 e2e 3/3, phase58 detach e2e 1/1, phase59 overflow e2e
  1/1, phase62TabRestyle unit 9/9.

## DEF-433: Reordering a squeezed strip (640px min width) leaves the active tab clipped at the strip edge - no scroll-into-view after the reorder

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (ADV-130, Phase 60 diff-pass)
- Phase: 60

Steps to reproduce:
1. `npm.cmd run build`, then `node test-fixtures/adv-p60/probe.cjs follow` (canonical
   `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`; fresh `--user-data-dir`).
2. Open `report.pdf`, `long.pdf`, `form.pdf` (3 tabs), set the window to 640x620 (the app
   minimum) so `.tab-list` overflows (156px wide, `scrollWidth` 238, 10px scrollbar).
3. Grab the ACTIVE tab's colour chip and drag it right to the strip edge; release.

Expected (Phase 60 criterion 6 - active tab never clipped in a squeezed strip): the live
follow and animated reflow work and the ACTIVE tab stays fully inside the strip.

Actual: the reorder commits correctly and the reflow runs, but the active tab ends at
`l=246 r=378` against the strip `[174,330]` - clipped 48px at the right edge. `scrollLeft`
stays 0 and the app never brings it back into view. Repeats 5 runs (`follow`, `narrowclip`,
`clip3`); `clip3-post.revealByScrolling` shows the strip COULD reveal it (`scrollLeft`
14-18 puts it at `l=198 r=330`) but does not.

Root cause: `scrollActiveIntoView` (`src/renderer/components/AppHeader.tsx:500-513`) is
re-run only when `activeId`, `tabs.length` or `instantMotion` change (effect deps
`AppHeader.tsx:514-516`). A reorder changes none of them, so the commit at
`AppHeader.tsx:888-896` (`onMoveTab` + the DEF-411 active restore) moves the active tab's
flow slot with no scroll correction. Same class as DEF-428 (resize) and DEF-422 (640px),
but a distinct trigger - a reorder - that neither covers; the Phase 60 criterion-6 e2e
(`e2e/phase60_tab_drag.spec.cjs:273-359`) only drags a BACKGROUND tab, so the
active-pushed-out case is untested.

Impact: breaks Phase 60 criterion 6 in the minimum-width squeezed strip after a reorder;
the active tab sits half outside the strip until the user scrolls manually.

Evidence: `test-fixtures/adv-p60/all.log`, `test-fixtures/adv-p60/results.json`;
`screenshots/adv-p60-narrow640-clip.png`, `screenshots/adv-p60-narrowclip.png`,

- CTO: ACCEPTED (TFL-43) -> DEF-433, routed to frontend-dev.

  the existing `scrollActiveIntoView` so the active tab is revealed in the squeezed 640px
  strip; add a narrow-width active-tab case to `e2e/phase60_tab_drag.spec.cjs` and keep
  verify + the phase60/58/59 suites green. Not the DEF-432 code path.
- qa: CLOSED (TFL-75 re-verification of TFL-76 round 2). `npm.cmd run build` exit 0;

  reduce` active [174,306] scroll 72->38 inside=true; Animations OFF (`data-animations="off"`)

- CTO: SUPERSEDED (Phase 72, ruling 9, TFL-202). Phase 72 retires the tab-strip scroll

## DEF-435: collapsed protection "i" pins over the LEFT panel, covering the leading edge of the Combine control — not at the canvas top-left

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: qa (TFL-88 / TFL-46.1 bug-hunt, current working tree f3cd127)
- Phase: 59 (item 2; REQUIREMENTS.md:3661-3665)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (`launchApp`) and open an encrypted PDF (toolbar Open → password prompt
   → `P59-Protect!`). The protection banner appears in the document column.
2. Wait ~10 s (or click the banner's collapse control) for the auto-collapse into the "i".
3. Observe the small "i" (info) icon: it renders over the LEFT panel's header, on top of
   the leading edge of the **Combine** control, instead of at the canvas's top-left.

Expected (REQUIREMENTS.md:3664-3665): the collapsed icon is "pinned at the canvas's
top-left ... never covers the page or a control, and the collapsed icon is always
reachable". The canvas begins to the right of the left panel.

Actual: the icon is placed relative to `.document-column`, which spans the whole stage
from x=64 (over the left panel) rather than starting at the canvas. The `.context-panel`
(left panel) occupies x=64..248; the page scroller (`.document-scroller`) starts at
x=248. Measured icon box x=80..108, y=52..80 lies inside the left panel, and the Combine
control box x=80..170.8125, y=52.5..78.5 overlaps it. `elementFromPoint` at the icon
centre (94,66) returns the icon's own `path` (so the icon intercepts the click), and
`iconOverlapsCombine=true`. A click on that region re-expands the notice instead of
activating Combine. The icon is reachable and does not cover the page, but it covers a
control, failing the stated requirement. The existing
`e2e/phase59_protection_notice.spec.cjs` passes because it treats `.document-column`
(x=64, width 2496) as "the canvas", which is wider than the real canvas (scroller
x=248..2296), so its top-left assertion is satisfied by an icon that is actually over the
left panel.

Commands + output (verbatim):
- `npm.cmd run build` → exit 0 (built in 761ms; `dist\main\index.js 8.1mb`).
- `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/phase59_protection_notice.spec.cjs` → `1 passed (15.2s)`;
  lines: `[P59-protect] box={"borderRadius":"8px","animationName":"protection-notice-in","animationDuration":"0.25s","width":2200,"height":74.171875}`;
  `[P59-protect] auto-collapse after 9503ms state=collapsed noticePresent=false`;
  `[P59-protect] icon={"x":80,"y":52,"width":28,"height":28} page={"left":748.53,"top":44,...} canvas={"x":64,"y":44,"width":2496,"height":1348}`;
  `[P59-protect] re-expanded={"notice":true,"icon":false,"state":"expanded"}`.
- `npx.cmd playwright test e2e/tfl46_protection_probe.spec.cjs` → `1 passed (14.2s)`;
  `[TFL46] icon={"x":80,"y":52,"width":28,"height":28,"right":108,"bottom":80,"cx":94,"cy":66}`;
  `[TFL46] documentColumn={"x":64,"y":44,"width":2496,"height":1348,"right":2560,...}`;
  `[TFL46] pageScroller={"x":248,"y":44,"width":2048,"height":1348,"right":2296,...} scrollParent={"tag":"DIV","cls":"document-scroller","left":248,...}`;
  `[TFL46] contextPanel={"x":64,"y":44,"width":184,"height":1348,"right":248,...}`;
  `[TFL46] combineCount=1 combine={"x":80,"y":52.5,"width":90.8125,"height":26,"right":170.8125,"bottom":78.5,"cx":125.40625,"cy":65.5}`;
  `[TFL46] hit={"iconCentre":"path.[object SVGAnimatedString]","iconTopLeft":"BUTTON.protection-notice-collapsed-toggle","combineCentre":"SPAN.","iconBelow":"path.[object SVGAnimatedString]"}`;
  `[TFL46] iconOverlapsCombine=true`.

Impact: fails the explicit "never covers ... a control" clause of the protection-notice
requirement and steals the click target from 28px of the Combine control (clicking there
re-expands the notice). HIGH: a stated acceptance requirement is broken; no document
corruption. The banner itself (rounded box, animation, auto-collapse dwell, re-expand,
collapse control, no page overlap) works.

Evidence: `screenshots/tfl46-icon-vs-panel.png` and zoomed
`screenshots/tfl46-icon-vs-panel-clip.png` (the "i" drawn over the Combine control's
leading glyph). Probe: `e2e/tfl46_protection_probe.spec.cjs`. Source anchors:
`src/renderer/components/ProtectionNotice.tsx:139-149`,
`src/renderer/styles.css:17134-17151` (`.protection-notice-collapsed-toggle { position:
absolute; top: var(--sp-2); left: var(--space-standard) }` anchored to a
`.document-column` that begins over the left panel), call site
`src/renderer/App.tsx:604-627`.

## DEF-444: Read-only checkbox / radio / dropdown / listbox fields render nothing under Phase 65's ENABLE_FORMS gate — the overlay suppression returns null and pdf.js does not paint those widget types

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH
- Found by: adversary (TFL-130 / TFL-49.8 diff-pass, Phase 65); ADV-134
- Phase: 65 (features A/B/C; criterion 2 "no field appears twice", criterion 3 "zero fields missing")

Steps to reproduce (static; a rendered fixture is named for qa):
1. Build a PDF whose AcroForm has a check box with /Ff ReadOnly (bit 1) set (a read-only /FT /Ch dropdown
   or listbox behaves identically). The existing `test-fixtures/phase65/form-locked-anon.pdf` carries only
   a read-only TEXT field, so a read-only non-text widget must be added for the rendered proof.
2. Open it on the Phase 65 build and inspect the widget's page region.

Expected (features A/B/C): the field is drawn exactly once - a truthful non-editable surface at the widget
rect (a disabled overlay control with the read-only reason), because pdf.js does not paint it.

Actual: nothing is drawn. `FieldEditor` returns null at `FormsOverlay.tsx:172`, and pdf.js's canvas op list
for the widget is empty, so the field is INVISIBLE - a gap where the printed box is, with no affordance and
no read-only reason.

Root cause: the single suppression gate
`if (kind === "signature" || (field.readOnly === true && isRealField)) return null;`
(`src/renderer/forms/FormsOverlay.tsx:172`) assumes every read-only widget is canvas-painted. pdf.js only
sets `hasOwnCanvas` for `TextWidgetAnnotation` (`readOnly && !noHTML`, `pdf.worker.mjs:55202`), the
push-button branch of `ButtonWidgetAnnotation` (`:55363`) and `SignatureWidgetAnnotation` (`:55894`); the
checkbox/radio branch (`:55355-55362`) and `ChoiceWidgetAnnotation` (`:55702`) never set it, and `noHTML`
is false for a field-level /Ff ReadOnly (`:53940`). So under `annotationMode: ENABLE_FORMS`
(`PageView.tsx:705`) pdf.js returns `separateForm: true` with an empty op list (`:54759`) for those
widgets.

Impact: HIGH - read-only checkbox/radio/dropdown/listbox fields vanish. Regression from the pre-diff
behaviour (a disabled control was visible). On the legal/immigration form class where read-only
computed/locked fields are common.

Evidence: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-134; anchors above.

History:
- adversary (TFL-130 / TFL-49.8): filed ADV-134 (diff-pass, HIGH).
- CTO: triaged ACCEPTED -> DEF-444 (HIGH). Renderer-only fix; assigned to frontend-dev. Phase 65 ruling 6
  carried a false premise (`hasOwnCanvas = readOnly && !noHTML` is text-only); corrected by ruling 7 in
  REQUIREMENTS.md.
- CTO: triaged FIX-READY (TFL-133). frontend-dev reason recorded verbatim: "the single suppression gate now
  suppresses the overlay ONLY for widgets pdf.js canvas-paints under `AnnotationMode.ENABLE_FORMS`:
  `if (kind === \"signature\" || (field.readOnly === true && isRealField && kind === \"text\")) {`. The
  comment block above it was rewritten to state the true rule... No editor or fill-path code changed."
  Verified in the tree at FormsOverlay.tsx:177; unit tests updated (`Tests 48 passed (48)`, 4 files) and
  `npm run verify` exit 0. Awaits qa FIX-READY verification (qa alone sets CLOSED). NOTE: the fix and its
  test edits were swept into commit ab62660 (a concurrent Phase 68 phase-close `git add -A`), not a Phase 65
  allowlist commit.
- qa (TFL-139, FIX-READY verification): CLOSED. Reproduced the fix on the running Electron app and added the
  missing rendered proof. `test-fixtures/phase65/make-locked-fixture.cjs` now appends a read-only check box,
  a read-only 3-widget radio group, a read-only dropdown and a read-only list box (each `/Ff` ReadOnly)
  alongside the existing read-only text and signature, and `form-locked-anon.pdf` was regenerated (9618

## DEF-445: Push-button fields still double-surface — pdf.js paints the push button on the canvas while FormsOverlay mounts an editable text editor over it (`formFieldKind` misclassifies `PDFButton` as `text`)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (TFL-130 / TFL-49.8 diff-pass, Phase 65); ADV-134 (secondary)
- Phase: 65 (feature A / criterion 2 "no field appears twice")

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build a PDF with a push button (`/FT /Btn` with the Pushbutton bit set; pdf-lib `PDFButton`).
2. Open it on the Phase 65 build: the canvas paints the push button (pdf.js sets `hasOwnCanvas` true,
   `pdf.worker.mjs:55363`) and `FormsOverlay` also mounts an editable text editor over it.

Expected: one surface - the push button's native canvas appearance, no editable overlay.
Actual: the editable text editor is drawn over the painted push button (double surface).

Root cause: `formFieldKind` (`src/main/services/forms.ts:152-166`) matches `PDFTextField` / `PDFCheckBox` /
`PDFRadioGroup` / `PDFDropdown` / `PDFOptionList` and falls through to `return 'text'` for a `PDFButton`,
so the engine reports the push button as a fillable `text` field (`src/shared/types.ts:791`).

Impact: MEDIUM - the duplicate box the phase set out to remove survives for push buttons. No data loss.
Pre-existing (not introduced by Phase 65), but it violates the phase's "no field appears twice" goal.

Evidence: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-134; `src/main/services/forms.ts:152-166`; `src/shared/types.ts:791-796`.

## DEF-446: Book View annotation placement also turns the book page — a placed ink/highlight mark commits to page 1 but the same gesture's terminal click fires the page-turn handler, so the view advances off the marked page

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa (TFL-136, Phase 66 chunk 3 focused verification, criterion 5; uncommitted chunk-3 tree, master HEAD)
- Phase: 66 (feature E / success criterion 5 "annotation marking in Book View")

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (`launchApp`) and open `assets/samples/report.pdf` through the toolbar Open button,
   stubbing `dialog.showOpenDialog`.
2. Enter Book View (`[aria-label="Book View"]`).
3. Arm ink through the Book View toolbar (`[data-book-tools]` -> `[data-ann-dropdown-toggle]` ->
   `[data-ann-dropdown-menu] [data-tool="ink"]`) and drag on the book page exactly like
   `e2e/phase51_gate.spec.cjs:227-238` (`mouse.move` -> `down` -> `move(+160,+90,{steps:8})` -> `up`).

Expected (criterion 5): the ink stroke commits to page 1 and is rendered in `[data-annotation-layer="1"]`,
with the view still on page 1.

Actual: the engine commits the ink on page 1 (id present, `kind:"ink"`, `page:1`), but the visible book
page advances to page 2 during the same gesture — `window.tflexDiagnostics().engineState.annotations`
reports the page-1 stroke while `[data-book-page]` reads `"2"` and `[data-annotation-layer="1"]` is gone.
Root cause: the Book View page `<figure>` carries the criterion-4 page-turn `onClick`
(`src/renderer/components/BookView.tsx:467-475` single, `:425-437` spread) unconditionally; the
annotation overlay's `pointerdown` (`e.preventDefault()`, `AnnotationOverlay.tsx:854-857`) does not
suppress the synthesized `click` from the drag's pointerup, so placement both marks and navigates.
Highlight behaves identically.

Impact: MEDIUM — the annotation is committed and is not lost (Previous, or re-entering Book View, renders
it), but every placement gesture immediately navigates off the marked page, so the marking workflow is
effectively unusable. No document corruption.

Evidence:
- `e2e/phase66_bookview_annotations.spec.cjs` tests "criterion 5: toolbar present, ink placed, survives
  leave + re-enter" and "criterion 5: highlight placed on book text, survives leave + re-enter" fail at
  the required `[data-annotation-layer="1"] [data-annotation-id]` assertion with
  `visiblePage:"2"` (`Received: 0`).
- `e2e/phase66_bookview_annotations.spec.cjs` test "criterion 5 characterization" confirms the same
  stroke renders on page 1 after `[data-book-prev]` (`onPage1: 1`) and survives leave + re-enter
  (`rendered: 1`).
- Screenshots: `screenshots/phase66-ann-ink.png`, `screenshots/phase66-ann-highlight.png` (post-gesture,
  page 2); `screenshots/phase66-ann-ink-page1.png`, `screenshots/phase66-ann-ink-reenter.png` (page 1).

Command: `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test e2e/phase66_bookview_annotations.spec.cjs`
-> `2 failed / 2 passed` (the two criterion tests red; persistence tests green).

History:
- qa (TFL-136): filed from the Phase 66 chunk 3 focused verification; criterion 5 red.
  Owner: frontend-dev (suppress the page-turn click when an annotation gesture consumed the pointer).
- CTO (TFL-64): triaged OPEN / MEDIUM. Real and evidence-backed (qa reproduced it on the current
  uncommitted chunk-3 tree): the mark commits but the gesture's terminal click fires the page-turn
  `onClick`. Dispatched frontend-dev **TFL-141** (priority high) to guard the three Book View

## DEF-447: Collapsed top-of-canvas "i" icons overlap the canvas "Book View" control (Phase 67 criterion 3 "no 'i' covers a canvas control")

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: qa (TFL-138 / TFL-104.7 phase-close QA, measured geometry probe)
- Phase: 67 (REQUIREMENTS.md:4293-4295 feature/CONTROL-INDEX "Collapsed icons never collide ... no 'i'
  covers a canvas control"; criterion 3)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (dev build via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`).
2. Open a document so a top-of-canvas notice can appear; let it auto-collapse (~10 s) or click its
   collapse control.
   - Conversion: open `test-fixtures/phase53/network.html`; the card collapses to `[data-conversion-icon]`.
   - 3D: open a PDF carrying a `/Subtype /3D` annotation (probe builds one); collapse `[data-pdf3d-collapse]`
     -> `[data-pdf3d-icon]`.
   - Protection: open a password-protected PDF (`e2e/lib/p52_crypto.cjs`); collapse `[data-protection-collapse]`
     -> `[data-protection-icon]`.
3. Measure `getBoundingClientRect()` of the collapsed icon and of the canvas `[data-book-view-open]`
   control (the "Book View" button at the canvas top-left).

Expected (REQUIREMENTS.md:4293-4295): a collapsed "i" covers no canvas control; its box must not
intersect any interactive control. The protection icon is the untouched reference for this promise.

Actual: every collapsed icon's box intersects the Book View control. Measured on the current tree
(window 2048x1392):
- Book View `[data-book-view-open]` rect = { left: 260, top: 56, right: 368, bottom: 83.4 }
- protection `i` rect = { left: 264, top: 52, right: 292, bottom: 80 }  -> overlaps (true)
- conversion `i` rect = { left: 300, top: 52, right: 328, bottom: 80 }  -> overlaps (true)
- 3D `i` rect = { left: 336, top: 52, right: 364, bottom: 80 }          -> overlaps (true)
The icons (28x28, z-index 8) paint over the Book View button's left and right ends; only the middle
"Book View" label stays hit-testable (the button centre x=314 lies between the two icon boxes). The
phase59 protection spec only checked overlap against the left panel's Combine control
(`[data-context-panel-combine]`, x 80-170, no overlap), so this collision is not covered by it.

Impact: MEDIUM. The Book View control's clickable area is reduced (its two ends are covered by the
collapsed icons) but the control stays operable at its centre, so the workflow is degraded, not
blocked, and no document content is affected. It does violate criterion 3's literal "neither overlaps
a canvas control" and the "no 'i' covers a canvas control" rule.

Evidence:
- `e2e/phase67_notice_geometry.spec.cjs` test 3 `both collapsed icons present (protection + 3D)`
  fails the `overlapBook` / `overlapBook3d` assertions; tests 1 and 2 log `overlapBook:true` for the
  conversion and 3D icons in their own scenarios. Runner log lines `P67_GEOM_BOTH`,
  `P67_GEOM_CONVERSION`, `P67_GEOM_3D`.
- Screenshots: `screenshots/phase67-both-collapsed-clip.png` (amber protection "i" and blue 3D "i"
  painted on the "Book View" pill), `screenshots/phase67-conversion-collapsed-clip.png`,
  `screenshots/phase67-3d-collapsed-clip.png`.

Command: `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase67_notice_geometry.spec.cjs` -> `1 failed / 2 passed`
(the failure is the Book View overlap assertion; all other measured criteria pass).

## DEF-448: Book View — changing an annotation's colour through the portaled colour popover also turns the book page (surviving DEF-446 class via a portaled annotation control)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Found by: adversary (TFL-146, Phase 66 adversarial diff-pass; ACCEPTED from ADV-135)
- Phase: 66 (feature E / success criterion 5 "annotation marking in Book View"; high-risk merge: annotation persistence)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex (`launchApp`) and open `assets/samples/report.pdf`; enter Book View (`[aria-label="Book View"]`).
2. In `[data-book-tools]` arm ink and drag on the book page to place a stroke on page 1 (the DEF-446 fix
   keeps the view on page 1 and the stroke commits to page 1).
3. Arm select, click the stroke (`[data-annotation-layer="1"] [data-annotation-id="<id>"]`); wait for
   `[data-content-action-bar]`.
4. Click `[data-content-action-bar] [data-ann-color-box]`, then
   `[data-color-popover] [aria-label="Built-in green"]`.

Expected (criterion 5): the annotation's colour changes to green and the view stays on page 1 (the
annotation's page), exactly as the DEF-446 placement gesture keeps still.

Actual: the colour IS applied (`color` `#2563eb` -> `green`) AND the book advances in the same click —
single layout `[data-book-page]` 1 -> 2; double layout (stroke on the right page) spread [1,2] -> [3,4]
(left-page indicator 1 -> 3). The annotation stays attached to its correct page, so this is a navigation
bug, not data loss, but the user is thrown off the page they are editing on every recolour.
Root cause: `AnnColorBox` mounts its `ColorPalette` via `createPortal(..., document.body)`
(`src/renderer/annotations/AnnColorBox.tsx:119`); the React synthetic click from a swatch bubbles through
the React tree to the Book View page `<figure>` `onClick` (`src/renderer/components/BookView.tsx:430-439`
spread-left, `:466-475` spread-right, `:503-512` single). The DEF-446 guard suppresses a turn only when
`(e.target).closest('.annotation-layer') != null` or the capture-phase `annLayerPressRef` is set; for the
portaled swatch the DOM target is body-rooted, so `closest('.annotation-layer')` is null and the
pointerdown happened on the portal (not inside the layer), so `annLayerPressRef` was set false. Both
guards miss.

Impact: MEDIUM — no data loss (the colour is applied and the annotation keeps its page), but the view
leaves the annotated page on every recolour, so annotation editing in Book View is degraded. No document
corruption.

Evidence (adversary TFL-146, fresh probes through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`):
- Screenshots `screenshots/adv-135-single-before.png` / `adv-135-single-after.png` (page 1 -> page 2 with
  the stroke recoloured green) and `screenshots/adv-135-double-before.png` / `adv-135-double-after.png`
  (spread [1,2] -> [3,4]).
- Probe console (single): `after-mark-click {page:"1", actionBar:1, color:"#2563eb"}` then
  `after-pick-green {page:"2", actionBar:1, color:"green"}`; double: `beforePage:"1", afterPage:"3",
  beforeColor:"#2563eb", afterColor:"green", pageTurned:true`. The turn first appears at the swatch click,
  not the selection click, isolating the popover as the trigger.
- Baseline Phase 66 specs green in the same run: `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test
  e2e/phase66_bookview.spec.cjs e2e/phase66_bookview_spread.spec.cjs e2e/phase66_bookview_annotations.spec.cjs`
  -> 10 passed / 0 failed; the 3 Book View unit files -> 17 tests passed.

History:
- adversary (TFL-146): filed ADV-135, MEDIUM, PENDING in ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md.
- CTO (TFL-64): ACCEPTED -> DEF-448 (MEDIUM). Real, deterministic, evidence-backed; it is the DEF-446
  class reached through a portaled annotation control, not a re-litigation of the closed placement case.

## DEF-467: Book View turn leaf is a live annotation hit surface - an armed-tool stroke begun during a turn commits to the OUTGOING page (and the destination layer is duplicated)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (escalation to HIGH defensible - the wrong page is persisted on save)
- Found by: adversary (TFL-271, Phase 77 adversarial diff-pass; ACCEPTED from ADV-146 / ADV-147)
- Phase: 77 (Book View correction; success criteria 4 and 6 - the turning leaf must be decorative and bounded)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch TFlex via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, open a 16-page PDF, enter Book View (`[aria-label="Book View"]`), switch to double.
2. Arm `ink` in the Book View toolbar (`[data-book-tools]`).
3. Click Next (`[data-book-next]`) and pause the turn leaf early (`document.querySelector('[data-book-turn]').getAnimations()[0].pause(); ...currentTime = 55`).
4. `document.elementFromPoint(<page centre>)`, then a short real mouse drag there; let the turn settle.

Expected: the transient turning leaf is decorative - it must never accept pointer/animation input; a stroke started after a turn begins marks the visible destination page or is ignored, and only one interactive annotation layer per page exists at a time.

Actual: `elementFromPoint` resolves to the leaf's `[data-annotation-layer]` for the OUTGOING page (`pointer-events: auto`), and the drag commits ink to the outgoing page (double: label `Page 3-4 of 16`, static `[3,4]`, ink on page 2; single: `Page 2 of 16`, static `[2]`, ink on page 1). The mark is invisible after the flip and would be saved to the wrong page with no warning. `[data-annotation-layer="3"]` also exists twice mid-turn.

Root cause: `renderTurnLeaf` passes the armed `annotationTool` to the leaf faces (`BookView.tsx:399-437`, tool at `:410`); `.book-view-turn { pointer-events: none }` (`styles.css:18717-18725`) is overridden for descendants by `.annotation-layer-active { pointer-events: auto }` (`styles.css:5862`), set by `AnnotationOverlay` when a tool is armed or an annotation is selected.

Impact: MEDIUM - a silent wrong-page annotation write that persists on save; narrow ~350ms window and an armed tool required. The duplicate non-interactive layer is a hit-test/oracle hazard.

History:
- adversary (TFL-271): filed ADV-146 (MEDIUM) and ADV-147 (LOW).
- CTO (TFL-238): ACCEPTED -> DEF-467; dispatched frontend-dev **TFL-273** (priority high) to make the turn leaf non-interactive (pass `initialAnnotationToolState` to the leaf faces at `BookView.tsx:410`; scoped `.book-view-turn .annotation-layer { pointer-events: none }`) with a unit assertion that no `.annotation-layer-active` exists inside `[data-book-turn]`. Awaiting fix; then FIX-READY -> qa FIX-READY verification -> CLOSED.
- qa (TFL-275, 2026-10-01): FIX-READY verification **FAILED criterion (b)** - remains OPEN. Commands: `npm run test:e2e -- phase77_bookview_correction phase66_bookview_spread phase66_bookview_annotations phase66_bookview_colorpopover phase77_fix_def467` = 20 passed / 2 failed (only the two DEF-467 attack tests); `npm run test:unit -- bookView bookViewSpread bookViewAnnotations` = 3 files / 27 tests, 0 failed; `npm run verify` exit 0. Criterion (a) PASS: no `.annotation-layer-active` inside `[data-book-turn]`. Criterion (c) PASS: the mid-turn drag committed no annotation to the outgoing page (double: before=[] after=[], beforeOut=afterOut=0; single likewise). Criterion (b) FAIL: the mid-turn `elementFromPoint` at the outgoing page centre (double x=0.75*stage width, single x=0.5*stage width) resolves to the leaf's `.textLayer` (`pointer-events: auto`, `styles.css:4882` overrides the leaf's inherited `none`) which is INSIDE `[data-book-turn]` - the decorative leaf is still a live (text-selectable) hit surface. Probe points: double {(0.5,0.5) textLayer inTurn, (0.65,0.3) textLayer inTurn, (0.75,0.5) textLayer inTurn, (0.85,0.7) svg inTurn=false, (0.6,0.7) textLayer inTurn}; single {(0.5,0.5) textLayer inTurn, (0.65,0.3) svg false, (0.75,0.5) stage false, (0.85,0.7) stage false, (0.6,0.7) textLayer inTurn}. Residual routed to frontend-dev: make the leaf's `.textLayer` (and other page hit surfaces) inert inside `.book-view-turn`. Spec: `e2e/phase77_fix_def467.spec.cjs`; evidence log under the run scratch dir.
- qa (TFL-278, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY re-check **PASS** -> **CLOSED**. Residual fix TFL-276 adds `.book-view-turn, .book-view-turn * { pointer-events: none !important; }` (`styles.css:18735-18738`), which beats the descendant `.textLayer`/`.annotation-layer-active .annotation-svg` opt-ins by specificity. Command `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase77_bookview_correction.spec.cjs e2e/phase77_fix_def467.spec.cjs e2e/phase66_bookview_spread.spec.cjs e2e/phase66_bookview_annotations.spec.cjs e2e/phase66_bookview_colorpopover.spec.cjs` = **22 passed / 0 failed**. Criterion (a) PASS: no `.annotation-layer-active` in the leaf. ## DEF-477: At the 30-preset cap a newly-saved print preset is silently dropped on disk while the picker shows it as saved - a phantom entry that vanishes on reopen

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (silent loss of a user-created preset at the cap boundary; the success notice asserts a save the disk did not take; the in-session picker diverges from disk without bound)
- Found by: adversary (TFL-325, Phase 81 named-print-presets settings-persistence diff-pass; ACCEPTED from ADV-154)
- Phase: 81 (named print presets; success criterion 3 - the list is capped - and criterion 4 - no silent no-op)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Seed a fresh temp user-data `settings.json` with 30+ valid distinct-name `printPresets` (for example `p00`..`p49`), launch the dev build via `e2e/lib/launch.cjs`, open `report.pdf`, then the standalone print window.
2. Confirm the picker lists exactly 30 (`p00`..`p29`).
3. Save a NEW name via the real controls (`fill [data-print-preset-name] = "extra"` -> click `[data-print-preset-save]`), wait for the `[data-print-preset-notice]` success text, then read `settings.json` back.

Expected: the success notice, the picker and the persisted list agree. Per the phase contract `cap 30` is a persisted-list ceiling: saving a 31st distinct name is refused with a visible `[data-print-preset-error]` (writing nothing), or evicted predictably - but notice, picker and disk must never disagree, and the notice must not assert a save the disk did not take.

Actual: `savePreset` appends to its in-memory `presets` list and calls `savePresets(next)` without enforcing the cap; main's `normalizePrintPresets` truncates the written list to its first 30 entries, so the newest name never reaches disk. Measured after the first save: disk list = 30 (`extra` absent), picker = 31 (`extra` present), notice "Preset \"extra\" saved.". A second new name makes disk = 30 (both absent) and picker = 32. Every new preset saved while at the cap reports success, shows in the picker for the rest of the session, and is gone on the next launch - silent loss of user-created data with no page error.

Root cause: `src/renderer/components/usePrintControls.ts:488-510` (`savePreset`) has no `PRINT_PRESETS_CAP` guard before it appends/builds `next`; `src/main/services/settings.ts:1024` (`normalizePrintPresets`) then silently truncates the written list at `PRINT_PRESETS_CAP` (`src/main/services/settings.ts:326`, value 30). The renderer already mirrors the main cap literals (`PrintPanel.tsx:123` hard-codes `maxLength={40}` for `PRINT_PRESET_NAME_MAX`), so the guard belongs in the renderer.

Impact: MEDIUM - at the cap, every new preset save falsely reports success, silently losing a user-created preset and diverging the picker from disk without bound in-session. Narrow (30 presets already saved) but a genuine data-loss/no-silent-no-op violation of success criteria 3 and 4.

History:
- adversary (TFL-325, 2026-10-02): filed ADV-154 (suggested LOW).
- CTO (TFL-317, 2026-10-02): ACCEPTED -> DEF-477, severity raised to MEDIUM.
