## DEF-482: `[data-txt-spellcheck]` is inert in the panel - clicking it does not flip `aria-pressed`, does not hide the underlines, and never persists `spellCheck.enabled`

- Status: CLOSED (qa TFL-354, 2026-10-02)
- CTO (TFL-343, 2026-10-02): renumbered DEF-478 -> DEF-482 during the phase-close ledger review - DEF-478 was already held by the Phase 80 Format Painter defect (`DEFECTS.md:8`, CLOSED, itself renumbered from DEF-477 by CTO TFL-339). No source or test traceability referenced this entry's number; only the Phase 82 ledger/ADV cross-references were updated.
- Severity: HIGH (breaks the stated CONTROL-INDEX promise for the feature's only control, and phase success criteria 2 - `spellCheck` persists across a reload - and 3 - the toggle always changes a persisted state; the control visibly does nothing until the panel is remounted)
- Found by: qa (TFL-348, Phase 82 phase validation)
- qa (TFL-354, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY retest PASS -> CLOSED. Command: `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase82_spellcheck.spec.cjs --workers=1` = 5 passed / 0 failed. T3 in the EDIT-mode panel now logs `T3-toggle-off-evidence {"ariaAfter":"false","spansAfter":[],"statusOff":"Spell check off","persistedOff":false}` (aria flips, underlines clear immediately, readable status, `settings.json` persists false) and T5 on the annotation-textbox surface logs `ariaAfter:"false"` / `persistedValue:false` / `aria-pressed` back to `true` on re-enable. Fixes confirmed in tree: `src/renderer/App.tsx:10359-10369` (flip routed through `trackAndSave`) and `src/renderer/components/DocumentView.tsx:3728-3729` (`spellCheck` in `textSelectionKey`).
- Phase: 82 (offline spell check; CONTROL-INDEX `[data-txt-spellcheck]` / `[data-spell-status]`)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. `npm.cmd run build`, then launch the dev build through `e2e/lib/launch.cjs` (fresh temp user-data dir; the operator's settings.json is untouched).
2. Open `report.pdf`; enter Edit mode; arm "Add a text box"; drag to place it; the panel Text field `[data-txt-text]` is enabled and spell check is on by default.
3. Fill `[data-txt-text]` with `teh world`; wait for a `[data-spell-misspelled]` (the "teh" squiggle).
4. Click `[data-txt-spellcheck]`; wait 1.5s; read `aria-pressed`, the `[data-spell-misspelled]` set, `[data-spell-status]` text, and `settings.json`.

Expected: `aria-pressed` flips to `false`; the underlines disappear immediately; `[data-spell-status]` shows a readable "Spell check off"; `settings.json` gains `spellCheck.enabled=false`; a reload keeps it off.

Actual: `aria-pressed` stays `"true"`, the `"teh"` underline stays, `[data-spell-status]` is blank/absent, and `settings.json` never gains a `spellCheck` field (still `null` after an 8s poll). The in-memory preference DID change: after deselecting and reselecting the text target (panel remount) the same control reads `aria-pressed="false"`, no underlines, status `"Spell check off"`. Reproduced on both the Edit-mode board and the annotation-textbox (floating-card) surface: T5 shows the same inert click, then `ariaAfterRemount:"false"` / `spansAfterRemount:[]`.

Root cause (from source): the published Inspector snapshot key `textSelectionKey` (`src/renderer/components/DocumentView.tsx:3716-3728`) does not include `spellCheck`, so the `useLayoutEffect` that republishes the snapshot (`:3734-3738`) never fires on a spell-check flip - the re-parented text panel keeps the stale `spellCheck` object (`Inspector.tsx:203` -> `<TextPropertiesPanel {...textPanel}/>`) until it remounts. Separately, App's `onSpellCheckEnabledChange` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:10359-10365`) calls `setSettings` without `trackAndSave` (there is no generic settings-persist effect), so the flip is never written to `settings.json`.

Evidence: `e2e/phase82_spellcheck.spec.cjs` T3 (`T3-toggle-off-evidence {"ariaAfter":"true","spansAfter":["teh"],"statusOff":"","persistedOff":null}`) and T5 (`T5-toggle-evidence {...ariaAfter:"true"...persistedValue:null...}` / `T5-remount-probe {"ariaAfterRemount":"false","spansAfterRemount":[]}`); screenshots `screenshots/phase82-spell-status-editmode.png` (edit-mode, click did nothing) and `screenshots/phase82-spell-status.png` (status only appears after remount).

Impact: HIGH - the feature cannot be turned off from the UI (the underlines never hide until the panel remounts) and the preference never survives a restart, violating phase criteria 2 and 3 and the CONTROL-INDEX `[data-txt-spellcheck]` promised action.

## DEF-479: The bundled dictionary lacks very common words, so correctly spelled common words are underlined as misspelled

- Status: CLOSED (qa TFL-354, 2026-10-02)
- Severity: MEDIUM (false-positive squiggles on everyday vocabulary materially degrade the feature and violate the CONTROL-INDEX promise that "a known word is not [underlined]")
- Found by: qa (TFL-348, Phase 82 phase validation; observed while executing the task's literal scenario 2a phrase "teh cat sat")
- qa (TFL-354, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY retest PASS -> CLOSED. Command: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/spellCommonWords.test.ts` (green within `npm.cmd run test:unit -- <phase 82 set>` = 9 files / 281 tests passed) and `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase82_spellcheck.spec.cjs --workers=1` (5 passed). The bundled `assets/dictionary/en-us.txt` now holds 65,456 words and contains cat/sat/dog/run/file/page/word/hello/blue/pdf; e2e T2 logs `T2-spans ["teh"]` for "teh cat sat" and T1 logs `T1-spans ["teh"]` for "teh world".
- Phase: 82 (offline spell check; feature A dictionary + CONTROL-INDEX `[data-spell-misspelled]`)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. Open `report.pdf`; enter Edit mode; place a text box; type `teh cat sat` in `[data-txt-text]`.
2. Wait for the squiggles.

Expected (the task's literal 2a expectation and the CONTROL-INDEX promise "a known misspelling is underlined, a known word is not"): only `teh` is underlined.

Actual: `[data-spell-misspelled]` = `["teh","cat","sat"]` - every word is flagged. The bundled list is the zxcvbn `english_wikipedia` frequency list (`assets/dictionary/LICENSE.txt`); a 20-word sample of common English shows 10 absent: `cat`, `sat`, `dog`, `run`, `file`, `page`, `word`, `spell`, `check`, `hello`, `blue`, `pdf`. Words that ARE present (`the`, `world`, `text`, `document`, `red`, `house`) behave correctly.

Evidence: `e2e/phase82_spellcheck.spec.cjs` T2 (`T2-spans ["teh","cat","sat"]`, hard assertion "only `teh` should be flagged" fails) and T1 (with dictionary words `teh world` the misspelled set is exactly `["teh"]`, proving the mechanism itself).

Impact: MEDIUM - users editing ordinary prose see widespread spurious underlines; the CONTROL-INDEX `[data-spell-misspelled]` "a known word is not [underlined]" action does not hold for common vocabulary. Fix is a data/coverage decision for the CTO (augment the bundled list or curate it), not a code change qa may make.

## DEF-480: `settings.changed` echo filter ignores `spellCheck`, so a stale echo can revert the user's spell-check toggle (DEF-072 class reopen)

- Status: CLOSED (qa TFL-354, 2026-10-02)
- Severity: MEDIUM (a stale echo whose only drift is `spellCheck` passes the filter and reverts the user's latest toggle; reopens the DEF-072 invariant the `settingsEcho.ts` header declares closed)
- Found by: adversary (TFL-352, Phase 82 diff-pass; ADV-156 accepted by CTO on triage)
- qa (TFL-354, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY retest PASS -> CLOSED. Command: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts test/unit/renderer/settingsEcho.test.ts` = 2 files / 83 tests passed. The adv spec now pins the FIXED behaviour: `sameSettings({spellCheck:on},{spellCheck:off}) === false` and `shouldApplyEcho(staleEcho(spellCheck:off), writeSeq=2, persisted(spellCheck:on)) === false`. Fixes confirmed: `src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts` guards `spellCheck` in `sameSettings` (:98), `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` (:134) and `differsOnlyInGeometry` (:244); `settingsEcho.test.ts` DEF-072 field-coverage guard passes with `spellCheck` present.
- Phase: 82 (offline spell check; C1 contract + DEF-482 fix delta)
- Source: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-156

Root cause: `src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts` compares every `AppSettings` field in `sameSettings` (:81-98), `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` (:111-138) and `differsOnlyInGeometry` (:212-233) - except the new `AppSettings.spellCheck` (`src/shared/types.ts:249`). `App.tsx:1310-1319` calls `shouldApplyEcho` on every `settings.changed` payload and on `true` runs `setSettings(echo)` wholesale. Repro pinned by `test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts` (5 passed): `sameSettings({spellCheck:on},{spellCheck:off}) === true` and `shouldApplyEcho(staleEcho(spellCheck:off), writeSeq=2, persisted(spellCheck:on)) === true`. The DEF-072 coverage guard (`settingsEcho.test.ts:905-957`) lists every optional field but not `spellCheck`, so it passes silently.

Expected: `sameSettings` returns false when only `spellCheck` differs; `shouldApplyEcho` discards a stale echo whose only drift is `spellCheck`, so the user's latest flip survives.

Evidence: `test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts`; `src/renderer/state/settingsEcho.ts`; `src/renderer/App.tsx:1256-1260,1310-1319`.

Fix owner: frontend-dev. Suggested fix: add a `spellCheck` comparison (`enabled` and `language`) to `sameSettings`, `differsOnlyInRecentFiles` and `differsOnlyInGeometry`, and add `spellCheck` to the DEF-072 `requiredFields` coverage list in `settingsEcho.test.ts`.

## DEF-481: a misspelled token with no suggestions opens an empty suggestion popover

- Status: CLOSED (qa TFL-354, 2026-10-02)
- Severity: LOW (a context-menu action opens a `[data-spell-suggest]` listbox with zero options and no message; violates the "never an empty popover" rule)
- Found by: adversary (TFL-352, Phase 82 diff-pass; ADV-157 accepted by CTO on triage)
- qa (TFL-354, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY retest PASS -> CLOSED. Command: `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/spellCheckTextarea.test.tsx` = 1 file / 5 tests passed. The spec "does not open an empty suggestion popover when there are no candidates" asserts a 46-char `q` run is flagged misspelled (`[data-spell-misspelled]` length 1) yet `[data-spell-suggest]` is null. Fix confirmed: `src/renderer/spell/SpellCheckTextarea.tsx:223` returns before `preventDefault`. e2e T1 additionally asserts no blank popover on a correctly spelled word.
- Phase: 82 (offline spell check; C2 UI, SpellCheckTextarea)
- Source: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-157

Root cause: `SpellCheckTextarea.handleContextMenu` (`src/renderer/spell/SpellCheckTextarea.tsx:201-231`) calls `e.preventDefault()` and opens the popover whenever the token is misspelled, regardless of `suggestions.length`. A misspelled token with zero candidates (e.g. a 46-char run of `q`, under `SPELL_WORD_MAX = 48`) therefore paints `[data-spell-suggest]` with zero `[data-spell-suggestion]` children (:317-340).

Expected: when the computed `suggestions` array is empty, return before `preventDefault` so the native menu shows, or render a single disabled "No suggestions" row.

Evidence: `test/unit/renderer/adv_phase82_settingsEcho.test.ts` ("ADV-157 repro"); `src/renderer/spell/SpellCheckTextarea.tsx:201-231,317-340`; `src/shared/spell.ts:160-186`.

Fix owner: frontend-dev. Suggested fix: in `handleContextMenu`, when `suggestions` is empty either return before `preventDefault` (native menu) or render a disabled "No suggestions" row, never an empty listbox.

## DEF-483: `[data-print-poster-scale]` is a silent no-op - changing Scale (%) never affects the poster preview or the composed/printed output

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (a Phase-83 CONTROL-INDEX control whose promised action - "(per-tile scale percent)" - is never applied; the preview, the tile crop and the composed PDF are byte-identical at 100% and 500%, so the control silently does nothing rather than fail loud)
- Found by: qa (TFL-359, Phase 83 phase validation; observed during the CONTROL-INDEX sweep while probing the poster path)
- Phase: 83 (Booklet + Poster imposition; CONTROL-INDEX `[data-print-poster-scale]` / CTO ruling 6 "One selected page is scaled to `posterScalePercent`")

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. Open `report.pdf`, open the print window, set Layout = Poster, page range Custom `1`, Rows = 2, Columns = 2, Cut marks on, Scale (%) = 100. Click Print (virtual-PDF destination).
2. Re-run the same with Scale (%) = 500. Compare the two composed sheet documents / produced PDFs.

Expected: the composed/printed tiles scale with `posterScalePercent` (100% -> 500% is visibly different), per the CONTROL-INDEX promise and CTO ruling 6.

Actual: the two composed documents are identical - `scaleAffectsOutput: false`; the renderer's `posterTiles`/`cropPosterTiles` derive only the grid+overlap rectangles, `composePrintHtml` never reads `settings.posterScalePercent`, and `mapPrintToPdfOptions` sets `scale` only from the `single`-path `scaling: 'custom'` `scalePercent`. The value is validated (`print.ts:264`), clamped/seeded (`printSettings.ts:170,273`) and persisted (`settings.ts:1020`), but never consumed by any compose/crop/preview path (grep of `src/**` shows no read outside validation/seed/persist).

Evidence: `e2e/phase83_imposition.spec.cjs` test 2 log `[p83|poster-scale-probe] {"scale100":100,"scale500":500,"scaleAffectsOutput":false}` (identical `composed.imgs` for both runs); both produced PDFs 4 portrait pages. Source: `src/renderer/components/usePrintControls.ts:459-467` (`posterTiles`), `:145-180` (`cropPosterTiles`), `src/main/services/print.ts:420-525` (`composePrintHtml`), `:356-372` (`mapPrintToPdfOptions`).

Impact: MEDIUM - the poster feature cannot be scaled from the UI; a promised control is inert. Does not corrupt output. Fix owner: frontend-dev (apply `posterScalePercent` to the poster tile crop and/or the composed sheet, and to the preview).

History:
- qa: opened (TFL-359, Phase 83 phase validation)
- orchestrator: FIX-READY - frontend-dev (TFL-360) reports: added the ONE shared pure derivation `posterTileRects(scale, rows, cols, overlapFraction)` (unit grid rects divided by S = the ORIGINAL-page region each tile samples) and `posterTileCanvasBox(tile, wPx, hPx, scale)` (pixel sample box + draw target enlarged by S) in `src/renderer/pdf/printSettings.ts`; `usePrintControls.ts` now derives `posterTiles` and `cropPosterTiles` from them and passes the same S in `onConfirmPrint`; `PrintPanel.tsx` preview zooms from the same derived rects (preview/print cannot disagree); test `printSettings - DEF-483 poster scale magnifies the tile derivation` added. verify clean (tsc 0); 3 files / 47 tests passed / 0 failed. Awaiting qa re-verification.
- qa (TFL-371, 2026-10-02): FIX-READY retest PASS -> CLOSED. Fresh `npm.cmd run build` (exit 0), then `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase83_imposition.spec.cjs` = 2 passed / 0 failed; the print-path scale probe printed `[p83|poster-scale-probe] {"scale100":100,"scale500":500,"scaleAffectsOutput":true}` and the new hard assertion `expect(scaleAffectsOutput).toBe(true)` passed. `posterTileRects`/`posterTileCanvasBox` are also covered by `printSettings.test.ts` in the 5-file / 183-test phase unit set (0 failed).

## DEF-484: Booklet creep under subset `both` (the default) is derived from the side count in the main compose but from the physical-sheet count in the preview, so printed creep disagrees with the preview

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (real break of the shared-source-of-truth rule, Phase 83 CTO ruling 2 - the preview and the main compose disagree on booklet creep for the default subset `both`)
- Found by: adversary (ADV-158, Phase 83 diff-pass; accepted by CTO)

2. In the preview read the per-side `padding-left` values; and run the same settings through the main compose (`composePrintHtml`) and read its per-cell `padding-left`.

Expected: byte-for-byte the same margins in preview and compose (CTO ruling 2: the shared `bookletSideOffset` is consumed by BOTH so they can never disagree; e2e for 16 pages expects `[0,10,10,0]` per physical sheet).

Subsets `front`/`back` agreed; only the default `both` disagreed.

Evidence: ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-158; `src/main/services/print.ts:441-446`; `src/renderer/components/usePrintControls.ts` (`bookletSides`).

Impact: MEDIUM - the printed creep is wrong for the default booklet subset and disagrees with the preview. Fix owner: backend-dev (derive the physical-sheet count/index for `both` in `composePrintHtml`).

History:
- qa: filed from ADV-158
- qa (TFL-371, 2026-10-02): CLOSED. Phase unit set `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/main/printImposition.test.ts test/unit/main/print.test.ts test/unit/main/printPresets.test.ts test/unit/renderer/printSettings.test.ts test/unit/renderer/printDialog.test.tsx` = 5 files / 183 tests passed / 0 failed, after a fresh `npm.cmd run build`. `test/unit/main/print.test.ts:677` "matches the renderer preview creep for subset both" asserts 16 pages, gutter 0, creep 10 -> per-side `[0,0,10,10,10,10,0,0]`, matching the renderer `bookletSides`; `print.ts:450-456` now offsets by PHYSICAL sheet for `both` (`sheetIndex = floor(i/2)`, `sheetCount = sheets.length/2`).

## DEF-485: A Page order set under Single/N-up leaks into Booklet - the compose stacks the 2-up sheet 1x2 or mirrors the page pair, while the control is shown disabled and the preview is always two columns

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH (real break of ruling 7 "non-applicable controls are disabled, not silently applied" AND ruling 2 preview/compose agreement - a disabled control changes the output)
- Found by: adversary (ADV-159, Phase 83 diff-pass; accepted by CTO)
- Phase: 83 (Booklet + Poster imposition; stale `pageOrder` carried into booklet settings)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. In Single layout set N-up = 4 and Page order = Vertical reversed, then switch Layout to Booklet (the Page order select is now disabled but retains its value).
2. Compose a booklet payload (`images:[A,B]`, `settings:{layoutMode:'booklet', pagesPerSheet:2, pageOrder:'verticalReversed'}`) and inspect the emitted grid and image DOM order. Vary the order across `vertical`/`verticalReversed`/`horizontalReversed`.

Expected: Booklet is a fixed 2-column landscape imposition; the disabled Page order control must not affect it (rulings 7 and 2).

Actual: for `vertical`/`verticalReversed` the composed grid became `grid-template-columns: repeat(1,...); grid-template-rows: repeat(2,...)` - a 1x2 stacked sheet. Impact: HIGH - the booklet imposition can be silently wrong (stacked/mirrored) while the UI claims the ordering controls are disabled. Fix owner: backend-dev (force the fixed horizontal 2-up layout in booklet compose; renderer must not carry a stale `pageOrder`).

History:
- qa: filed from ADV-159
- qa (TFL-371, 2026-10-02): CLOSED. `test/unit/main/print.test.ts:716` "ignores a stale pageOrder and stays a fixed 2-column 2-up" asserts that for `vertical`/`verticalReversed`/`horizontalReversed` the compose keeps `grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr)` / `grid-template-rows: repeat(1, 1fr)` and image order `['A','B']`; `print.ts:437-440` forces the fixed booklet `{cols:2,rows:1,slots:[0,1]}` layout and `printSettings.ts:244-246,338-349` force `pageOrder:'horizontal'` in both `buildPrintSettings` and `seedPrintDialogState`. Phase unit set 5 files / 183 tests passed; the e2e booklet preview (`screenshots/phase83-booklet-preview.png`) shows the fixed 2-up sides.

## DEF-501: Live `exportText` still returns a page removed by "Remove blank pages" (ignores doc.order/deleted)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (degrades the Export Text / XLSX / PPTX text-export workflows with wrong, duplicated text; saved PDFs are correct, so there is no document corruption)
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 87 (FEA-039 Remove blank pages; Phase 87 qa phase-validation gate)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. Open a document and remove a blank page through the PAGES panel -> "Remove blank pages..." -> Scan -> Remove N selected.
2. Read `await window.tflex.engine.getState(docId)` -> `pageCount` is 3 (removal applied).
3. Read `await window.tflex.engine.exportText(docId)` -> returns 4 pages, still including the removed page 2.

Expected: after the removal the live engine's `exportText` reflects the visible order and returns the 3 surviving pages (as the Phase 87 criterion requires and as the saved/reloaded file already does).

Actual: `_exportTextImpl` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:2290-2295`) serialises `doc.pdfDoc` directly and iterates `doc.pdfDoc.getPageCount()`; it never consults `doc.order`/`doc.deleted`, so deleted pages are still exported. On the 4-page Phase 87 fixture (page 2 truly blank) it returned `["ONE","THREE","THREE","FOUR"]` after removing page 2, whereas the same document saved and reopened correctly yields `["ONE","THREE","FOUR"]` (3 pages). `serializeDoc` (`engine.ts:6266-6315`) DOES honour `doc.order`, so save/saveAs/`getDocumentBytes` are correct; only the live `exportText` channel is stale. This is a pre-existing `exportText` limitation (documented in `test/unit/main/phase87BlankPagesEngine.test.ts:8-13`, which reloads via `getDocumentBytes` instead), exposed now because the Phase 87 criterion accepts live `exportText` as its oracle. It also affects every other page-deleting op, and the XLSX/PPTX/TXT export writers that read `engine.exportText`.

Evidence: `e2e/phase87_blank_pages.spec.cjs` P87-CORE -> `[p87|exportText-after-removal] ["p1:ONE","p2:THREE","p3:THREE","p4:FOUR"]` vs `[p87|exportText-after-reload] ["p1:ONE","p2:THREE","p3:FOUR"]`; `getState.pageCount` 3 at both points. Screenshot `screenshots/phase87_after_removal.png`.

Impact: MEDIUM - "Export Text" and the XLSX/PPTX writers emit a removed page (and a duplicated neighbour's text) until the document is saved/reloaded. Fix owner: backend-dev (make `_exportTextImpl` iterate `doc.order` and index `extractTextFromRawPdf` by the original index, matching `createDocxFromDoc`). After a fix, the Phase 87 P87-CORE assertion `expect(afterPages.length).toBe(3)` will pass.

History:
- qa (TFL-441, 2026-10-03): filed from the Phase 87 phase-validation e2e. P87-CORE reports FAIL on criterion 3's `exportText` page-count clause; criteria 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and the live-engine refusal checks pass.
- qa (TFL-447, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. `_exportTextImpl` now iterates `doc.order` and indexes `extractTextFromRawPdf` by the original index. Phase 87 e2e P87-CORE re-run returns `exportText-after-removal ["p1:ONE","p2:THREE","p3:FOUR"]` (3 pages) and the spec's `expect(afterPages.length).toBe(3)` passes; engine spec `DEF-501: exportText honours doc.order after a delete` passes; 4/4 e2e, 307/307 unit, verify exit 0.

## DEF-502: Remove-blank-pages dialog keeps a stale checked page after the threshold is tightened, so Confirm deletes a page that is no longer a candidate

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH (a non-blank, no-longer-candidate page can be removed without being visible or selected)
- Found by: adversary (ADV-169)
- Phase: 87 (FEA-039 Remove blank pages; adversarial diff-pass TFL-442)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. Open a document; run the blank-page scan with threshold 0.005 so page 1 (measured 0.4% ink) is the only candidate and is pre-checked.
2. Lower `[data-blank-scan-threshold]` to 0.001 (below page 1's measured coverage) WITHOUT re-scanning. The candidate list empties and `[data-blank-scan-report]` reads "No blank pages found."
3. Click `[data-blank-scan-confirm]`.

Expected: the confirm control reflects the CURRENT candidate selection; with zero candidates it is disabled and removes nothing.

Actual: the button still reads "Remove N selected" and is enabled; clicking it hands the stale checked page to the host, which calls `engine.removeBlankPages` and deletes page 1. Root cause: `checked` is seeded only when `measurements` changes (`BlankPagesDialog.tsx:60-66`) while `candidates` reclassifies on `[measurements, threshold]` (`:51-54`), and `onConfirmClick` sends the stale `[...checked]` (`:99-101`). Related UX defects raised in the same pass: after a successful removal the dialog stays open with stale checked rows (a second Confirm then errors), and the threshold input coerces `Number()` on every keystroke (`:158`) so intermediate decimals cannot be typed and out-of-range values are accepted in-session.

Evidence: adversary probe `test-fixtures/adv442/adv442_dialog.probe.test.tsx` (passes, encoding the bug): confirm text "Remove 1 selected", disabled false, `onConfirm payload: [[[1]]]`.

Impact: HIGH - silent deletion of a page the user excluded. Fix owner: frontend-dev. Fix must intersect the checked set with the current candidates on every threshold change (or key checked state to `(measurements, threshold)`), make the confirm control derive its count/enabled state from the current candidates, and reset/close on a successful removal.

History:
- adversary (TFL-442, 2026-10-03): filed as ADV-169, suggested HIGH; CTO accepted it as DEF-502 and routed it to frontend-dev.
- qa (TFL-447, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. `BlankPagesDialog` now derives the confirm count/enabled state from `effectiveChecked` (checked set intersected with the current candidates); the threshold input keeps a raw string and commits a clamped `[0,1]` value on blur/Enter. Unit `never confirms a checked page that is no longer a candidate (DEF-502)` passes: threshold 0.005 with page 1 at 0.4% -> enabled "Remove 1 selected"; same measurements at 0.001 -> 0 candidates, disabled "Remove 0 selected", click does not call `onConfirm`. Clamp tests (`on Enter`, `above 1`, `below 0`) pass; Phase 87 e2e 4/4 green with the new blur-commit input.

## DEF-503: A batch remove-blank-pages leaves annotations on surviving pages reporting their OLD visible page

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (the annotation overlay paints on the wrong visible page until a save/reload re-derives pages from /Annots)
- Found by: adversary (ADV-170)
- Phase: 87 (FEA-039 Remove blank pages; adversarial diff-pass TFL-442)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch):
1. Open a 4-page document; on visible page 3 add one annotation, one text box and one placed signature.
2. Run Remove blank pages and delete visible page 1 (old visible page 3 becomes visible page 2).

Expected: every page-anchored model is renumbered to the new visible page, exactly as the delete bookkeeping promises: `textBoxes` and `placedSignatures` move from page 3 to page 2, so the annotation does too.

Actual: `box.page` and `sig.page` become 2, but `ann.page` stays 3 while `pageCount` is 3. Root cause: `applyOpToDoc`'s delete case (`engine.ts:5347-5389`) drops annotations for the deleted page via `dropPageAnnotations` and shifts the signature/text-box registries, but never renumbers annotations on surviving pages; `buildState` (`engine.ts:5167-5175`) flattens `doc.annotations[origIdx]` verbatim. The renderer groups by `a.page` (`DocumentView.tsx:3559-3570`), so the overlay paints on the wrong visible page. INHERITED: the pre-existing single `engine.applyOp({kind:'delete'})` shows the same, and the Phase 87 batch inherits it by reusing `applyOpToDoc`.

Evidence: adversary probe `test-fixtures/adv442/adv442_engine.probe.test.ts` (1 failing assertion): `ann.page = [{"id":"ann-p3","page":3}]` while `pageCount = 3`, vs `box.page`/`sig.page` = 2. Also a spec-coverage gap: `test/unit/main/phase87BlankPagesEngine.test.ts` never creates an annotation.

Impact: MEDIUM - page-numbering/navigation correctness on any page deletion. Fix owner: backend-dev. Fix must shift annotations on surviving pages with the same `deletedVisiblePage` logic as signatures/text boxes (and correct `doc.annotations` indexing), and the Phase 87 engine spec must add an annotation case.

History:
- adversary (TFL-442, 2026-10-03): filed as ADV-170, suggested MEDIUM; CTO accepted it as DEF-503 and routed to backend-dev.
- qa (TFL-447, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. `buildState` now rewrites each flattened annotation's `page` to its current visible page (`vi + 1`). Engine spec `DEF-503: after a delete, flattened annotations carry the current visible page` passes: annotation, text box and placed signature created on visible page 3 all report page 2 after removing visible page 1, pageCount 3; the spec-coverage gap (no annotation case) is now covered. 4/4 e2e, 307/307 unit, verify exit 0.

## DEF-504: `npm run build:renderer` fails: postcss cannot resolve the `@fontsource-variable/inter` CSS import, so no renderer bundle is produced

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: HIGH (a broken renderer build produces no bundle, so the Phase 89 e2e and packaging/release gate cannot run against a fresh build)
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 89 (FEA-033 Bates numbering; focused frontend verification TFL-473)

Steps to reproduce (from repository root):
1. Run `npm.cmd run build:renderer`.
2. Observe exit 1 and the postcss `@import` resolution error.

Expected: exit 0 and a renderer bundle produced under the build output (the phase e2e/packaging gate requires a fresh renderer bundle).

Actual (verbatim, excerpt):
```
vite v8.2.2 building client environment for production...
transforming...
Unable to resolve `@import "@fontsource-variable/inter/index.css"` from C:/Users/tanzi/OneDrive/App Development/TFlex/src/renderer
233 modules transformed.
Build failed in 154ms
error during build:
Build failed with 1 error:

[plugin vite:css] C:/Users/tanzi/OneDrive/App Development/TFlex/src/renderer/styles.css:undefined:NaN
Error: [postcss] ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'C:\Users\tanzi\OneDrive\App Development\TFlex\@fontsource-variable\inter\index.css'
```

The package IS installed (`node_modules/@fontsource-variable/inter/index.css` exists; declared in `package.json:29` as `"@fontsource-variable/inter": "^5.2.5"`), but `postcss-import` resolves the bare specifier against the project root (`<root>\@fontsource-variable\inter\index.css`) instead of `node_modules`. The renderer TEST toolchain was fixed for the same class of resolver problem via `vitest.config.ts` `resolve: { preserveSymlinks: true }`; the production `vite build` CSS path has no equivalent fix. `src/renderer/styles.css:9` (`@import url("@fontsource-variable/inter/index.css");`) is pre-existing (not touched by the Phase 89/88 diffs), so this is a pre-existing build gap surfaced by the phase gate, not a Bates regression.

Evidence: `npm.cmd run build:renderer` exit 1 (full output in the TFL-473 artifact); contrast item 4 `npm.cmd run verify` exit 0.

Impact: HIGH. With no renderer bundle, the Phase 89 e2e/packaging gate cannot run on a fresh build. Fix owner: frontend-dev / frontend toolchain owner (resolve the font import for the production CSS pipeline, e.g. import the CSS from TS or adjust the resolver). The QA task that found this must not edit config to make it pass.

History:
- qa (TFL-473, 2026-10-03): filed from the Phase 89 frontend focused verification (item 5 / verdict f). The four unit/verify commands passed (2/2 files 27 tests, 4/4 files 56 tests, watermark 1/1 8 tests, verify exit 0); only the renderer build fails.
- qa (TFL-478, 2026-10-03): CLOSED on the Phase 89 phase-validation gate. The TFL-474 fix landed (`vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` carry `resolve.preserveSymlinks: true`) and `npm.cmd run build` now exits 0 on a clean tree: typecheck + `vite build` (renderer bundle produced, `dist/renderer/assets/index-*.js` + `index-*.css`) + `build:node`, EXIT=0. Regression: `npm.cmd run verify` exit 0. (Note: there is a pre-existing duplicate DEF-504 id for a closed Phase 86 entry above; this closure targets the Phase 89 build entry.)
- CTO (TFL-463, 2026-10-03): Phase 88 phase-close commit `4629c4f458ada2a69477782e6fd81275d0073f32` carried the `vite.config.ts` half of this fix (needed to unblock Phase 88's TFL-471 renderer build). The still-uncommitted `vitest.config.ts` sibling change stays with this Phase 89 entry and must ride the Phase 89 close commit - it is not Phase 88 work.

## DEF-508: Bates dialog resets `[data-bates-report]` to "Not applied yet." (and the page scope) right after an apply that persists changed defaults

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: MEDIUM (the stamp/refusal is correct and a toast reports it, but the dialog's promised report is wrong after any apply that changes the remembered defaults - the normal first-use case - breaking the phase's report acceptance criterion; no document corruption or data loss)
- Found by: qa
- Phase: 89 (FEA-033 Bates numbering; phase validation TFL-478)

Steps to reproduce (from application launch, clean profile):
1. Launch TFlex and open a multi-page PDF (4-page fixture, one large word per page).
2. Press Ctrl+3 (REVIEW) and click the Action Dock verb "Bates numbering..." (`[data-dock-verb="bates"]`).
3. Set Prefix `BATES-`, Start 7, Padding 5; uncheck "All pages", set From 2 To 3; click "Apply numbering".
4. Expected: `[data-bates-report]` shows `2 pages stamped: BATES-00007, BATES-00008`.
   Actual: it briefly shows that text, then resets to `Not applied yet.`; the Pages scope also re-seeds to "All pages" / From 1 / To 1.
5. Refusal variant: set Prefix to an unencodable character (`漢`) and Apply.
   Expected: the report keeps the readable `... cannot encode "漢" ...` error.
   Actual: the error appears then resets to `Not applied yet.`.

Observed report transitions (MutationObserver on `[data-bates-report]`):
```
["Not applied yet.", "2 pages stamped: BATES-00007, BATES-00008", "Not applied yet."]
["Not applied yet.", "Engine error: addBates: the Helvetica font cannot encode \"漢\" in the stamp label", "Not applied yet."]
```

Expected (CONTROL-INDEX): "`[data-bates-report]` - readable 'N pages stamped' plus the labels, or the refusal text - never blank after a run."

Actual: the report is not blank, it is reset to the pre-apply placeholder `Not applied yet.` after the apply settles, so the promised success/refusal text cannot be read in the dialog.

Root cause (read-only inspection): `onBatesConfirm` (`src/renderer/App.tsx:6392`) calls `onBatesDefaultsChange` before returning, which writes the changed defaults to `AppSettings.batesDefaults`; that changes the `batesDefaults` useMemo identity (`App.tsx:9971`) and therefore the `initialDefaults` prop. `BatesDialog`'s re-seed `useEffect` keyed on `[open, initialDefaults, currentPage, totalPages]` (`src/renderer/components/BatesDialog.tsx:163-177`) then re-runs and calls `setReport(null)`, `setReportError(false)`, `setApplying(false)`, `setRangeAll(true)`. When the chosen values already equal the remembered defaults (e.g. a second identical apply) no settings write occurs and the report stays.

Evidence:
- `e2e/phase89_bates.spec.cjs` test `P89-REPORT` FAILs on `expect.soft(current).toContain('2 pages stamped')` and on the refusal text (`current === "Not applied yet."`).
- Live engine content IS correct: `exportText` page 2 = `"BRAVOBATES-00007"`, page 3 = `"CHARLIEBATES-00008"`; pages 1 and 4 unchanged (so the defect is the report, not the stamp).
- Screenshot: `screenshots/phase89_report_after_apply.png` (dialog re-seeded to All pages; only the toast "Bates numbers applied." visible).

Fix owner: frontend-dev. Suggested direction: seed the dialog only on the `open` rising edge (do not re-seed on `initialDefaults` identity changes while open), or do not persist defaults synchronously inside the confirm path.

History:
- qa (TFL-483, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. Fix authored by frontend-dev on TFL-480 (`src/renderer/components/BatesDialog.tsx` re-seed effect now runs only on the rising edge of `open` via a new `seededForOpenRef` edge guard; new unit assertion in `test/unit/renderer/phase89BatesDialog.test.tsx`). Independent re-run of the fix-verify commands: `npm.cmd run build` exit 0 (typecheck + `vite build` renderer bundle `dist/renderer/assets/index-Bf0viocg.js` + `index-P70DfLll.css` + `build:node`); `npm.cmd run test:e2e -- e2e/phase89_bates.spec.cjs` 7 passed / 0 failed (P89-REPORT now PASS: report-current = `2 pages stamped: BATES-00007, BATES-00008`, refusal-current = `Engine error: addBates: the Helvetica font cannot encode "漢" in the stamp label`); `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase89BatesDialog.test.tsx` 1 file / 8 tests passed; `npm.cmd run verify` conventions clean (338 source files) + tsc clean, exit 0. Fix is minimal (`seededForOpenRef` present only in BatesDialog.tsx; no src/main, src/shared, src/preload, config or e2e/spec edits in the fix) and the fresh-open re-seed is preserved (unit close->reopen assertion restores the `Not applied yet.` placeholder + all-pages scope).

"Helvetica"` (`src/renderer/components/BatesDialog.tsx:57,234`); `App.tsx:11750` passes `defaultFont={settings?.editDefaultFont ?? "Helvetica"}`. `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/renderer/phase89BatesDialog.test.tsx` -> Test Files 1 passed / Tests 9 passed, including the new assertion at `phase89BatesDialog.test.tsx:144-150` that mounts `defaultFont: "Times"` and asserts the payload `font === "Times"`.

## DEF-513: The Bates encodability pre-check is font-agnostic - a bundled font over-refuses Latin-Extended/Greek labels it can actually draw (ADV-180)

- Status: CLOSED
- Severity: LOW
- Found by: adversary (ADV-180)
- Phase: 89 (FEA-033 Bates numbering; phase issue TFL-464)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build a one-page fixture; call `engine.addBates` with `{ pages: [1], font: "DejaVu Serif", prefix: "\u03a9" }` (or `prefix: "\u0101"`).
2. Inspect the Result.

Expected: REQUIREMENTS.md:5333 (Phase 89 item 6) - the refusal is for a character the **chosen** font cannot encode; a bundled family that embeds as a real TTF should accept the characters it can draw.

Actual: the pre-check calls `undrawableStandardFontChars(label)` (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4364-4372`), built on `sanitizeForStandardFont` (`:5208-5246`), which unconditionally drops every code point > 0xFF. It refuses `\u03a9`/`\u0101` with DejaVu Serif even though the embedded font draws both (verified glyph ids 1/2; `\u4e16` -> .notdef). Over-refusal only - the op is all-or-nothing and leaves the bytes unchanged. Reachable through the IPC channel; no font control exists in the shipped dialog.

Evidence: adversary diff-pass TFL-484 (ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md ADV-180); `test/unit/main/phase89BatesAdversary.test.ts` A4b/A5c (observation-only) logs.

Fix owner: backend-dev. Suggested direction: make the pre-check use the font that will actually be embedded - keep the WinAnsi check for a StandardFont family, and for a bundled family probe the font's real glyph coverage (`.notdef`/throw = unencodable) before any mutation, then refuse only the truly-undrawable characters.

History:
- CTO (TFL-464, 2026-10-03): ACCEPTED from ADV-180 (adversary diff-pass TFL-484). Assigned backend-dev (font-aware encodability pre-check).
- qa (TFL-492, 2026-10-03): CLOSED. Independent phase-close verification. Source: `_addBatesImpl` resolves `fontFamily = settings.font ?? DEFAULT_SETTINGS.editDefaultFont ?? 'Helvetica'`, validates `isEditFont`, keeps the WinAnsi check for StandardFont families, and for a bundled family probes a throwaway `PDFDocument.create()` for real glyph coverage (`src/main/services/engine.ts:4370-4399`, helper `bundledFontUnencodableChars` :5284). `npm.cmd run test:unit -- test/unit/shared/bates.test.ts test/unit/main/phase89BatesSettings.test.ts test/unit/main/phase89BatesEngine.test.ts` -> Test Files 3 passed / Tests 26 passed, including the two new DEF-513 cases (`phase89BatesEngine.test.ts:194` U+03A9 and `:219` U+0101) and the unchanged `:243` default-font U+6587 refusal (engine-error, bytes byte-for-byte unchanged, no undo entry).

## DEF-524: Phase 92 chunk-E1 EncryptDialog adoption dropped the shipped busy guard on the header close X; Esc now dismisses the encrypt dialog while encryption is in flight

- Status: CLOSED (duplicate of the canonical DEF-524 entry at the top of this ledger; closed there via TFL-615)
- Severity: MEDIUM - a shipped disabled/busy condition was dropped (TFL-610 brief line 44: "Preserve every disabled/busy condition"). The busy document-operation dialog can now be dismissed via two paths (header X and Esc); the encrypt still completes, so there is no corruption or data loss.
- Found by: qa (TFL-611)
- Phase: 92 (TFL-513 chunk E1, delivered as TFL-610)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Launch the dev app and open `report.pdf`.
2. Deliver stage -> Encrypt document (or Ctrl+K -> "Encrypt document").
3. Observe the header close X while `busy` is true (or inspect the adopted source).

Expected: the header close X is disabled while busy (pre-adoption shipped `disabled={busy}`), and Esc does not close while busy (TFL-610's self-flagged assumption a; TFL-611 asks to confirm it).

Actual: `src/renderer/components/EncryptDialog.tsx:110-121` passes `blockBackdropClose={busy}` but NOT `closeDisabled={busy}`; the shell header X (`src/renderer/components/DialogShell.tsx:215-227`) is therefore enabled during busy. `DialogShell`'s Esc effect (`DialogShell.tsx:136-146`) fires whenever `onClose` is set, so Esc closes the encrypt dialog while busy. Pre-adoption HEAD had `disabled={busy}` on the close button and no Esc handler of its own. Live harness read: `[TFL611 encrypt] closeDisabled:false` (the prop is never bound to busy, so the X stays enabled in every state).

Root cause: the TFL-610 brief's DO-NOT "Do not add `closeDisabled` - no E1 dialog disabled its header close X" is factually wrong for EncryptDialog (its close X did carry `disabled={busy}`). The developer followed the DO-NOT and disclosed the deviation in the TFL-610 report; the CTO must reconcile the brief DO-NOT with the preserve-busy-condition requirement.

Evidence: focused commands 1-3 green (tfl611_cmd1.log / tfl611_cmd2.log / tfl611_verify.log); live spec `e2e/tfl611_dialogshell_screens.spec.cjs` -> 1 passed (tfl611_screens.log); screenshot `screenshots/tfl611-encrypt-dialog.png`.

Fix owner: frontend-dev (pending CTO disposition). Direction: pass `closeDisabled={busy}` to DialogShell; if Esc must also be gated while busy, wrap `onClose` with a `busy` check, because the shell deliberately keeps Esc live regardless of `blockBackdropClose`/`closeDisabled`.

History:
- qa (TFL-611, 2026-10-03): FILED during focused verification of TFL-610 (chunk E1). All three prescribed commands PASS; chunk does not reach the E2 gate as-is until this is adjudicated.
- CTO (2026-10-03): duplicate DEF number (canonical DEF-524 is at the top, CLOSED via TFL-615 with the `closeDisabled={busy}` fix). The Esc aspect raised here is RULED intended, not a defect: Phase 92 Ruling 3 makes the shell own Esc-to-close for every adopter and states explicitly that `blockBackdropClose`/`closeDisabled` leave Esc unaffected; the pre-adoption EncryptDialog had no Esc handler of its own, so no shipped Esc gate was lost, and dismissing the progress modal does not abort or corrupt the in-flight encrypt. Any future dialog that must gate Esc while busy wraps its `onClose` at the call site (a per-dialog decision, not a shell change). No further action.
## DEF-525: Phase 97 - the per-machine installer overwrites Adobe Acrobat's default handler for the eight PDF-family extensions

- Status: CLOSED (verified by qa, TFL-657 - manifest + generated-NSIS proof; installed-registry leg INCONCLUSIVE pending operator release-gate install)
- Severity: HIGH - a silent, machine-wide change of the user's existing OS defaults for eight Acrobat-proprietary file types, to an app that explicitly only registers as a candidate and cannot render them.
- Found by: adversary (TFL-655), filed from ADV-192
- Phase: 97 (TFL-518 chunk A, delivered as TFL-652)

Steps to reproduce:
1. On a machine where Adobe Acrobat owns the eight types (HKLM default, no per-user UserChoice): `reg query "HKLM\Software\Classes\.xdp"` -> `Acrobat.XDPDoc`.
2. Install the Phase 97 x64 NSIS build.
3. Re-query `HKLM\Software\Classes\.xdp` (and the other seven) and double-click the type.

Expected: Jovrel is only a SELECTABLE candidate for the eight non-pdf types (the Phase 97 contract and `electron-builder.yml:36-43`: "This never sets the Windows default handler on its own - the user picks that in Settings"). Adobe's existing default is untouched.

Actual: electron-builder feeds every `win.fileAssociations` row to the NSIS `APP_ASSOCIATE` macro, which writes the extension's DEFAULT value - `WriteRegStr SHELL_CONTEXT "Software\Classes\.${EXT}" "" "${FILECLASS}"` (`node_modules/app-builder-lib/templates/nsis/include/FileAssociation.nsh:65-74`) - in addition to `OpenWithProgids`. With no `HKCU\...\FileExts\.<ext>\UserChoice` for any of the eight, the HKLM default is the effective handler, so a Phase 97 install makes Jovrel the machine default for `.aaui/.bpdx/.fdf/.pdx/.rmf/.sequ/.xdp/.xfdf`; double-clicking them then launches Jovrel, which says it cannot display them. The shim also never sets `.pdf`, so this is the eight new rows (`.pdf` keeps its shipped behaviour per criterion 5).

Root cause: `fileAssociations` is a "claim the default" mechanism in electron-builder's NSIS target, not a candidate-only registration; the contract only ever promised a candidate.

Evidence: `ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md` ADV-192 (registry probe `test-fixtures/phase97-adversary/reg_probe.ps1`, attachment 3ce6305b; `registry-evidence.txt`, attachment 934929b8); `FileAssociation.nsh:65-74`; `NsisTarget.js:630-659`.

Fix owner: backend-dev. Direction: stop using `win.fileAssociations` for the eight non-pdf extensions; register Jovrel as a NON-default candidate via the Windows capabilities model - keep/again write the `Jovrel.<ext>` ProgID (DefaultIcon + `shell\open\command`) but write ONLY `Software\Classes\.<ext>\OpenWithProgids` value `Jovrel.<ext>`, add `HKLM\Software\RegisteredApplications` -> `Software\Jovrel\Capabilities`, and populate `Capabilities` `FileAssociations` (`.ext` -> `Jovrel.<ext>`, with ApplicationName/Description/Icon) so Jovrel appears in Settings > Default apps and the Open-with list without touching any existing default. `.pdf` stays exactly as shipped. Update the config/manifest unit test to assert the new candidate registration and that no `Software\Classes\.<ext>` DEFAULT is written.

History:
- adversary (TFL-655, 2026-10-04): FILED from ADV-192 during the Phase 97 diff-pass. Confirmed against electron-builder source and the live registry.
- CTO (2026-10-04): triaged ACCEPTED. Chunk A's packaging approach is wrong for a "candidate" phase; a fix chunk is dispatched to backend-dev before the phase can close.

## DEF-526: Phase 97 - the acrobat: protocol registration hijacks Adobe's per-machine handler and uninstall deletes third-party registration unconditionally

- Status: CLOSED (verified by qa, TFL-657 - manifest + generated-NSIS proof; installed-registry leg INCONCLUSIVE pending operator release-gate install)
- Severity: HIGH - hijacks a third-party URL-protocol handler machine-wide on install, and destroys it on uninstall, with no identity guard.
- Found by: adversary (TFL-655), filed from ADV-193
- Phase: 97 (TFL-518 chunk A, delivered as TFL-652)

Steps to reproduce:
1. On a machine with Adobe Acrobat DC: `reg query "HKLM\Software\Classes\acrobat" /s` -> default `URL:Acrobat Protocol`, `DefaultIcon` = Acrobat.exe, `shell\open\command` = `"...Acrobat.exe" /u "%1"`, plus `shell\open\ddeexec`.
2. Install the Phase 97 build, re-query the class root (Jovrel's values), then uninstall, re-query.

Expected: Jovrel registers as a candidate without disturbing a pre-existing third-party `acrobat:` registration; uninstall removes only what Jovrel created, using an identity guard (the same discipline as the legacy-cleanup steps at `electron-builder.nsh:108-192`).

Actual: `customInstall` (`electron-builder.nsh:256-259`) unconditionally overwrites the existing HKLM class root default, `DefaultIcon` and `shell\open\command` with Jovrel's exe, so Jovrel becomes the per-machine `acrobat:` handler for all users (a URL protocol has no OpenWithProgids candidate slot). `customUnInstall` (`electron-builder.nsh:270-272`) then runs `DeleteRegKey SHELL_CONTEXT "Software\Classes\acrobat"`, unconditionally deleting Adobe's `DefaultIcon` and `shell\open\ddeexec` subkeys, which Jovrel never created and does not restore. After a Jovrel install+uninstall cycle, Adobe's `acrobat:` protocol is gone.

Root cause: the acrobat: handling writes the class root (the handler) instead of a candidate location, and the uninstall delete has no identity guard.

Evidence: `ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md` ADV-193 (registry probe `test/fixtures/phase97-adversary/reg_probe.ps1`, attachment 3ce6305b; `electron-builder.nsh:249-272`).

Fix owner: backend-dev. Direction: do NOT write `Software\Classes\acrobat` default/DefaultIcon/shell\open\command. Register the protocol as a candidate: ProgID `Jovrel.acrobat` (DefaultIcon + `shell\open\command`), `Software\Classes\acrobat\OpenWithProgids` value `Jovrel.acrobat`, and `Capabilities\URLAssociations` `acrobat` -> `Jovrel.acrobat`. Uninstall deletes only Jovrel's own values/keys (Capabilities, the RegisteredApplications value, `Jovrel.*` ProgIDs and OpenWithProgids values) and never `Software\Classes\acrobat`. If a non-hijacking candidate registration is not achievable for a URL protocol, stop and report rather than hijacking.

History:
- adversary (TFL-655, 2026-10-04): FILED from ADV-193 during the Phase 97 diff-pass.
- CTO (2026-10-04): triaged ACCEPTED. Fix dispatched with DEF-525.
